  14. Copy and paste the video link into the Live streaming page URL on Zoom.
  15. (Optional) On Zoom’s livestream configuration page, under Resolution, select Full HD (1080P) when streaming a meeting/webinar if the setting’s value is 1080p.
  16. Click Save on the Zoom page.** **
  17. When you are ready to begin the event, start your Zoom meeting or webinar as the host.
  18. Click More in the meeting controls.
  19. Click Live on Custom Live Streaming Service.** **
  20. Once Zoom has started the livestream, return to the YouTube stream event and click Go Live.
Live stream in a meeting or webinar from your mobile device
  1. Start the webinar or meeting as the host.
  2. Tap More in the meeting/webinar controls.
  3. Tap YouTube. This will launch your browser and ask you to log in to YouTube.
  4. Select the YouTube channel you wish to stream to (if you have multiple channels).
  5. After you authenticate successfully, you will be allowed to specify the following settings on the Broadcasting to YouTube Live page:
  • Zoom Meeting title on YouTube: Automatically populated with the Zoom Webinars topic. Access the text box to change it.
  • Privacy: You can choose Public, Unlisted, or Private.
  • (Optional) Under Resolution, select Full HD (1080P) when streaming a meeting/webinar if the setting&rsquo s value is 1080p.
  1. Click the Go Live! button. You will now see a progress bar, letting you know that your session is being prepared for streaming. The live stream will then begin and be shown.
  2. Return to the Zoom app to continue the meeting or webinar.
  3. Streaming stops when you end the webinar or meeting, or click the LIVE notification in the top-left corner of the meeting/webinar window, tap Stop Live Stream, then confirm by tapping Stop Live Stream again.

To start a meeting as the host from a SIP/H.323 device, you will need to include the host key in the dial string. You can find your host key at zoom.us/profile. Learn more about host key.

H.323

Call out from the device using one of the following dial strings:** **

Meetings without a passcode:

[IP Address]##[Meeting ID]###[Host Key] Example: 192.168.1.25##123456789###123456

Meetings with a passcode:

[IP Address]##[Meeting ID]#[Passcode]#[Layout]#[Host Key] Example: 192.168.1.25##123456789#12345#11#123456

SIP

Call out from the device using one of the following dial strings:

Meetings without a passcode:

[Meeting ID]…[Host Key]@[IP Address] Example: 123456789…123456@192.168.1.25

Meetings with a passcode:

[Meeting ID].[Passcode]..[Host Key]@[IP Address] Example: 123456789.12345..123456@192.168.1.25

Note: There are additional options for dial strings, including the ability to join with a specific video layout. Learn more about SIP/H.323 dial strings.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.

  2. In the navigation menu, click Meetings.

  3. On the Upcoming tab, locate the Zoom meeting you want to start.

  4. Hover over the name of the meeting, then click Start. The Zoom Workplace app should launch automatically to start the meeting.

  5. Confirm that you are signed in at zoom.us/profile in the same browser.

  6. Start the meeting by clicking on the URL Link in your e-mail or calendar invitation. The Zoom Workplace app should launch automatically and start the meeting.

How to use waiting room during a meeting

Admit participants from the waiting room

Enable or disable waiting room

  2. Toggle on or Toggle off Enable waiting room feature. When enabled, participants joining the meeting will be placed in the waiting room. When disabled, participants will join the meeting without being placed in the waiting room.

Rename participants in the waiting room

Note: This feature requires the Rename participants in the Waiting Room subsetting to be enabled.

  1. As the host or co-host, click Participants .

Send participants to the waiting room
  1. As the host, click Participants .
  2. Click More next to the participant’s name and choose Put in Waiting Room.
Send messages to participants in the waiting room

Note: This feature is not available on Linux.

  1. As the host, click Chat .

  3. Click Waiting room participants.
  4. Enter and send your chat message to the waiting room. Once the message has been sent, the participants in the waiting room will see the message on the waiting room screen.

Hosting a Personal Audio Conference meeting

Category: Product features > Host features > Personal Audio Conference (PAC)

How to schedule a Personal Audio Conference

You can schedule a PAC if you want it to appear on your upcoming meetings in the Zoom desktop client, mobile app, and web portal.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Meetings.
  3. Click the ellipses icon in the top-right corner, then click Schedule a personal audio conference.
  4. Enter the required information, then click Schedule. Note: You can also configure your PAC settings like dial-in numbers and passcodes.

Alternatively, you can start a PAC without scheduling and copy the invite to participants.

How to copy the invitation for participants

You can copy the auto-generated invitation for conference participants and send it to them by email, add it to a calendar invite, or share elsewhere. If you have set a listen-only password, you will also have the option to copy the invitation for listen-only participants.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Personal Audio Conference.
  3. Click Copy Invitation For Participants. If you added a listen-only passcode, you can also click Copy Invitation For Listen-Only Attendees.
  4. Click Select All.
  5. Right-click to copy, or press Ctrl+C (Windows or Linux) / Cmd+C (macOS).
  6. Paste the invitation where you want to share it.

Note: If the option to only allow authenticated users to join meetings is disabled, external users or users not signed in can click the invite link to join the conference by dialing in or using call me.

How to start the PAC as a host

You can either start a PAC meeting from a phone or the Zoom web portal. The PAC meeting will not start until the host has joined and entered the Host Key.

  • Telephone
  • Web
  1. Dial in to one of the Zoom Global dial-in numbers enabled for your account.
  2. Enter the PAC meeting ID when prompted, followed by #.
  3. Enter the Host Key when prompted, followed by #.
Host controls through DTMF tones

If you have entered the host key to start the meeting, you will have host controls available to you by entering DTMF tones on your dial pad. The following commands are available:

DTMF command: **

When the host presses **, only the host will hear the audio prompt. They will reach the feature menu which will give the following response:

  • *4 to end the meeting
  • *5 to lock or unlock the meeting
  • *6 to mute or unmute yourself
  • *7 to start or stop the meeting recording
  • 99 to mute or unmute all participants

When the participant presses **, only the participant will hear the audio prompt. They will reach the feature menu which will give the following response

  • *6 to mute or unmute yourself

DTMF command: *7

When the host selects *7, the host will hear the following

  • The recording capability has not been enabled
  • The recording failed to start, please contact our support
  • The recording failed to stop, please contact our support
  • The meeting is now being recorded
  • The recording is now being stopped

If the host selects *7, all participants will hear the following

  • The meeting is now being recorded
  • The recording is now being stopped

DTMF command: *5

When the host selects *5, the host will hear the following

  • The meeting is now being locked
  • The meeting is now being unlocked

DTMF command: *#

When the host selects *#, they will notified there are x number of participants in the meeting

DTMF command: 99

When the host selects 99, they will be notified that all participants are muted/unmuted.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Personal Audio Conference.
  3. Click Start Conference. This will open the PAC controls in your browser. You will have options to dial in to the meeting, or if you have call out enabled, there will be a Call Me option.
  4. Join the conference by phone or use the call me option:
  • Under Join by phone, follow the instructions to join by phone:
  • Dial one of the numbers listed.
  • Enter the conference ID when prompted, followed by #.
  • Enter your host key, followed by #.
  • Under Call Me, select the country/region code of your phone number, then enter the phone number you want Zoom to dial. Answer the call to join the conference.
  1. In your browser, you will have host controls available at the bottom of your screen:
  • Mute/Unmute: Mute or unmute your phone. You can also dial *6 to mute/unmute during the conference. This is only DTMF command available when joining from the web portal.
  • Invite: Invite other participants to join.
  • Mute All: Mute all users dialed in.
  • Record: If enabled, record the meeting to the Zoom cloud.
  • Lock: Lock new participants from dialing into the meeting.

Starting a cloud recording

Category: Product features > Host features > Recordings

How to start a cloud recording

Only hosts and co-hosts can start a cloud recording. If you want a participant to start a recording, you can make them a co-host or use computer recording. Recordings started by co-hosts will only appear in the host’s list of recordings in the Zoom web portal.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Zoom Web App

To record a meeting to the cloud manually (you can also start your cloud recording automatically):

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Start your instant or scheduled meeting as the host.
  3. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the More icon .
  4. Click the Record icon .
  5. Click Record to the cloud to begin recording. A recording indicator will appear in the top-right corner of the meeting window.** Note: If you are muted, a Recording alert** pop-up window will appear indicating that You are muted.
  6. To pause the recording, in the meeting controls toolbar, click the Record icon , then click Pause recording.
  7. To stop recording, do one of the following:
  • In the meeting controls toolbar, click Record , then click Stop recording.
  • In the meeting controls toolbar, click End , then click End meeting for all or Leave meeting. This option will stop the cloud recording by either ending the meeting for everyone or removing yourself from the meeting.

Note: It’s not possible to Record to computer files from an iOS or Android device.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Start or join a meeting as the host or co-host.
  3. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap the More icon .
  4. Tap the Record icon .
  5. Tap Start recording. In the top-left corner, the app will show that it’s recording.
  6. (Optional) To pause or stop the recording, in the top-left corner, tap the recording indicator.
  • Next to Recording, tap the pause icon to pause the recording.
  • Next to Recording, tap the stop icon to stop the recording, then tap Stop to confirm.

After the meeting ends, the recording will process and appear under Recording & Transcripts on the Zoom web portal.

  1. Open your browser.
  2. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  3. Start or join a meeting as the host or co-host.
  4. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the More icon .
  5. Click the Record icon .
  6. Click Record to the cloud to begin recording.
  7. To pause the recording, in the meeting controls toolbar, click the Record icon , then click Pause recording.
  8. To stop recording, do one of the following:
  • In the meeting controls toolbar, click Record , then click Stop recording.
  • In the meeting controls toolbar, click End , then click End meeting for all or Leave meeting. This option will stop the cloud recording by either ending the meeting for everyone or removing yourself from the meeting.

How to manage your cloud recordings after the meeting

Once the meeting has ended, the recording must be processed before viewing. If enabled in email notification settings, Zoom will send an email to the host’s email address when the process is completed. The email includes share options.

Your recordings are accessible from Zoom Hub on the Zoom desktop app and the Recordings & Transcripts page in the Zoom web portal. If you can’t find or share a cloud recording, learn how to troubleshoot these issues.

Learn more about how to manage your cloud recordings:

  • Download, share, or delete cloud recordings
  • Trim the playback range of a shared recording

Cloud recording processing times

Once you stop the recording, you don’t need to remain in the meeting for the recording to process. Cloud recordings generally take about 2 times the duration recorded to process, but occasionally may take up to 24 hours due to higher processing loads. For example, an hour-long meeting with only 30 minutes recorded would typically take 30-60 minutes to process.

Note: If your recording is still being processed after 48 hours, learn how to troubleshoot this issue.

Sharing screen and broadcasting to breakout rooms

Category: Product features > Host features > Screen Sharing

How to share your screen to all meeting breakout rooms

Once breakout rooms are open for participants, the host or co-host can share their screen from the main session directly into all open breakout rooms. This allows the presenter to share visual information to all breakout rooms at once, guiding them on the next steps or tasks.

  1. Click Share Screen in the meeting controls.
  2. Enable the Share to breakout rooms option along the bottom of the share window.
  3. Choose what you would like to share, including an entire screen, a specific open program, or others.
  4. (Optional) Click the Share Sound option as well to include audio with the shared content.
  5. Click Share. The selected content will be shared to all breakout rooms. Any active shares in any breakout rooms will be interrupted for the host’s/co-host’s shared screen. Annotation or whiteboarding is saved before the host’s shared content is viewed.

You can also use the Video option, found under Advanced sharing tab, to share playback of a locally stored file, which will also share the audio.

How to broadcast to all breakout rooms

After breakout rooms are open for participants, the host can broadcast a message or mic audio to all breakout rooms.

Broadcast a message to all breakout rooms

The host can broadcast a message to all breakout rooms, to share information with all participants.

Note: This must be enabled in your breakout room settings.

  1. In the meeting controls, click Breakout Rooms .
  2. Click Broadcast, and select Broadcast Message.
  3. Enter your message and click the send icon . The message will appear for all participants in breakout rooms, and disappear after ~10 seconds.
Broadcast mic audio to all breakout rooms

The host can broadcast their voice to all breakout rooms, to share verbal information with all participants.

Note: This must be enabled in your breakout room settings.

  1. In the meeting controls, click Breakout Rooms .
  2. Click Broadcast, and select Broadcast Voice.
  3. Click the broadcast voice icon to begin broadcasting. Your mic audio will be broadcast to all breakout rooms.
  4. Click the stop icon to stop your broadcast. Note: You press and hold the B key on your keyboard your voice as needed.

Using file sharing integrations

Category: Product features > Participant features

How to enable file sharing integrations

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin with the privilege to edit integration settings.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Advanced then Integration.
  3. Enable one or more of these toggles:
  • Box
  • Google Drive
  • Microsoft OneDrive
  • Microsoft SharePoint

How to share a file in Zoom chat

You can share a file in Zoom chat to individual contacts, multi-users chat groups, and channels. Shared files are not directly uploaded to Zoom, but rather this will create and post a shareable link for the file. Contacts in the chat can click the file to open a browser and view the file using the 3rd-party file sharing service.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab.
  3. Select the contact, group-chat, or channel you want to share the file with.
  4. Click File and then click the file sharing service. A webpage will open for this service.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Follow the on-screen instructions to authorize Zoom to access your account. You will see a web page with your files.
  7. Select the file you want to share. Note: If you’re sharing a SharePoint file, you need to select the SharePoint site before viewing the file directory.
  8. In the bottom panel, select one of the following sharing options:
  • Anyone in your organization: Only members in your organization can click the link to view or download the file. Notes:
  • If you’re sharing a Google Drive file, enter your organization’s domain.
  • If you’re sharing a OneDrive or SharePoint file, this option is only available for work or school accounts.
  • Anyone with the link: Anyone with the link can view or download the file.
  1. Click Choose. The file’s permissions will change so that others can access it.
  2. When prompted by your browser, click the option to open Zoom. Zoom will post a link to the shared file. Contacts in the chat can click the link to open a browser and view the file in the 3rd-party file sharing service.

Note: By sharing the file, you are changing the file permissions in the 3rd-party file sharing service, so that the file is accessible for the entire organization. If you no longer want to share a file and need to revert permissions, sign in to your 3rd-party file sharing account.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  • If you’re sharing a Google Drive file, enter your organization’s domain.
  • If you’re sharing a OneDrive and SharePoint file, this option is only available for work or school accounts.
  • Anyone with the link: Anyone with the link can view or download the file.
  1. Tap Choose. The file’s permissions will change so that others can access it.
  2. When prompted by your browser, tap the option to open Zoom. Zoom will post a link to the shared file. Contacts in the chat can click or tap the link to open a browser and view the file in the 3rd-party file sharing service.

Note: By sharing the file, you are changing the file permissions in the 3rd-party file sharing service, so that the file is accessible for the entire organization. If you no longer want to share a file and need to revert permissions, sign in to your 3rd-party file sharing account.

Automatically joining meetings with computer audio

Category: Product features > Participant features > Audio

How to enable automatically connect to computer audio

To enable Automatically connect to computer audio:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.
  3. Click Meetings & webinars.
  4. Under Join experience, then When joining meetings and webinars, toggle on Automatically connect to computer audio. When you join a meeting, your computer audio will automatically set as the audio for the meeting, as opposed to joining by phone or another method.

Note: If you don’t see this setting, it may be disabled by an admin. Learn more about audio types for joining Zoom meetings.

Joining a Zoom meeting

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in meetings

How to join a Zoom meeting

Join by clicking the meeting link

If you were invited to a Zoom meeting by the host, you may have a meeting invite in your email or calendar.

  1. In the meeting invite, click the join link below Join Zoom Meeting. You will be prompted to launch the meeting on the Zoom Workplace app or click Join from your browser to join on the web if you don’t want to download the app.
  2. Check your audio and video settings, then click Join. You will either join the meeting automatically or be placed in the waiting room until the host admits you.
Join on the Zoom Workplace desktop or mobile app

For the best meeting experience, sign in to your Zoom account and join a meeting from the Zoom Workplace desktop or mobile app. You can download the latest version of the app from the Download Center. Otherwise, you will be prompted to download and install Zoom when you click a join link.

If joining from the Zoom desktop or mobile app, the app on your device must meet the following version requirements:

  • Zoom Workplace desktop app for Windows, macOS, or Linux: Global minimum version or higher

  • Zoom Workplace mobile app for Android or iOS: Global minimum version or higher

  • Windows | macOS | Linux

  • Android | iOS

Home tab
  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. Click the Home tab . Meetings that you have scheduled or have been invited to will be listed in chronological order for today. Note: If you do not see the Home tab, click the More tab , then click Home.
  3. (Optional) Click the ellipses icon to filter and search for meetings.
  4. Click the meeting you want to join.
  5. On the meeting card, click Join if you’re a meeting participant or click Start if you’re the host.
Meetings or Calendar tab
  1. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app.
  2. Click the Meetings tab or Calendar tab . Notes:
  • If you have set up the calendar and contacts integration to connect your calendar, you will have the Calendar tab. If you haven’t connected your calendar, you will have the Meetings tab.
  • If you do not see either the Meetings or Calendar tab, click the More tab , then click Meetings or Calendar.

  1. Click the Zoom meeting you want to join.

  2. On the meeting card, click Join if you’re a meeting participant or click Start if you’re the host.

  3. Sign in to the Zoom Workplace mobile app.

  4. At the bottom of the app, tap the Meetings tab or Calendar tab . Meetings that you have scheduled or have been invited to will be listed in chronological order for today. Notes:

  • If you have set up the calendar and contacts integration to connect your calendar, you will have the Calendar tab. If you haven’t connected your calendar, you will have the Meetings tab.
  • If you do not see either the Meetings or Calendar tab, tap the More tab , then tap Meetings or Calendar.
  1. Tap the Zoom meeting you want to join.
  2. Tap Join if you’re a meeting participant or tap Start if you’re the host.
Join from a web browser

In a web browser, you can join a Zoom meeting through the Zoom Web App by entering the meeting ID and choosing to open the Zoom Workplace desktop or mobile app, or join a meeting directly from a web browser without downloading any plugins or software.

  • Zoom Web App
  • Join from browser link
  • Launch the Zoom Workplace desktop or mobile app

The Zoom Web App allows you to join a meeting from a web browser without downloading any plugins or software. The Zoom Web App has limited features. Learn more about using the Zoom web app.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. Click the Meetings tab .
  3. Click the meeting you want to join.
  4. Click Join if you’re a meeting participant or click Start if you’re the host.

The meeting host must enable** Show a “Join from your browser” link** for their participants.

  1. Locate the meeting invite link from your email or calendar invitation.

  2. Click the join link to join the meeting. On your web browser, a pop-up window will prompt you to open or download the application.

  3. In the pop-up window, click Cancel.

  4. At the bottom of the page, click join from your browser. You will be directed to a new page.

  5. Click Allow to allow Zoom permission for your microphone and camera.

  6. Sign in with your name to join the meeting.

  7. (Optional) Select the Remember my name for future meetings check box.

  8. Click Join.

  9. Open your web browser.

  10. Go to join.zoom.us.

  11. Enter your meeting ID provided by the host/organizer.

  12. Click Join. Notes:

  • If this is your first time joining from Google Chrome, you will be asked to open the Zoom Workplace desktop app to join the meeting.
  • (Optional) Select the Always open these types of links in the associated app check box to skip this step in the future.
  • In the pop-up window, click Open Zoom Meetings (PC) or Open zoom.us (Mac).
  • If this is your first time joining from Firefox, you may be asked to open Zoom Workplace or the Zoom installer package.
  • To skip this step in the future, select the Remember my choice for zoommtg links check box.
  • Click Open Link.
Join through other methods

You can also join a Zoom meeting through Zoom Chat, Auto-call, dialing in from a phone, SIP/H.323 device, or a Zoom Room.

  • Zoom Chat
  • Auto-call
  • Telephone
  • SIP/H.323
  • Zoom Room

If you are online and signed in to the Zoom Workplace desktop app or mobile app, contacts can invite you to their live meeting directly. You will receive an incoming message notification, displaying who is inviting you to the meeting, along with a ringtone. Click Join to join the meeting.

If auto-call is enabled and you have opted in to auto-call, you automatically receive a call at the start of your scheduled meeting, displaying who is inviting you to the meeting, along with a ringtone. Click Join to join the meeting.

You can join some meetings by calling a phone number.

  1. If available, dial the phone number provided in the meeting invitation.
  2. After connecting, enter the meeting ID and passcode.

Note: If you have already joined the meeting by computer, you will have the option to enter your 6-digit participant ID to be associated with your computer. If you have not joined on your computer, press # again when prompted to enter in your participant ID.

Learn more about joining a meeting by phone.

  1. Dial the IP address provided to you in the meeting invitation (requires Room Connector port add-on).
  2. Enter the meeting ID by touch (DTMF) tones followed by #. You can also use dial strings, such as 192.168.10.55##000111000 to dial directly into the meeting.

If you’re using a Zoom Room, learn how to start or join a meeting.

Joining a Zoom meeting or webinar by phone

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in meetings

Zoom dial-in numbers

Zoom has toll numbers available for many countries that are included with all plans. For audio plan subscribers, Zoom also has toll-free and additional toll numbers available. The dial-in numbers available are dependent on the host’s audio subscription and settings.

If the meeting invite does not provide a local number for your country, there is a more extensive list of Zoom international dial-in numbers. If a number is not listed, this means that it is not available on the account that you’re currently signed in with.

If you have a Zoom Phone license, you can dial in to a meeting or webinar using Zoom Phone without incurring usage charges.

How to locate your participant ID

A participant ID is a unique identifier assigned to a participant when they join a meeting, especially if they join by phone or as a panelist in a webinar.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. Start or join a Zoom meeting.

  3. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the Join Audio icon .

  4. Click the Phone call tab, and you will find the Participant ID.

  5. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  6. Start or join a Zoom meeting.

  7. In the meeting controls toolbar, tap the Join Audio icon .

  8. Tap Dial In, and you will find the Participant ID.

  9. Sign in to the Zoom web app.

  10. Start or join a Zoom meeting.

  11. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the Join Audio icon .

  12. Click the Phone call tab , and you will find the Participant ID.

Panelists on a webinar will receive an email from Zoom containing their participant ID.

How to join a Zoom meeting or webinar by phone

Follow the sections below if you want to join a Zoom meeting or webinar on a desktop, mobile, or web app for video and screen sharing, but want to join the meeting audio using your phone.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android
  • iOS
  • Web app

You can join a meeting using the Zoom Workplace app for video and screen sharing, but join the meeting audio using your phone.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Join a Zoom meeting or webinar. You will be prompted to join the audio automatically.
  3. (Optional) If the join audio prompt does not appear, or you closed out of it, click Join Audio in the meeting controls.
  4. (Optional) If you’re automatically joined with computer audio, click the up arrow next to Audio, then click Switch to phone audio.
  5. Click the Phone Call tab. Note: If you are subscribed to the Audio Plan add-on, you can also use the Call me option.
  6. Follow the instructions for dialing in:
    • In the Country/region drop-down menu, select the country or region you’re calling from.
  • Call one of the numbers provided.
  • Enter your meeting ID followed by #.
  • Enter your participant ID followed by #.
  • Enter the passcode, if prompted, followed by #.
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Join a Zoom meeting or webinar. You will be prompted to join the audio automatically.
  3. (Optional) If the prompt to join audio does not appear or you closed it, tap Join Audio in the meeting controls.
  4. Tap Dial In.
  5. (Optional) Tap the down arrow at the top to select the country you’re calling from, if not selected by default.
  6. Tap the phone icon next to the number you want to call.
  7. Tap Call. Note: If prompted, allow Zoom to make and manage phone calls.
  8. Return to your home screen and open the Zoom mobile app again.
  9. (Optional) When you leave the meeting, you will have the option to Leave Meeting or Leave with Telephone Connected, to stay dialed into the meeting after leaving from the Zoom app. Note: If you’re on an Android device that can’t make calls, follow the instructions for dialing in:
    • Dial one of the numbers provided.
  • Enter your meeting ID, followed by #.
  • Enter your participant ID, followed by #.
  • Enter the passcode, if prompted, followed by #.
  • Tap Back after dialing in.
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Join a Zoom meeting or webinar. You will be prompted to join the audio automatically.
  3. (Optional) If the prompt to join audio does not appear or you closed it, tap Join Audio in the meeting controls.
  4. Tap Dial In.
  5. (Optional) Tap the down arrow at the top to select the country you’re calling from, if not selected by default.
  6. Tap the phone icon next to the number you want to call.
  7. Tap Dial. Note: If prompted, allow Zoom to make and manage phone calls.
  8. Return to your home screen and open Zoom again.
  9. (Optional) When you leave the meeting, you will have the option to Leave Meeting or Leave with Telephone Connected, to stay dialed into the meeting after leaving from the Zoom app. Note: If you’re on an iOS device that can’t make calls, follow the instructions for dialing in:
    • Dial one of the numbers provided.
  • Enter your meeting ID, followed by #.
  • Enter your participant ID, followed by #.
  • Enter the passcode, if prompted, followed by #.

  3. (Optional) If the prompt to join audio does not appear or you closed it, click Join Audio in the meeting controls.

  6. Follow the instructions for dialing in:
  • Select the country you’re calling from in the drop-down menu.
  • Dial one of the numbers provided.
  • Enter your meeting ID, followed by #.

How to join a meeting or webinar by phone only

Join as a host

You can join and start any Zoom meeting from your telephone and control the meeting with DTMF tones.

  1. Dial an in-country number. If you dial a toll number, your carrier’s rates will apply. You can find the numbers on your meeting invitation or view the full list of international dial-in numbers.
  2. Enter the meeting ID followed by #.
  3. To be recognized as the host, enter your host key, which you can find on your user profile, followed by #. Note: If you enable join before host and join only from your telephone, you will not be recognized as the host and will not have host controls. If you need to host meetings from your phone with full host controls, do not enable join before host.
Phone controls for the meeting host

If you have entered the host key to start the meeting, you will have host controls available to you by entering DTMF tones on your dial pad. To hear all available commands, enter ** on your phone. Listed below are what you can enter on the dial pad with their corresponding functions:

  • *4 - End the meeting for all participants
  • *5 - Lock or unlock the meeting
  • *6 - Mute or unmute yourself
  • *7 - Start or stop recording Note: All participants in the meeting will be notified when the recording is stopped or started.
  • *# - Hear the number of participants in the meeting
  • 99 - Mute or unmute all participants
Considerations for joining by phone as the host

  • If you have scheduled the meeting from a basic account, the meeting will time out after 40 minutes with a 30-minute warning notification, based on the time limits for Zoom meetings.

  • If you would like the meeting to last for up to 30 hours, the meeting will need to be scheduled by a Licensed user on a Pro or above account.

  • The number of phones that can connect to a Zoom meeting or webinar is determined by account type and the add-on assigned to the user account.

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License: 100 Dial-In Users

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License + Large Meeting 500: 500 Dial-In Users

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License + Large Meeting 1000: 1000 Dial-In Users

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License + Large Meeting 3000: 3000 Dial-In Users

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License + Large Meeting 5000: 5000 Dial-In Users

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License + Webinar 500: 500 Dial In Users*

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License + Webinar 1000: 1000 Dial In Users*

  • Zoom Workplace Pro License + Webinar 3000 and above: 3000-7000 Dial In Users*

  • Zoom Workplace Business License: 300 Dial-In Users

  • Zoom Workplace Enterprise License: 1000 Dial-In Users

*Up to 500 panelists can also dial in to a webinar, but they count towards the total number of dial-in users. For example, for a Webinar 1000, a maximum of 500 panelists and 500 attendees can join the webinar by phone.

Join as a participant
  1. Dial an in-country number. If you dial a toll number, your carrier’s rates will apply. You can find the numbers on your meeting invitation or view the full list of international dial-in numbers.
  2. When prompted, enter the meeting ID—the nine (9), ten (10), or eleven (11) digit ID—provided to you by the host, followed by #.
  3. If you have joined on a computer or mobile device or are a panelist in a webinar, enter your Participant ID followed by #. Press # to skip.
  4. Enter the passcode when prompted, followed by #. The host will include this passcode in the meeting invite.

If you join by computer or mobile device later, you can enter the Participant ID to bind your phone and device session together and show your video when you speak on the phone. To enter your participant ID once you are in the meeting, enter #, the Participant ID, followed by # on your phone.

Phone controls for participants

You can enter the following commands via DTMF tones using your phone’s dial pad while in a Zoom meeting:

  • *6 - Toggle mute/unmute
  • *9 - Raise/lower hand

Joining a Zoom meeting without an account

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in meetings

How to use Zoom without an account

There are many ways to join a meeting, but the easiest ways to join as a guest are to click the link provided to you by the host or enter the meeting ID and passcode directly into Zoom.

Note: Depending on the host’s settings, you can join the meeting from your desktop browser without downloading Zoom first. Joining meetings from a web browser gives you access to basic Zoom meeting features.

Use the link provided
  1. Click the meeting invite link you received from the host, for example in your email or calendar invitation. On your web browser, a pop-up window will prompt you to open or download the application.
  2. In the pop-up window, click Cancel.
  3. At the bottom of the page, click the Join From your Browser link. Note: If you don’t see the link to join from the browser, the host may not have it enabled and you will have to join a Zoom meeting by opening the Zoom client or downloading it first.
  4. In the pop-up window at the top-left corner of the screen, click Allow to allow Zoom permission for your microphone and camera.
  5. In the Your Name field, enter a display name.
  6. (Optional) Select the Remember my name for future meetings check box.
  7. Click Join. You will join the meeting as a guest.
Enter the meeting ID and passcode in Zoom
  1. In your web browser, go to zoom.us/join.
  2. Enter the meeting ID provided by the host/organizer.
  3. Click Join. A pop-up window will prompt you to open or download the application.
  4. Do one of the following:
  • Launch the meeting on the Zoom client if it’s already downloaded on your device.
  • Click Cancel in the pop-up window, then click Download Now to download Zoom before joining.
  • Click Cancel in the pop-up window, then click the Join from Your Browser link if you do not want to download Zoom before joining the meeting. Note: You are not required to download Zoom on a desktop device before joining, but you will have access to limited functionality if you join from your browser. If you want to join a meeting from an Android or iOS device, you must download the Zoom mobile app.
  1. If prompted, allow Zoom to use your microphone and camera.
  2. Enter a display name, then click Join.
  3. (Optional) Select the Remember my name for future meetings check box.
  4. If prompted, enter a meeting passcode, then click Join again. You will join the meeting as a guest.

Learn more about ways to join virtual meetings on Zoom.

Joining meeting audio by phone (call me)

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in meetings

How to join meeting or webinar audio by phone

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

You can dial your own phone device to access any meeting from your phone device.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. Start or join a meeting.

  3. Click Join Audio if you haven’t joined the meeting by audio. If you’ve already joined the meeting using computer audio, click Switch to Phone Audio.** **

  4. Click the Call Me tab.

  5. Click the drop-down menu to select the country code of your phone number.

  6. Enter your phone number, then click Call. Note: If you are dialing a phone number that includes an extension, type a hyphen “-” after the phone number and enter the extension. For example, 6032331333-156 dials the extension 156.

  7. Sign in to Zoom mobile app.

  8. Start or join a meeting.

  9. Tap Join Audio if you haven’t joined the meeting by audio. If you’ve already joined the meeting using computer audio, click More then Disconnect Audio.** **

  10. Tab Join Audio then Dial in.

  11. Click the drop-down menu at the top to select the country or region to display dial-in numbers for.

  12. Tap the phone button next to a dial-in number.

Participant controls in a meeting

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in meetings

How to access participant controls

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app

After joining a meeting on the Zoom desktop app, participants can access features in the meeting controls toolbar at the bottom of the meeting window.

Note: The options listed here are based on the default order and the placement of your controls may vary depending on customization and usage. Some controls may not be available to you if the meeting host or an admin on your account has disabled a feature, if your Zoom plan is not supported, or if your device is not supported.

  • Join audio : If you haven’t joined the meeting audio yet, you will have the Join audio option in your meeting controls toolbar. Click Join audio to choose an audio option, such as Join with computer audio.
  • Audio / : Mute and unmute your microphone.
  • To access more audio controls, click the up arrow icon next to Audio. This is where you can change the microphone and speaker that Zoom is currently using on your computer, leave computer audio, and access all audio settings.
  • Tip: Use the following keyboard shortcuts to mute or unmute yourself. You can also use push to talk if you want to unmute yourself by holding the spacebar.
  • Windows: Alt + A
  • macOS: Command(⌘) + Shift + A
  • Video / : Turn your camera on or off.
  • To access more video controls, click the up arrow icon next to Video. This is where you can select a different camera, adjust your virtual background, and access all video settings.
  • Participants : Open the Participants panel to view who’s currently in the meeting and invite other participants. Hover over your display name and click More to access additional options:
  • Rename: Change your screen name that is displayed to other participants in the meeting.
  • Edit profile picture
  • Share/Unshare my pronouns:** **If you have entered your pronouns in your profile, you can choose to share or unshare your pronouns in the current meeting.
  • Chat : Open the Chat panel to chat with other meeting participants.
  • React : Send emoji floating effects, emoji reactions, raise hand, and other nonverbal feedback to communicate issues or feedback to the host and other meeting participants without disrupting the meeting. Reactions, raise hand, and other nonverbal feedback (yes, no, slow down, speed up, I’m away, and be right back) are shown on your video tile and next to your name in the Participants panel. Floating effects are shown over your video tile (only available when video is on).
  • Share : Start a screen share (if the host allows). You will be able to select the desktop or application you want to share.
  • AI Companion : Open the AI Companion panel to use AI Companion in the meeting. Click one of the preset options such as Catch me up, Was my name mentioned, or Are there any action items, or enter your own prompt.
  • Meeting info : View the meeting ID, passcode, invite link, host’s name, and your participant ID, as well as a description of the meeting.
  • Apps : Open the Zoom Apps panel to use Marketplace Apps directly in the meeting.
  • More :
  • Record :
  • Record to this computer: Depending on the host’s settings, you may be able to record to your computer.
  • Request to record to this computer: The host will need to give you permission to record. Clicking this option will send a request to the host to allow you to record to your computer.
  • Request host to record to the cloud: Clicking this option will send a request to the host to start cloud recording. Participants do not have access to start cloud recordings.
  • Transcript: Open the Transcript panel to view the meeting transcript.
  • Captions : Show automated or manual captions if available.
  • Docs : Open or create a Zoom Doc from within the meeting.
  • Notes : Open or create a Zoom Note from within the meeting.
  • Whiteboards : Open or create a Zoom Whiteboard from within the meeting.
  • Start billable hours: Start or stop tracking billable hours for the meeting.
  • Reset to default: Reset the toolbar options to the default placement.
  • Leave : Leave the meeting. Only the host can end the meeting for all participants.

After joining a meeting on the Zoom mobile app, participants can access features in the meeting controls toolbar at the bottom of the meeting window, except for Leave meeting which appears at the top-right corner.

Note: Some controls may not be available to you if the meeting host or an admin on your account has disabled a feature, if your Zoom plan is not supported, or if your device is not supported.

  • Join audio : If you haven’t joined the meeting audio yet, this option allows you to connect to the meeting’s audio. Once connected, you can mute or unmute your microphone.
  • Unmute / Mute : Mute and unmute your microphone.
  • Stop video / Start video : Turn your camera on or off. Note: If using the mobile app for Android or iOS, your video will automatically turn off if you switch away from Zoom to another app or your home screen.
  • Participants : Open the Participants panel to view who’s currently in the meeting and invite other participants. Tap your display name to access additional options to rename yourself or mute/unmute yourself.
  • Chat : Open the Chat panel to chat with other meeting participants.
  • Reactions : Send emoji floating effects, emoji reactions, raise hand, and other nonverbal feedback to communicate issues or feedback to the host and other meeting participants without disrupting the meeting. Reactions, raise hand, and other nonverbal feedback icons (yes, no, slow down, speed up, and I’m away) are shown on your video tile and next to your name in the Participants panel. Floating effects are shown over your video tile (only available when video is on).
  • Share : Start a screen share. You will be able to select what you want to share, such as your screen, photos, or a website URL.
  • AI Companion : Open the AI Companion panel to use AI Companion in the meeting. Click one of the preset options such as Catch me up, Was my name mentioned, or Are there any action items, or enter your own prompt.
  • Record : Request the host to start cloud recording.
  • Show CC : Show automated or manual captions if available.
  • Whiteboards : Open or create a Zoom Whiteboard from within the meeting.
  • Docs : Open or create a Zoom Doc from within the meeting.
  • Notes : Open or create a Zoom Note from within the meeting.
  • Apps : Open the Zoom Apps panel to use Marketplace Apps directly in the meeting.
  • More :
  • Audio settings: Access microphone modes, such as noise removal or original sound for musicians.
  • Captions & translations: Adjust caption language and open the Captions panel.
  • Meeting settings: Access some personal settings related to the meeting you are currently in.
  • Background & effects: Configure or adjust your virtual background, filters, or avatar.
  • Pair with a Zoom Room: Connect to a nearby Zoom Room and control the Zoom Room from your mobile device.
  • Disconnect audio: Disconnects you from the meeting audio. You must tap Join audio in the meeting controls again if you want to connect to the meeting’s audio.

After joining a meeting on the Zoom Web App, participants can access features in the meeting controls toolbar at the bottom of the meeting window.

Note: The options listed here are based on the default order and the placement of your controls may vary depending on customization and usage. Some controls may not be available to you if the meeting host or an admin on your account has disabled a feature or if your Zoom plan is not supported.

  • Join Audio : If you haven’t joined the meeting audio yet, you will have the Join audio option in your meeting controls toolbar. Click Join audio to choose an audio option, such as Join Audio by Computer.

  • Participants : Open the Participants panel to view who’s currently in the meeting and invite other participants. Hover over your display name and click More to access additional options:
  • Rename: Change your screen name that is displayed to other participants in the meeting.
  • Share/Unshare my pronouns:** **If you have entered your pronouns in your profile, you can choose to share or unshare your pronouns in the current meeting.
  • Chat : Open the Chat panel to chat with other meeting participants.
  • Reactions : Send emoji reactions, raise hand, and other nonverbal feedback to communicate issues or feedback to the host and other meeting participants without disrupting the meeting. Reactions, raise hand, and other nonverbal feedback icons (yes, no, slow down, speed up, and I’m away) are shown on your video tile and next to your name in the Participants panel.
  • Share Screen : Start a screen share (if the host allows). You will be able to select the tab or window you want to share.
  • AI Companion : Open the AI Companion panel to use AI Companion in the meeting. Click one of the preset options or enter your own prompt.
  • More :
  • Captions : Show automated or manual captions if available.
  • Request the host to record to the cloud : Clicking this option will send a request to the host to start cloud recording. Participants do not have access to start cloud recordings.
  • Whiteboards : Open or create a Zoom Whiteboard from within the meeting.

  • Start/Stop Incoming Video: Allows you to disable incoming participant videos. This can be used in order to preserve bandwidth and improve the quality of your meeting experience.

Participating in meeting breakout rooms

Category: Product features > Participant features > Joining and participating in meetings

How to join a meeting breakout room

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app
  • Telephone

  1. The host will need to invite you to join the breakout room.

  2. Click Join.

  3. If you choose Later, you can join by clicking Breakout Rooms in your meeting controls.

  4. Click Join Breakout Room. You will have access to full controls similar to the meeting.

  5. The host will need to invite you to join the breakout room.

  6. Tap Join.

  7. If you tap Later, you can join by tapping Join Breakout Room .

  8. Tap Join. You will have access to full controls similar to the meeting

  9. The host will need to invite you to join the breakout room.

  10. Click Join in the notification pop-up.

  11. If you choose Later, you can join by clicking Breakout Rooms in your meeting controls. You will have access to full controls similar to the meeting. Note: The web client does not support local recording.

When joining a breakout room by telephone, you do not need to do anything to join. Once the host starts the breakout rooms, you will be notified that you have been added to a breakout room. You will be able to mute and unmute like you can in the main session. Use *6 to mute or unmute.

How to self-select a breakout room

Note: Participants not joined with the desktop or mobile app will not be able to self-select a breakout room. The host will need to facilitate moving these participants manually.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS

If the host has allowed participants to self-select and join breakout rooms of their choosing, participants will be able to view and select from a list of breakout rooms the host has created. They will be able to enter and leave breakout rooms freely.

Note: Participants not joined with the desktop or mobile app will not be able to self-select a breakout room. The host will need to facilitate moving these participants manually.

  1. Click Breakout Rooms in your meeting controls. This will display the list of open breakout rooms created by the host.
  2. (Optional) Click Expand All to expand all available rooms and see which participants are in that particular room.
  3. Hover your pointer over the number to the right of breakout room you wish to join, click Join, then confirm by clicking Join.
  4. Repeat as necessary to join other breakout rooms, or click Leave Room to return to the main session.

If the host has allowed participants to self-select and join breakout rooms of their choosing, participants will be able to view and select from a list of breakout rooms the host has created. They will be able to enter and leave breakout rooms freely.

  1. Tap Breakout Rooms on the top-left side of the meeting controls. This will display the list of open breakout rooms created by the host.
  2. Tap the Breakout Room you wish to participant in and then tap Join.
  3. Repeat as necessary to join other breakout rooms, or click Leave Room to return to the main session.

How to ask for help in a meeting breakout room

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app

If you click Ask for Help, it will notify the meeting host that you need assistance and they will be asked to join your breakout room.

  1. Click Ask for Help in the meeting controls.
  2. Confirm that you would like assistance by clicking Invite Host.

If you tap Ask for Help , it will notify the meeting host that you need assistance and they will be asked to join your breakout room.

  1. Tap Ask for Help .
  2. Confirm that you would like assistance by tapping Invite Host.

If you click Ask for Help , it will notify the meeting host that you need assistance and they will be asked to join your breakout room.

  1. Click Ask for Help in the meeting controls.
  2. Confirm that you would like assistance by clicking Invite Host.

How to record while in a breakout room

  • Windows | macOS
  1. Ask the host for permission to record. The host needs to allow recording before opening the breakout rooms. If the host has already open the breakouts rooms, they can join your breakout room to allow you to record.
  2. Click Record in the meeting controls to start a computer recording.
  3. Click the pause or stop icon in the meeting controls to pause or stop the recording. You can also pause or stop the recording by clicking the indicator in the top-left corner.

Learn more about computer recording.

How to leave a breakout room

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web app
  • Telephone

You can leave the breakout room and return to the main meeting session at any time, or you can leave the meeting entirely from the breakout room.

  1. Click Leave Breakout Room.
  2. Choose if you want to leave the breakout room or the entire meeting.
  3. When the host ends the breakout rooms, you will be notified and given the option to return to the main room immediately, or in 60 seconds.

  1. Tap Leave.
  2. Choose Leave Breakout Room.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux

Provide non-verbal feedback and reactions during meetings (participants)

To provide non-verbal feedback or reactions to the host of the meeting:

  1. Join a Zoom meeting as a participant.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the React icon .
  3. Choose from the following icons or click to choose from a full set of emojis. Click the icon again to remove it.
  • Clapping Hands
  • Thumbs Up

Adjusting recording video layouts

Category: Product features > Participant features > Recordings

Computer recording video layouts

Note: Computer recordings are only available when recording with the Zoom desktop app.

Speaker view

The recording captures only the video of the active speaker, switching views as different participants speak. Learn more about the Speaker view or how to apply this video layout to your computer recording.

Note: The following changes are also captured in the recording:

  • Pinning participants
  • Spotlighting participants
  • Customer gallery order
Gallery view

The recording captures a grid layout displaying all participants’ videos simultaneously. Learn more about the Gallery view or how to apply this video layout to your computer recording.

Note:

  • Gallery view recording can display a maximum of 25 participants.
Dynamic gallery view

Dynamic gallery is an enhanced version of the gallery view. It automatically crops video tiles to focus on faces and best utilize available screen space. This view automatically crops all tiles (including your own) to show more participants. Other participants may still see your full background. To expand or shrink your self view, hover over your video tile, from the menu , click Expand self view or Shrink self view.

Dynamic gallery view supports up to 25 or 49 participants per screen. You can switch to the next page to view additional participants.

Note: Dynamic gallery view of up to 9 participants requires desktop app for Windows, macOS, or Linux version 6.7.5 or higher. Dynamic gallery of up to 25 or 49 participants requires version 7.0.0 or higher.

Multi-speaker view

The recording highlights and enlarges the current speakers’ video tiles, while still showing other participants in a smaller gallery view below. Learn more about the Multi-speaker view or how to apply this video layout to your computer recording.

Notes:

  • With 4 or fewer participants, gallery view is used.
  • With enough participants, up to 4 active speakers will have their video tiles enlarged and highlighted.
  • Pinning videos is supported, keeping the pinned video in focus.
  • Spotlighting is not supported as it takes control of the video layout for all participants.
Immersive view

The recording recreates a class or conference room by placing up to 25 participants on a single virtual background. Learn more about the Immersive view or how to apply this video layout to your computer recording.

Notes:

  • Only the immersive scene is captured, not the individual video tile.
  • Cloud recordings aren’t supported.
Shared screen or window

When a participant shares their screen, the computer recording will capture the shared content as it appears to the person recording. Once screen sharing ends, the recording will revert to the previous video layout.

Note: Your recording layout will change based on whether Record video during screen sharing or Place video next to the shared screen is enabled.

  • Shared content only: Captures only the shared screen or window, excluding participant videos.

  • The recording participant must:

  • Disable Record video during screen sharing.

  • Share with participants video on top of shared content: Shows the shared screen with participant video tiles over the shared content.

  • The recording participant must:

  • Enable Record video during screen sharing

  • Disable Place video next to the shared screen

  • Participant video tiles can be resized and relocated but will remain in the top-right corner of the recording.

  • This layout isn’t available in dual monitor mode. Instead, the share with participants video next to shared content is used.

  • Share with participants video next to shared content: Displays the shared screen with participant video tiles next to the shared content.

  • The recording participant must:

  • Enable Record video during screen sharing

  • Enable Place video next to the shared screen

  • Participant video tiles can be resized and moved but will stay in the top-right corner of the recording.

  • This layout isn’t available in dual monitor mode. Instead, the share with participants video on top of shared content is used.

Cloud recording layouts

Notes:

  • Cloud recordings are available with the Zoom desktop app, mobile app, web portal, and Zoom Rooms.

  • Cloud recordings can capture multiple layouts simultaneously, but this must be set in the Recording settings on the web portal before the meeting starts. Changes made after the meeting begins won’t apply.

  • ​​Changes to participants’ personal views don’t affect cloud recordings.

  • The host and co-hosts can start, pause, and stop cloud recordings. After the session ends, the recording will only appear in the host’s recordings list on the web portal.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux | Web client

  • Android | iOS

Speaker view

The recording captures only the video of the active speaker, switching views as different participants speak. Learn more about the Speaker view or how to apply this video layout to your cloud recording.

Note: Spotlighting participants and having all participants follow the host’s custom gallery order isn’t captured in the gallery view recording.

Gallery view

The recording captures a grid layout displaying all participants’ videos simultaneously. Learn more about the Gallery view or how to apply this video layout to your cloud recording.

Notes:

  • Spotlighting only one participant and having them follow the host’s custom gallery order is not captured in the gallery view recording.
  • Spotlighting 2–9 participants is captured in the gallery view recording.
Dynamic gallery view

Dynamic gallery is an enhanced version of the gallery view. It automatically crops video tiles to focus on faces and best utilize available screen space. This view automatically crops all tiles (including your own) to show more participants. Other participants may still see your full background. To expand or shrink your self view, hover over your video tile, from the menu , click Expand self view or Shrink self view.

Dynamic gallery view supports up to 25 or 49 participants per screen. You can switch to the next page to view additional participants.

Note: Dynamic gallery view of up to 9 participants requires desktop app for Windows, macOS, or Linux version 6.7.5 or higher. Dynamic gallery of up to 25 or 49 participants requires version 7.0.0 or higher.

Shared screen or window

When a participant shares their screen, the cloud recording captures the shared content as seen by all.

  • If participant video tiles are recorded, only the active speaker is shown during screen sharing.
  • Once screen sharing stops, the recording will revert to the selected video layout.

Note: Your recording layout will change based on whether you’ve enabled these cloud recording settings before the session starts:

  • Record active speaker with shared screen
  • Record gallery view with shared screen Note: Records the gallery view when no content is being shared. When content is shared, only the shared content and the active speaker view are recorded.
  • Record tiles when sharing

Shared content only: Captures only the shared screen or window, excluding participant videos.

  • Disable Record tiles when sharing

Before the session starts, the host must:

Note:

  • Cloud recordings only capture the active speaker during screen sharing.
  • To prevent the speaker’s tile from overlapping the shared content, set the resolution of the shared content to 1600x900.

Note: The mobile app layouts are similar to the desktop and web clients, but the narrower screen may add black bars to the sides of video or shared screens. This can also vary based on whether the device is in portrait or landscape mode.

Note: Spotlighting participants and having all participants follow the host’s custom gallery order isn’t captured in the gallery view recording.

Gallery view

Notes:

  • Spotlighting only one participant and having them follow the host’s custom gallery order is not captured in the gallery view recording.
  • Spotlighting 2–9 participants is captured in the gallery view recording.
Shared screen or window

When a participant shares their screen, the cloud recording captures the shared content as seen by all.

  • If participant video tiles are recorded, only the active speaker is shown during screen sharing.
  • Once screen sharing stops, the recording will revert to the selected video layout.

Note: Your recording layout will change based on whether you’ve enabled these cloud recording settings before the session starts:

  • Record active speaker with shared screen
  • Record gallery view with shared screen Note: Records the gallery view when no content is being shared. When content is shared, only the shared content and the active speaker view are recorded.
  • Record tiles when sharing

Shared content only: Captures only the shared screen or window, excluding participant videos.

Before the sessions starts, the host must:
  • Enable Record active speaker with shared screen
  • Enable Record gallery view with shared screen
  • Enable Record active speaker, gallery view and shared screen separately
  • Enable Shared Screen * Note: *This is a sub-setting under Record active speaker, gallery view and shared screen separately
  • Disable Record tiles when sharing

Shared content with active speaker: Captures the shared screen or window, with a tile of the active speaker’s video in the top-right corner next to the shared content.

Before the session starts, the host must:

  • Enable Record gallery view with shared screen
  • Enable Record active speaker, gallery view and shared screen separately
