Frequently asked questions about the Software Quarterly Lifecycle Policy

Why is Zoom utilizing a quarterly minimum version schedule?

Zoom’s software quarterly lifecycle policy is designed to help ensure Zoom users receive the latest features, as well as any security and privacy enhancements we make to the platform. We support our customers in making educated decisions about risks to their own environments, and Zoom Security Bulletins exist to aid them in making those determinations. As always, we encourage customers to apply Zoom updates as they’re released, and the Software Quarterly Lifecycle Policy sets a maximum limit for that delay.

We understand that it isn’t always possible for organizations to update all employees and need additional time for software reviews. With this in mind, we may update the minimum app version every 3 months and will provide a 90-day notice for the next minimum version requirements, which are detailed in the chart above.

Does this new release window include all Zoom products and services (Zoom Phone, CRC, etc.) or only the Zoom Workplace desktop and mobile apps?

This policy will affect the Zoom app for meetings (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, Blackberry, and Intune), Zoom Rooms (including Whiteboards and Zoom Room Controllers), Zoom Phone Appliances, VDI Client and Plugin, Meeting SDK, Video SDK, and more.

Which Zoom Room Devices will be required to be updated?

All devices running Zoom Rooms software will be required to be updated by each enforcement date.

Will users be able to use Zoom Chat, Zoom Phone, Zoom Meetings, Zoom Webinars, etc. when using an unsupported version after the enforcement date?

On the date of each new enforcement, users on an app below the minimum version will be signed out of their app. They must update to the minimum version or higher before they are able to sign in to their Zoom account again and regain full access Zoom features. Zoom Phone users will not be able to make or receive calls, including emergency 911 calls. Zoom Room devices will be placed in Maintenance Mode, with a notification that an admin must update the device.

What happens when customers are approaching the minimum version and do not update in time?

Customers will be prompted to update the Zoom desktop or mobile app to the current minimum version before they can sign in or join a meeting/webinar. If unable to immediately update, they will be provided the option to join a meeting through the web app instead. Users will only receive a notification if the Zoom app is below the minimum version.

If you have prompts disabled at the device level, the administrator will be responsible for applying updates. For other products, such as Zoom Rooms, the scheduling functionality will be disabled and a warning will be displayed.

What should users/admins expect to see if the installed version is below the minimum enforced version?

Refer to this support article for more details and screenshots of expected error messages.

How often will there be new releases?

Zoom releases bundled updates regularly to help mitigate backward compatibility issues for most products, and because of these regular release cadences, there will be multiple versions available between the minimum version and the latest version. To see historic release cycles, please refer to our release notes.

Are there any other enforcements we should be aware of?

Besides Zoom enforcing a minimum version for our various clients, there are other changes to system prerequisites to be aware of and prepared for. These app prerequisites are detailed on their respective support articles, such as the system prerequisites for Windows, macOS, and Linux, the Zoom Room system requirements, and others.

Zoom has established an End-of-Life Support Guideline for certified Zoom Rooms devices and Zoom Phone appliances regarding hardware end-of-sales and Zoom’s estimated support timeline. Learn more about the Zoom Rooms devices and Zoom Phone appliances End-of-Life Support Guideline.

How long can customers expect a given version release to be supported?

Zoom will make an effort to support a given version for at least 9 months before it falls below the minimum version.

How can customers see which versions their users are running?

As an admin or account owner, you can view which versions users on your account are running through the Dashboard or within the user management portal by filtering by client type. Individual users can check the version directly in the desktop and mobile app.

Do customers have the ability to choose which version they would like to be on?

No, Zoom only provides the latest version through the app and our website.

Am I secure if I’m not on the latest version of Zoom?

Zoom is committed to enhancing the security of its products and services and protecting customers from external threats. We recommend users use the latest Zoom software with all current security updates. Users can easily check for updates and upgrade by visiting our website. We always encourage customers to look at our release notes for any included security enhancements. Customers can also look at our Security Bulletins to learn more about fixed issues.

What happens if a major vulnerability is detected and fixed? Will Zoom deploy additional updates and/or make forced updates?

In the case of an urgent security or other matter, Zoom may choose to release a forced or prompted update, and customers will have to update to the latest version of the app to be on the most secure version. Zoom reserves the right to release or push out forced, off-schedule updates to help keep customers secure.

Frequently asked questions about the minimum version enforcements for VDI

I cannot update my Zoom Room or VDI client myself. How can I have my Zoom Room or VDI client updated?

Zoom Rooms and VDI clients can only be updated by account admins. Admins can remotely update the Zoom Room software through the Zoom web portal, while the VDI client is deployed through your VDI environment.

Are VDI Plugins required to be updated with the VDI Meeting Client as well?

Yes, the VDI Plugin and Meeting Client must be updated with each enforcement, with the minimum version detailed in the chart above. Customers are strongly encouraged to upgrade the VDI Plugin to the same version as the VDI client to benefit from the latest improvements in performance and new features.

Are patch releases also supported for 9 months?

Zoom will release one scheduled VDI version per release branch, a X.X.10 release. This release contains all the VDI-supported features for that entire release branch of the main desktop app, including enhancements and bug fixes from the main desktop app’s X.X.0 and X.X.5 releases.

Any releases outside of these scheduled releases (X.X.11, X.X.12, etc.) are typically considered extension patch (EP) releases. These releases will remain on the same release branch and generally include additional bug fixes, compatibility issues with virtual environments, and security enhancements found in that branch. This allows accounts with intensive testing and review processes to avoid having to start or restart a review process in order to resolve current issues and vulnerabilities.

Because these patch releases can be developed and released months after the scheduled release of that branch, Zoom cannot reasonably continue supporting these branches longer than already expected. As such, patch releases will generally have the same lifecycle as the scheduled release they are based on. For example, an X.X.13 patch, released 3 months after the X.X.10 release, would be affected by the same lifecycle enforcement as the X.X.10 version, even though it had only been available for 6 months.

Learn more about Zoom’s VDI release cycle.

Will VDI client/plugins only be supported for 9 months?

Due to technical limitations and considerations, many products will be supported beyond 9 months, but this is the minimum we are striving for. Zoom reserves the right to change this policy in the future. Zoom still encourages account admins to keep Zoom products as up-to-date as possible.

For more information, see the managing VDI minimum client versions article.

What VDI versions can I expect to be enforced beyond the upcoming enforcement?

Zoom understands that some customers require testing and updating processes for maintaining their VDI environments that extend beyond the 90-day notice of the next specific versions to be enforced. To aid with this, Zoom is providing a proposed longer-term outlook of VDI versions we anticipate to be enforced through the end of 2026.

Proposed VDI client and plugin version enforcements 2026

Bandwidth need when using 3G, 4G/LTE, or 5G

Category: Network configuration

You need to have a data plan on your mobile devices to start or join a video meeting.

For iPad, the active speaker will be in a non full-screen mode when transmitting in 3G, 4G/LTE, or 5G. For iPhone, the active speaker will be in full screen mode when transmitting in 3G, 4G/LTE, or 5G.

For both iPad and iPhone, you can see full screen with sufficient mobile bandwidth. You can also see multiple attendees in gallery view.

If the bandwidth is low, it will automatically scale to a smaller screen.

Note: To conserve data usage on mobile plan, you can turn off video. Or jump to “home” screen, iOS will put the app into “recording” mode which turns off video automatically, preserving audio.

In March 2025, Poly will update and consolidate its Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) servers to enhance provisioning efficiency and performance for all eligible Poly device models. Following this update, eligible devices will automatically connect to the new ZTP servers for provisioning. To ensure a seamless transition, you must allow network access and ensure your network permits eligible Poly devices to communicate with the new ZTP servers and associated platforms. Review documentation from Poly to confirm your network configuration aligns with the updated requirements. Prepare your network ahead of time to avoid disruptions in device provisioning. Devices that are unable to access the new ZTP servers due to network restrictions or improper configuration will fail to provision correctly. Instead of the feature being unavailable, users can select to blur their background or choose from four default virtual background images. When a virtual background image is selected, it is applied seamlessly within the WebRTC Redirection session. Web App
New or enhanced feature Video carrot toggle for video effects in the Zoom Web App Users can access video effects more easily through the new carrot (˅) toggle next to the Video icon in the Zoom Web App. This menu lets users quickly adjust camera settings, blur their background, enable auto-framing, show an avatar, or open video & effects settings. Web App
New or enhanced feature Ultrasound signal playback and detection for My Notes recording restrictions When you join a meeting with My Notes or recording restrictions enabled, the Zoom Web App plays an ultrasound signal through your device. The Zoom desktop app on the same device detects this signal from your system audio and applies the corresponding My Notes restriction, preventing transcription from occurring. The signal is only played when recording restrictions are active in the meeting and does not trigger in unrestricted meetings. This allows recording restrictions to be enforced automatically across both apps on the same device without requiring additional configuration. Web App
New or enhanced feature Stop Incoming Video setting enforcement in the Zoom Web App Users joining a meeting through the Zoom Web App will no longer see or be able to use the Stop Incoming Video option when it has been disabled and locked by an admin at the account level. Web App
New or enhanced feature Meeting info support in the Zoom Web App Users can view meeting details in a redesigned Meeting info layout when joining a meeting through the Zoom Web App. The updated layout provides clearer access to key information such as the meeting ID, passcode, host name, and invite link, all within a streamlined interface. Web App
New or enhanced feature Enhancements to waiting room audio testing Users in the waiting room of the Zoom Web App can test their speaker and microphone before joining a meeting. Clicking the Test Speaker and Mic button opens the Audio Settings popup, allowing users to verify and adjust their audio devices prior to entering a session. This reduces audio-related disruptions at the start of meetings. Web App
New or enhanced feature Encryption details and copy button in the Meeting info dialog Users can view encryption details and easily copy the meeting link directly from the Meeting info dialog in the Zoom Web App. The dialog displays the meeting’s encryption status and includes a new Copy button for quickly sharing the meeting link. Web App

General features
New or enhanced feature Enhancements to meeting window multitasking behavior Users joining a meeting through the Zoom Web App can multitask more efficiently within the same browser tab. Instead of occupying the entire page, the meeting is displayed within the Zoom Web App interface. When users navigate to other areas of the app, such as Chat or Canvas, the meeting automatically minimizes, enabling them to switch between tasks without leaving the tab or disrupting their meeting experience. This functionality is available in the Zoom Web App, including on Chromebooks, and is not supported in the standalone web experience. Web App
In-meeting features
New or enhanced feature Dark theme now available across all in-meeting panels on Zoom Web App The Zoom Web App now supports dark mode for the participant list, in-meeting chat, invite dialog, Q&A, polling, interpreter, and breakout room panels. This update delivers a consistent dark theme experience across all major in-meeting UI panels, aligning the Web App with the desktop app’s existing dark/light mode toggle. Web App
Meeting & Webinar features
New or enhanced feature Switch to Zoom App from the Zoom Web App during meetings and webinars Users who join a meeting or webinar through the Zoom Web App can switch to the Zoom desktop app during an active session using the new Switch to Zoom App option. If the desktop app is not already installed, the transition is completed only after the app has been downloaded and the user has successfully joined the session through the desktop app. During this process, the user remains connected to the web session and is not removed until the app join is confirmed. This behavior aligns with the existing Switch Device functionality and mirrors the experience currently available in Zoom Events on the web. Web App
Meeting features
New or enhanced feature Enhancements to the mobile web launcher Users joining a meeting from a mobile browser are guided more seamlessly toward opening the Zoom Workplace app. The updated launcher prioritizes the app experience while still displaying a join in browser option for users who prefer or require it. The flow reduces friction in the transition from the mobile browser to the native app, resulting in a faster path to joining meetings. Web App
Webinar features
New or enhanced feature Raise hand, poll, and Q&A support for mobile webinars on Zoom Web App Webinar attendees and panelists using the Zoom Web App on mobile devices now have access to Raise Hand, Poll, and Q&A features during webinars. These interactive capabilities, previously available only on the desktop web client, bring full webinar participation support to mobile web users. Web App

General features
New or enhanced feature Waffle menu enhancements with personalized product access Users can access a redesigned waffle menu that displays only the products they are entitled to use. Products appear in the same order as in the standard desktop app and open in new browser tabs for seamless navigation. The menu automatically hides disabled or deactivated products while still preserving access to related assets, such as recordings, through the hub until they are deleted in accordance with Zoom’s retention policies. Users can also reorder products within the menu and access three common meeting shortcuts for quick actions. This personalized experience ensures users see only relevant products and can navigate more efficiently across Zoom. Note: This feature is being rolled out gradually and is currently available to selected users only. Web App

New or enhanced feature Enhancements to profile and settings menu Users can access an updated Profile and Settings menu in the Zoom Web App that closely aligns with the desktop app experience. The new popup includes integrated download flows, allowing users to easily access Zoom desktop and mobile app installation options directly from the web interface. By matching the desktop app’s design and functionality, the updated menu enables seamless navigation between web and desktop environments. This alignment delivers a more consistent and intuitive experience across Zoom platforms while providing quick access to app downloads. The update addresses previously outdated content and supports a cohesive user experience across devices and platforms. Web App

The popups feature dynamic width settings that scale to 90% of the screen width with a maximum width of 1000 pixels. This responsive design ensures popups remain properly sized across different platforms and browser windows. The enhanced popup functionality provides optimal viewing experiences regardless of screen dimensions. Web App
New or enhanced feature Default video mirroring with customizable settings Users in Zoom Web App meetings have their video mirrored by default, matching the experience of the desktop app. The mirror video setting can be toggled on or off through the app settings menu. This functionality applies to both the user’s own video view and how they appear to themselves during meetings. The feature ensures consistent video presentation across all Zoom platforms while giving users control over their preferred viewing experience. Web App

New or enhanced feature Sync missing Zoom Contact Center system fields to Session History records In the Zoom Contact Center integration, custom fields are created on the Session History object to accommodate all missing engagement data fields. This update ensures all relevant Zoom Contact Center engagement data attributes are properly reflected in Session History records, improving data integrity and traceability. Web portal
New or enhanced feature Enhancement to Salesforce engagement mapping for contact center data Account owners and admins can access a new mapping configuration interface to connect Zoom Contact Center data with Salesforce fields. The configuration supports customizing the mapping of global and custom Zoom Contact Center variables, duration metrics, recording URLs, and other engagement data to corresponding Salesforce fields. When enabled, admins can view and select from dynamically queried Salesforce fields based on the chosen entity type. Admins can configure up to 20 mapping rows, and the system maintains logging functionality even if mapped fields are deleted. The system displays warning messages if mapped fields are deleted, ensuring admins stay informed of any configuration issues. New or enhanced feature Send emails for instant Zoom Meetings started from Salesforce Salesforce sends a meeting invite email every time an instant Zoom meeting is started from Salesforce, ensuring consistent communication and better visibility for all participants. New or enhanced feature Enhanced SFDC integration for 3P-recorded meetings with automated task/event creation The Zoom Revenue Accelerator (ZRA) and Salesforce (SFDC) integration automatically creates task/event activities in SFDC for meetings recorded via third-party platforms (e.g., external Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet). ZRA exposes webhooks with metadata identifying 3P recorded meetings. The integration layer will use these events to create corresponding tasks/events in SFDC. The existing Conversation analysis complete webhook will be extended or updated to include this data. ZRA also shifts from directly pushing analysis to SFDC to using webhooks for syncing, supporting create, update, and delete operations. On the SFDC side, updates include adding ZRA scopes and webhook support to the Zoom Marketplace App, along with an OAuth flow for authorization and backend logic to handle new data flows. Previously, only a ZRA analysis object was synced, limiting visibility into meeting activity. Web portal

New or enhanced feature Enhancements to Salesforce CTI Connector session history creation The Create session history at the start of the engagement setting allows session history to be created at the start of an engagement rather than at the end. When enabled, session history will be generated as soon as the engagement begins (answered), capturing key details such as caller number, dialed number, and start date/time. Once the engagement is completed, the session history will be updated with additional details from the engagement log. When disabled, the existing behavior remains unchanged, and session history will be created only upon engagement completion. Additionally, the Task record will continue to be created at the beginning of the engagement with the status Open, transitioning to Completed once the engagement concludes. The agent’s name will also be populated in the Owner field of the session history. This update ensures greater flexibility in tracking engagements and enhances real-time visibility for agents managing customer interactions. Web portal

New or enhanced feature Improved context sharing for transferred engagements in Zoom Contact Center When agents handle transfers across multiple channels, and for all transfer scenarios&mdash whether voice, video, or web chat&mdash the Salesforce Zoom Contact Center CTI Connector passes on important context when an engagement is transferred to another agent. This includes ensuring that the context is seamlessly transferred along with the engagement. The receiving agent will then see a screen pop with the correct customer record, allowing them to pick up where the previous agent left off. Additionally, for agents using the CTI connector, any CRM records created during the engagement, such as Case records in Salesforce, will be retained and passed on when the engagement is transferred. For agents using the CTI connector in ServiceNow, when receiving a transferred voice call, the agent will see the screen pop of the existing interaction record associated with the previous agent’s engagement, rather than creating a new record. This ensures that a single interaction record is maintained, with multiple phone logs associated with it, regardless of how many agents are involved in handling the call. For scenarios with multiple potential customer matches, clarifying information gathered by the first agent is also passed to the next agent. This feature must be enabled by Zoom. Web portal

August 25, 2024 version 2.17.0
Changes to existing features
  • Enhancement to participant information storage Participant email addresses are stored in Zoom Meetings records instead of participant names. The custom field, Participants by Emails, has been created on the meeting object and added to the layout. When adding participant details using the Zoom Meeting API, the system will check for the presence of email addresses alongside participant names. If an email address is available, it will be added to the newly created field. This field is included in the existing page layout of the package and added to the necessary permission sets. Field permissions will be respected when updating the field value to ensure proper access control. Previously, participant information stored on synced meeting records in Salesforce was limited to a comma-separated list of participant names.
  • Implement Apex for saving and updating a Task There are several enhancements and updates to the system to save and update tasks by running Apex directly on the integration frontend. As part of this enhancement, a new web service method will be introduced, which allows customers to create and update tasks directly on the Notes page, streamlining the process and reducing potential errors. Previously, tasks were saved or updated by the calling integration API, then the integration service call package API endpoint, which caused frequent timeout errors and long execution times in some customer organizations due to their custom Task logic.
New and enhanced features
  • General features
  • Add Zoom Revenue Accelerator option under Zoom User Settings The Zoom Revenue Accelerator Settings option has been added to the Zoom User Settings page. This enhancement includes open authorization (OAuth) functionality, enabling the addition of a Salesforce connection for the Zoom Revenue Accelerator (ZRA) product in the integration service database, similar to the existing process for other products. If a Salesforce connection already exists, the system will update the existing connection row with the ZRA product value. This connection will be used when making Salesforce API calls requested for ZRA dialer functionality through the proxy API.
  • Meeting & Webinar features
  • New fields and improved logic for Zoom Meetings The trigger logic for events and meetings has been updated. This update ensures that the creation of repeat events in Salesforce results in the appropriate creation of recurring meetings on the Zoom side. Additionally, new fields have been created for the recurring meetings data sync:
  • New fields have been added to the meeting object records to indicate the occurrence type. These fields help distinguish between individual occurrences and the main parent meeting record in the cases of recurring meetings.
  • A new field has been created to specify if a meeting is an occurrence or the main parent meeting record. This field identifies and manages recurring meetings effectively.
  • A new lookup field has been added. This field allows meeting records to relate to themselves, providing better organization and traceability for recurring meetings.
  • Store email addresses of the invitees in Zoom Meeting record To store invitees’ email addresses in Zoom Meeting records, a new custom field called Invitees by Emails is created on the meeting object. This field will also be added to the existing page layout of the package and incorporated into the necessary permission sets. Users must ensure that field permissions are observed when updating the value of this field.
  • Updates to meeting and event sync logic The event/meeting will always link to the matched contact/lead during sync, regardless of the owner. This change ensures more accurate and expected linking of records. Previously, when syncing meeting and event records created from outside Salesforce, the system only linked the meeting/event record to the matched contact/lead if the owner of the contact/lead matched the owner of the Zoom Meeting.
  • Update External Zoom Meeting page to include created meetings There are several updates to the Salesforce sync flow to include syncing meeting records upon creation. The External Zoom Meeting page will display meeting records that have been created but not synced to Salesforce (due to no matching record being found). Additionally, the design of the External Zoom Meeting page has been updated to align with the Meetings tab design on the Zoom Web App, providing a consistent user experience.
  • Enhancements to the synchronization of recurring meeting data in Salesforce Additional fields are introduced within the meeting object records to better categorize each meeting occurrence. These fields have been created to distinguish whether a record is an individual occurrence or the main parent record in a series of recurring meetings. To enhance relational data, a lookup field has been added, allowing meeting records to be associated with themselves and streamlining the organization of related meetings. The trigger logic on both event and meeting triggers has been updated, ensuring seamless handling of repeat event creation from Salesforce, which corresponds with the creation of recurring meetings in Zoom. Additionally, repeat events and Zoom Meeting (ZM) occurrence records have enhancements to configured settings for meeting data synchronization, ensuring that meeting data remains consistent and up-to-date across platforms. These updates simplify the management of recurring meetings and enhance the integration between Salesforce and Zoom.
  • Phone features
  • Support for softphone IVR navigation for call center agents Call center agents can use the Interactive Voice Response (IVR) key press functionality for softphone interfaces embedded within third-party applications like Salesforce and Microsoft Teams.
Resolved issues
  • Resolved an issue in Zoom Phone call queues where the voicemail link on a call queue is not automatically populating as expected when the voicemail is ready, and where the link only appears on the Zoom call log after a user with the necessary permissions accesses the related Task object associated with the Zoom call log.
  • Resolved an issue where call logs are being registered in Tasks for all users associated with a call queue, not just the user who answered the call this issue occurred regardless of whether the Log answered calls in queue against answered member option was checked or unchecked. Note: This fix ensures that call logs are correctly registered only for the user who answered the call when the option is enabled, or for all call queue members when the option is disabled. This fix will ensure that call logs accurately reflect the intended behavior based on the configuration settings.
  • Resolved an issue where users encountered discrepancies between the picklist values displayed in the native Salesforce UI and the Zoom softphone widget. Specifically, the softphone widget was not adhering to the profile-specific picklist values and dependent picklist values defined within Salesforce.
  • Resolved issue where no call history was recorded in Activity under Contact object (but under the member list object, there is call history), and where some call history shows NULL in related to, the other calls show the name in related to under the Task object.
  • Resolved an issue where there was a typo in the Zoom Contact Center SMS channel configuration.
  • Resolved an issue where the entity field could not get the entity list when saving the configuration in the Zoom Contact Center integration.
  • Resolved an issue regarding the direction displaying inbound on the engagement page, even though it was an outbound call.
  • Resolved an issue where the screen pop still occurred even with the settings being off in the softphone layout, and where the screen pop no longer occurred after removing the contact or all objects (contact, case, account).
  • Resolved an issue when the SFDC CTI connector was used for screen-pop cases, in some scenarios, the Relate to field was not populating the case number or engagement ID.
  • Resolved an issue where the profile section displays the Address book field as Salesforce even when this is not present when searching by extension number.
  • Resolved an issue where a new agent did not receive a screen pop for contact details when that same agent completed a warm transfer to another queue (escalates the call), and a new agent picked up.
  • Resolved an issue where users who rapidly send a second SMS following an initial message encountered an error that was displayed as a red banner at the top of the Zoom Phone widget interface, stating: “Your Direct Number has been removed by your admin. You cannot send message.”
  • Resolved an issue where the SMS tab stayed visible in the Zoom Phone widget in Salesforce when the user did not have the SMS capability enabled (and the user could not send or receive SMS messages).
July 22, 2024 version 2.16.0
Changes to existing features
  • Save lead or contact ID when a call is ringing The lead or contact ID will be saved during the ringing phase if the user clicks to dial or selects a lead/contact on the keypad. This change ensures that the target lead or contact is accurately recorded as soon as the call is initiated, reflecting the user’s intent from the moment they click to dial or make a selection. This enhancement ensures that call records accurately capture the intended target from the beginning of the call process. Previously, the lead or contact was only saved when the call was accepted and the Note page was displayed.
New and enhanced features
  • Contact Center Features
  • Screen Pop setting for post-engagement Account owners and admins can enable or disable the Screen pop activity/task record setting. This setting enhances agent workflows by controlling the screen pop behavior for task records created after call engagements. When this setting is enabled, the CTI will screen-pop the task record created for the call once the engagement is completed. Agents will see the auto-created task record screen pop once the engagement is completed. When this setting is disabled, the task record will still be created in Salesforce, but the screen pop will not occur after the engagement is completed. Agents will not see the auto-created task record screen pop, but the task record will still be created in Salesforce. This update aims to provide greater flexibility and control over task record management, improving the efficiency of post-call workflows for agents.
  • Phone features
  • Create click to SMS button for the mobile click-to-call layout Agents can click a phone number within the Salesforce mobile app to initiate a call directly through the Zoom Phone mobile app. An option for click-to-SMS has been added. This option allows agents to send SMS messages directly from the Salesforce mobile app. The click-to-SMS feature uses the admin settings for both click-to-call and click-to-SMS.

  • Resolved issues where no call history is recorded under Activity in the Contact object, though it is present under the Member List object, and where some call histories show NULL in the Related to field under the Task object.

New and enhanced features
  • Admin features
  • Screen Pop settings for voice channel The Salesforce CTI integration allows account owners and admins to configure the Screen Pop Settings for the voice channel in the Zoom Contact Center admin portal. This setting allows admins to choose whether agents see the screen pop of matching CRM records during call ringing or after the call is answered. This setting applies to both softphone layout and IVR-based search settings. Agents see the Screen Pop Settings according to the configured setting for inbound and outbound engagements.
  • Support for creating call log records for SMS activity Call log object records are available for SMS activity. This feature is disabled by default. When enabled, the phone numbers of the parties are added as fields in the task record and Zoom Call Log object.

This provides a streamlined and user-friendly interface for managing SMS channel settings with the new UI design. Additionally, a Computer Telephony Integration (CTI) adapter functionality, specifically for the Salesforce CRM adapter, is added to the ZECO platform. This feature enhances the integration between ZECO and Salesforce CRM, enabling more efficient and seamless telephony interactions within the CRM environment.

It also helps ensure accurate linking of meetings to the correct contacts or leads, even if attendees do not sign in to the meeting. Admins must reauthorize Zoom Meetings to use this feature.

Other features, such as creating tasks and session history after the SMS ends, are still available. This feature must be enabled by Zoom.

Using Zoom Support resources

Category: Support and resources > Support resources > Using Zoom Support

How to search Zoom’s resources

Start a search on Zoom Support

On the Zoom Support homepage, you can enter your query into the search bar to search through knowledge articles, Community posts, Learning Center courses, Developer documentation, and much more.

You can also search by clicking Search in the navigation menu when you’re viewing an article. As you type, you will see suggestions based on popular customer queries to help you formulate the right string of words. After entering your query, press the Enter key to access the Search results page.

Navigate the Search results page

By default, the Search results page showcases all the matching content available for you to view across a variety of Zoom content types.

Use the available filters to refine your search results. Some examples of the available filtering options include:

  • Source: Choose to search all available sources (default) or select specific content sources.
  • Category: Choose to select specific categories based on Zoom products or popular topics.

To reset and remove any filters you’ve added, click Clear All Filters.

Use generated answers

Occasionally, you may encounter a generated answer above the search results. The answer box will only appear if we have a high level of confidence in properly and accurately answering your query.

The components of the generated answer box include:

  • Generated answer for you: An answer is provided in the box based on your inquiry.
  • Helpful icon : The generated answer was helpful.
  • Not helpful icon: Provide specific feedback on the answer you were provided.
  • Copy answer icon : Copy the answer provided to your clipboard so you can paste it elsewhere.
  • Toggle on/off icon** **: Toggle the generated answer box on or off during the duration of your search experience.
  • Learn more citations: Shows which articles were used in order to generate the answer that was provided. You can click on these links to open the support articles.
  • Rephrase options: Rephrase the answer provided into a different format.
  • Step-by-step instructions icon
  • Bullet-point summary icon
  • Summary icon
Best practices and tips for searching

For best results, enter queries that are concise but not too short. For example, “meetings” may be too vague to provide helpful results, so “how to join a zoom meeting” will produce more dedicated and helpful results on the search page.

Use double quotes (“) around a word or phrase to find content that includes all of those words. For example,”payment method”.

Don’t worry about spelling! Our spell checker will automatically correct or provide suggestions.

Use synonyms or alternate phrasing if your first search doesn’t work (for example, try “invoice” vs. “billing statement”).

How to connect in the Zoom Community

The Zoom Community is an interactive support forum that complements the Zoom Support site. With a platform to connect with other Zoom customers, you can:

  • Ask questions, find solutions, and collaborate with global Zoom users
  • Get tips and best practices from other Zoom users
  • Form authentic human connections with real people with similar goals
  • Earn fun rewards and badges that foster a positive sense of knowledge and growth
Join the Community

We welcome all Zoom customers to come together on the Zoom Community to ask questions, share solutions, and collaborate with peers in creative ways.

Follow these simple steps and get started in the Zoom Community today:

  1. Access the Zoom Community.
  2. Sign in with your Zoom account credentials.
  3. Start engaging!
Search in the Community

There is a lot of content within the community, and oftentimes, frequently asked questions and answers already exist. Therefore, we encourage you to first search the community to see if your question has already been asked and answered.

Learn more about searching for existing answers in the Zoom Community.

How to use Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat

Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat is an AI-powered digital agent designed to quickly answer your questions, resolve issues without additional support, and deliver personalized experiences tailored to your needs.

  1. In the bottom-right corner of the Zoom Support site, click the Zoom Virtual Agent icon .
  2. Select from available options or enter your own prompt. Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat will respond according to your input. Not the answer you’re looking for? Try entering another query or check out our example prompts for help.
Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat example prompts

Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat performs best when asked clear, concise, and specific questions using simple language and asking one question at a time. We recommend avoiding overly complex or open-ended questions to get the most accurate response from our AI-powered digital agent.

Here are some of example questions or prompts you might ask:

  • How do I join a meeting?
  • My microphone isn’t working
  • I need to upgrade
  • I can’t login
Dos
  • Clearly state your purpose
  • Use simple language
  • Provide context
  • Use keywords
  • Utilize provided options
  • Provide feedback
Don’ts
  • Use slang or informal language
  • Expect human-like conversations
  • Try to trick the bot
  • Leave out key details
  • Ask overly complex questions

How to contact Zoom Support and manage existing cases

On the Contact Zoom Support page, when you click Contact Us, the Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat will open. Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat is an AI-powered digital agent designed to quickly answer your questions, resolve issues without additional support, and deliver personalized experiences tailored to your needs. Learn more about support plans and options based on account and user type.

Admins on accounts with a Premier Support plan will have additional workflows based on entitlements when contacting Zoom Support. They can choose between the digital agent experience or directly submit a case to Zoom Support.

Access your Support Dashboard

The Support Dashboard includes information about your plan type, support options, open cases, and more.

  1. In the top-right corner of the Zoom Support site, click Sign In.
  2. Sign in to your Zoom account. After signing in, you will be redirected back to the support site.
  3. In the top-right corner of the Zoom Support site, click your initials, then click Support Dashboard.
Support case statuses
  • New: A case has just been submitted and is awaiting pick up by Zoom Support.
  • Open: A case that has been picked up, assigned, and responded to by Zoom Support. Cases in this state may also indicate that the case may be awaiting a Zoom Support update after a customer has responded to Zoom Support.
  • Awaiting Info: Zoom: A case is awaiting info from Zoom. For example, the Zoom Support team would be working with peer teams to provide next steps or resolution. Alternatively, the case could be pending a new Zoom release for a fix to a reported issue.
  • Awaiting Info: Customer Response: A case is pending information from a customer based on the last Zoom update. Cases in this state will have 3 follow-ups completed over the course of 7 days. If a customer has not responded, Zoom Support will place the case in a Resolved state.
  • Resolved: Either the issue has been resolved, or the customer has not responded back to Zoom Support over the course of 3 follow-ups over 7 days. Cases in a Resolved state remain in this state for 7 days, and can be reopened during this timeframe, before entering the Closed state.
  • Closed: A case has transitioned from a Resolved state and can no longer be reopened.
Zoom Support response times

Learn about the order in which we prioritize our responses and the definitions for resolution when requesting support from Zoom.

Respond to an open support case
  1. Access your Support Dashboard.
  2. On the My Requests tab, in the table of open cases, click the number of the case that you want to update.
  3. (Optional) To add an attachment, click the Attachments tab, then upload the file for Zoom Support.
  4. On the Activity tab, add updates in the text box as needed, then click Send.
Escalate a case (account owners and admins)

Account owners and admins can escalate their own cases when eligible. For more information, learn how to escalate a support case.

Call Zoom Support

Zoom customers can call Zoom Support. Your experience may vary depending on your account type, user type, support plan, and additional account configurations.

  • Zoom Virtual Agent for Phone is available to all Zoom customers 24/7.
  • Live phone support is limited to account owners and admins on accounts with a Premier Support plan and will require account authentication. Regional business hours apply.

Note: Zoom Support does not currently support sign languages, such as American Sign Language (ASL), when contacting us by phone. We recommend using the Zoom Virtual Agent for Chat to request to chat with a live agent.

Using the Zoom Network Connectivity Tool

Category: Troubleshooting and known issues > Troubleshooting

How to access the Network Connectivity Tool

The network connectivity tool can be accessed after opening the Zoom desktop app or the Zoom Rooms app.

  • Zoom desktop app
  • Zoom Rooms app

The network connectivity tool can be accessed by the following keyboard shortcuts:

  • Windows: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D
  • macOS: Cmd+Option+Shift+D

Note: These keyboard shortcuts can be customized through the Keyboard Shortcuts tab of the desktop app’s Settings menu.

  1. On the controller or touch display, tap Settings .
  2. Tap Help, then tap Advanced diagnostics.

The network connectivity tool can also be accessed by the following keyboard shortcuts:

  • Windows: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D
  • macOS: Cmd+Option+Shift+D

How to test Zoom’s connection on your network

  • Zoom desktop app
  • Zoom Rooms app
Test general network connectivity
  1. After accessing the Network Connectivity Tool, click the Smart Test tab.
  2. Click Network Test.
  3. Click Start Test. The tool will test and report information on each of the following items as the section is complete:
  • Network Information: Tests basic network connectivity. When this section is complete, click View Results to view more information, such as network adapter name, IP address, IP activate, as well as detected proxy connections. Click Export Log to export client generated memlogs.
  • MTR: Tracing the connection between the device and Zoom servers. Click View Results to view a detailed breakdown of the traceroute. Click Export Log to export the client generated memlogs.
  • Service Status: Provides connectivity status and details for connections to Zoom Meetings and Chat services.
Test Zoom Phone connectivity
  1. After accessing the Network Connectivity Tool, click the Smart Test tab.
  2. Click Phone Test.
  3. Click Test. The tool will test and report information on each of the following items when the test is complete:
  • Latency (RTT): Tests the delay in communications between the device and Zoom’s servers.
  • Packet Loss: Tests the percentage of data packet loss between the device and Zoom’s servers.
  • Jitter: Tests the latency variation between the device and Zoom’s servers.
  • Codec: Lists the sending and receiving audio codec used during the test.
  • Clock Rate (KHz)
Test Zoom Meeting connectivity
  1. After accessing the Network Connectivity Tool, click the Smart Test tab.
  2. Click Meeting Test.
  3. Click Test. The tool will open a meeting to start the test. Note: To fully test audio and video connectivity, other participants should be invited to the test meeting.
  4. Click End to end the meeting and associated network test.

Once you have completed the desired tests, tap X to close the tool, then tap Send problem report to provide the data to Zoom support.

How to test specific connections with Zoom Support

If working with Zoom Support directly to troubleshoot connections to a specific location or server, a specific URL can be provided for the tool to run the same network test for this specific connection.

  2. Click the drop-down menu and one or more of the following test types:
  • MTR
  • Cert
  • Ping
  • Traceroute
  1. Enter the host domain or IP address provided by Zoom.
  2. Click Start Test.

If working with Zoom Support directly to troubleshoot connections to a specific location or server, a specific URL can be provided for the tool to run the same network test for this specific connection. Once you have completed the desired tests, tap X to close the tool, then tap Send problem report to provide the data to Zoom support.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the top-right corner, click you profile picture.
  3. Click Help, then click Give Feedback.
  4. In the Give Feedback form, select a Product Area from the drop-down.
  5. Under How satisfied are you with the experience?, choose a number between 1 and 5.
  6. Enter your feedback, then click Submit.
Send feedback specific to AI responses

If you’re using the AI chat panel in Zoom Workplace, you can submit feedback about AI responses directly from the chat panel.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. Send a prompt to the AI chat panel.

  3. After receiving a response, click the good response icon or bad response icon under the response.

  4. (Optional) Select a related category about what you liked or what could be improved.

  5. (Optional) Select or clear the check box next to Include your prompt with the feedback. Note: Allow users to send text feedback, including the prompts they send to AI must be enabled.

  6. (Optional) Enter additional feedback.

  7. Click Submit.

  8. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  9. In the top-left corner, tap your profile picture or initials.

  10. Tap Settings.

  11. Tap About.

  12. Tap Send feedback.

  13. On the Give feedback form, select a Product Area from the drop-down.

  14. Under How satisfied are you with the experience?, tap a number between 1 and 5.

  15. Enter your feedback, then tap Submit.

Send feedback specific to AI responses

If you’re using the AI chat panel in Zoom Workplace, you can submit feedback about AI responses directly from the chat panel.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Send a prompt to the AI chat panel.
  3. After receiving a response, tap the good response icon or bad response icon under the response.
  4. (Optional) Select a related category about what you liked or what could be improved.
  5. (Optional) Select or clear the check box to Include your prompt with the feedback. Note: Allow users to send text feedback, including the prompts they send to AI must be enabled.
  6. (Optional) Enter additional feedback.
  7. Tap Submit.

Viewing Zoom Workplace notifications in the activity feed

Category: Using the Zoom Workplace app > Features > Desktop App

How to open the activity feed and view Zoom notifications

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the app header, click the bell icon . The Activity panel will open. By default, your activity feed will show different types of activities, such as:
  • Direct messages from 1-on-1 chats
  • @mentions in channels or groups
  • Reactions to your messages
  • Channel updates you’re following
  • Shared files
  1. Click an unread notification to open that item. Actions will vary based on the notification type. For example, clicking an unread message opens the 1:1 chat, group chat, or channel where it was posted.
  2. Click the Focus tab to view smart follow-ups and highlights, or click the Other tab to view all notifications. By default, the activity feed focuses on unread notifications.
Filter notifications
  1. In the Activity panel, click the filter icon .
  2. Click the Show unread only toggle to enable or disable notifications based on read state. When enabled, only unread notifications will appear in the activity feed, and they will clear once you view them. When the Show unread only toggle is disabled, all notifications will appear in the activity feed, regardless of their read state.
  3. To filter notifications for a specific product, hover over Product, then click the product you want to view.
  4. To filter notifications by type, hover over Notification type, then click the notification type you want to view.
  5. To clear filters, click Clear all filters.
Clear all notifications

To clear all notifications in the Activity panel:

  1. Click the mark all as read icon .
  2. Click the filter icon , then click the Show unread only toggle to enable it.

How to customize notification preferences in the activity feed

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the app header, click the bell icon . The Activity panel will open.
  3. Click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Notification settings. The Manage Activity Center Notifications window will appear.
  5. (Optional) Make the following adjustments as needed:
  • To enable a notification, select the check box next to the activity type.
  • To disable a notification, clear the check box next to the activity type.
  • Click Reset to restore notification defaults.
  1. Click Save to confirm the changes.

Using Siri with Zoom

Category: Using the Zoom Workplace app > Features > Mobile App

How to add Zoom shortcuts to Siri

  1. Open the Zoom app.
  2. Tap Settings.
  3. Tap Siri Shortcuts.
  4. Choose the shortcut you would like to add and tap Add to Siri.
  5. Tap the red record button to record the sound for the shortcut.
  6. Tap Done to save the recorded sound.

How to perform a Zoom action with Siri

  • Say “Hey Siri, call [Zoom contact name] with Zoom” to start a Zoom meeting with that contact.
  • You can say “Hey Siri” followed by the words you chose when setting up the other shortcuts to perform these actions.
  • You can also give instructions to Siri by:
  • holding down the Home button on an iPhone 8 and older models
  • holding down the power button on an iPhone 10
  • holding down the side button on an iPhone 11 and higher models

Note: You do not need to set up a shortcut to call a Zoom contact with Siri.

Using the Zoom Web App on Chromebook and web browser

Category: Using the Zoom Workplace app > Features > Zoom Web App

How to use the Zoom Web App on Chromebook and web browser

Sign in and join

After installing and launching the Zoom Web App (or navigating to https://app.zoom.us/wc in your Chrome Browser), click Join Meeting to join a meeting without signing in. If you want to sign in and start or schedule your own meeting, click Sign In.

To sign in, use your Zoom, Apple, Google, Facebook, or SSO credentials. If you have a Zoom account but cannot remember your password, reset your password.

Home tab

After signing in, you will see the Home tab, where you will see these options centered around meetings:

  • New Meeting: Start an instant meeting.
  • Join: Join a meeting that is in progress.
  • Schedule: Opens a new tab to schedule a meeting.
Contact Center tab

If you have a Zoom Contact Center license, use this tab to access contact center features like voice, video, messaging, inbox, address book, and analytics.

Note: The Zoom Contact Center Zoom Web App supports all major features, such as voice, video, messaging, inbox, analytics, engagement details, disposition, and consumer profile. You can use the Zoom Contact Center Zoom Web App on all supported web browsers.

Zoom Chat tab

This tab contains your chats and channels. Here you can chat with contacts, share files and screenshots, set and check message reminders, and more.

Note: To enable users to access the Zoom Chat tab on the Zoom Web App, administrators must configure the following settings:

  • Advanced chat encryption should be disabled.
  • The setting for Users can share files in chats and channels should be either disabled or enabled and set to “Anyone”. The Zoom Chat could work if this setting is disabled. If users wish to enable it, then it should be set to “Anyone” exclusively.
Phone tab

If you have a Zoom Phone license, this tab allows users to make phone calls with Zoom Phone, as well as view their call and voicemail history, access shared lines, and send SMS messages.

Note: If you do not have Zoom Phone set up on your account, this tab will not be visible.

Meetings tab

This tab lists your upcoming meetings and webinars. Clicking on an upcoming meeting provides more information and options, such as starting the selected meeting.

Docs tab

This tab provides users with the ability to draft, organize, and share working materials and documents.

Contacts tab

Select the Contacts tab to view and manage your contacts. A directory of all your contacts and user groups are displayed, and, if your organization has Zoom Rooms, you will also see a list of Zoom Rooms.

Click on a contact to see more profile information, as well as the option to meet with a video meeting.

Whiteboards tab

This tab provides users a set of easy-to-use tools tocollaborate together to capture ideas, processes, and concepts.

In-meeting controls

Once you have started or joined a meeting, you can access the meeting controls located at the bottom of the meeting window (move your mouse in the Zoom window to display meeting controls).

Learn more about meeting controls for hosts, co-hosts, and attendees. You can also join a test meeting to familiarize yourself with meeting controls before joining a scheduled meeting.

Settings

From any tab of the Zoom Web App, click your profile picture, then click Settings. Alternatively, while in a meeting or webinar, you can click More in the meeting controls, then click Settings.

There, you can adjust audio, video, chat, and virtual background settings, further customizing your meeting experience to suit your devices and needs.

Learn more about the settings available in the Zoom Web App.

How to record a Zoom Meeting on a Chromebook

Note: Recording is also available for meetings joined through the web browser and only supports cloud recordings.

  1. Enable automatic recording.
  2. Sign in or join a meeting on the Chromebook.
  3. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the Record button .
  4. Click Record to the Cloud.
  5. To stop recording, click either the Stop Recording button or the End Meeting button to terminate the recording. You can also click Pause Recording button to temporarily pause the recording.

Zoom Frequently asked questions

Category: Using the Zoom Workplace app > Frequently asked questions

Getting started with Zoom

Where can I download Zoom?

You can download the latest version of Zoom from the Zoom Download Center. You’ll find the desktop app, mobile app, browser extensions, and other Zoom tools available for your device.

Learn more about downloading Zoom.

How do I use Zoom on my PC or Mac?

After installing Zoom, open the Zoom desktop app and sign in or join a meeting. You can start or schedule meetings, join meetings using a meeting ID or invitation link, adjust your audio and video settings, and manage your account from the desktop application.

Learn how to use the Zoom desktop app.

Do you need a Zoom account to join a meeting?

No. You can join most Zoom meetings without creating a Zoom account if you’re invited by the meeting host.

You’ll only need a Zoom account if:

  • You’re hosting or scheduling meetings.
  • The meeting host requires authentication.
  • You want to manage your personal settings or subscription.

Learn more about joining a Zoom meeting without an account.

How can I create a Zoom account?

You can create a free Zoom account by signing up at zoom.us/signup. A free account lets you host meetings, schedule meetings, and access your Zoom profile and settings.

Is Zoom free?

Yes. Zoom offers a free Basic plan that includes video meetings and collaboration features.

Paid plans provide additional meeting time, participant capacity, cloud recording, webinars, and advanced administration features.

A Basic Zoom license is free. Learn more about Zoom plans and pricing.

Where can I learn how to use Zoom?

Visit the Zoom Learning Center for free self-paced courses, tutorials, and training covering Zoom Meetings, Webinars, Phone, AI Companion, and other Zoom products.

Joining a Zoom meeting

How do I join a Zoom meeting?

You can join a Zoom meeting by:

  • Clicking the meeting invitation link.
  • Visiting https://zoom.us/join and entering the meeting ID.
  • Opening the Zoom desktop or mobile app and selecting Join.

Learn more about joining a meeting.

How do I connect my audio in Zoom?

When joining a meeting, select Join Audio or Join with Computer Audio to use your computer or mobile device’s speakers and microphone.

You can also choose a headset or external microphone from the audio settings.

Learn more about connecting your audio.

Can I use a Bluetooth headset with Zoom?

Yes. Zoom supports Bluetooth headsets and earbuds as long as they’re connected and compatible with your computer or mobile device.

Do I need a webcam to use Zoom?

No. A webcam isn’t required to join a Zoom Meeting or Webinar. You can participate using audio only, view other participants’ videos, and share your screen without turning on your camera.

Scheduling a Zoom meeting

How do I schedule a Zoom meeting?

You can schedule a meeting using:

  • The Zoom desktop app
  • The Zoom mobile app
  • The Zoom web app
  • The Zoom web portal
  • Supported calendar integrations

After scheduling, Zoom generates a meeting invitation that you can share with participants.

Learn more about scheduling a Zoom meeting.

How do I invite people to a Zoom meeting?

Open your scheduled meeting and copy the meeting invitation or join link. Send it by email, messaging app, calendar invite, or any communication platform your participants use.

Learn more about inviting others to join a meeting.

Hosting a Zoom Webinar

How do I buy a Zoom Webinar license?

To host webinars, you need a licensed Zoom account with a Zoom Webinar add-on. Webinar licenses can be purchased from the Billing page of your Zoom account.

How do I host a webinar?

After purchasing a webinar license:

  1. Schedule your webinar in the Zoom web portal.
  2. Share the registration or join link with attendees.
  3. Start the webinar from the Zoom desktop app or Zoom web portal.

Learn more about getting started with Zoom Webinars.

Meeting and webinar features

How do I share my screen in Zoom?

During a meeting, select Share Screen, choose the window, application, or entire screen you want to share, then click Share.

Learn more about sharing your screen.

Can I record my Zoom meeting?

Yes. Meeting hosts can record meetings locally to their computer. Licensed users can also save recordings to Zoom Cloud, depending on their account settings and admin permissions.

Learn more about computer recording and cloud recording.

Where are my Zoom recordings saved?

The recording location depends on the recording type:

  • Local recordings: Saved to your computer, typically in the Documents folder.
  • Cloud recordings: Available in the Recordings page of the Zoom web portal.

Learn more about locating your recording.

My Zoom account

Not sure where to start? Our billing and account management hub is designed to assist you in completing the most common billing and account management tasks.

Get Started

How do I reset my password?

You can reset your password at zoom.us/forgot_password.

After verifying your email, you’ll receive instructions to create a new password.

Read step-by-step instructions and how to fix common password issues.

How do I find my Zoom account?

Sign in to the Zoom web portal and open your Account Profile. Your role (Owner, Admin, or Member) appears in your account information.

Learn more about the Account Profile page.

How do I find my Zoom account owner?

Sign in to the Zoom web portal and open your Account Profile. The account owner’s information is displayed within your account details.

Learn more about the Account Profile page.

Zoom troubleshooting

Why isn’t my Zoom camera working?

If your camera isn’t working:

  • Check that Zoom has camera permission.
  • Close other apps using the camera.
  • Select the correct camera in Zoom settings.
  • Restart Zoom or your device.

Read tips on troubleshooting a camera that won’t start or show video.

Why is there an echo during my Zoom meeting?

Echo usually occurs when:

  • Someone joins the meeting audio from multiple devices.
  • Two participants are in the same room using speakers.
  • A microphone picks up audio from nearby speakers.

Using headphones often eliminates echo.

Learn about common causes of audio echo

Why isn’t Zoom audio working on my mobile device?

Check that:

  • Your microphone and speaker permissions are enabled.
  • Your device volume isn’t muted.
  • Bluetooth devices are connected correctly.
  • You’re connected to the meeting audio.

Restarting the Zoom app or reconnecting to audio often resolves the issue.

Read tips on troubleshooting audio that isn’t working on your iOS or Android device.

Additional Zoom products

Where can I learn about other Zoom products?

Visit the Zoom Support Center for help with Zoom Phone, Zoom Rooms, Zoom Events, Zoom Contact Center, AI Companion, and other Zoom solutions.

Getting started with the Zoom Workplace desktop app

Category: Using the Zoom Workplace app > Getting started > Desktop App

How to sign in and join

After installation, open the Zoom Workplace app on your device. When you open the app for the first time, you have the options to sign in, join a meeting, or sign up.

  • Sign in: If you already have a Zoom account and want to sign in or start your own scheduled meeting, click Sign in.
  • Join a meeting: To join a meeting without signing in, click Join a meeting. You will be prompted to enter the meeting ID and passcode.
  • Sign up: If you don’t have a Zoom account yet, click Sign up to create a free Basic account.

How to use the Zoom Workplace desktop app

The Zoom Workplace desktop app interface was updated in version 6.7.0. The following instructions are based on the updates made in version 6.7.0.

Navigate through the app

On the Zoom desktop app, use the left navigation bar to select from various Zoom workspaces available to you, such as Chat, Calendar, Phone, Contacts, and Hub. You can customize your navigation bar by dragging or pinning tabs to fit your needs. The More tab includes additional items not currently displayed on the left navigation bar, and your most recently used tab will appear above the More tab.

The left navigation bar also includes quick access to desktop settings. At the bottom, click the gear icon to manage your settings.

In the app header, use the back and forward icons to navigate between your recently visited pages, or click the history icon to view your recent history.

Global search

In the app header, use the search bar to perform a global search of your Zoom Workplace account, including contacts, meetings, chats, channels, whiteboards, docs, and more. You can refine your search results for certain content types using sorting and filters.

Create menu

Next to the search bar in the app header, click the plus icon (+) to access quick links for creating a new meeting, chat, doc, clip, and more.

Activity feed

In the app header, click the bell icon to open the Activity feed. In the Activity feed, you can view your notifications, mark them as unread, filter the displayed notifications, and manage the types of notifications you receive.

Calendar side panel

In the app header, click the calendar icon to open the calendar side panel. In the calendar side panel, you can view your upcoming meetings for the day or choose a different date to view scheduled meetings. Join a meeting directly from the calendar side panel, or click the ellipsis icon on a scheduled event to access options such as copying the invitation, emailing everyone, declining the invitation, and more.

If you have a Google, Microsoft 365, or Exchange account, connect your third-party calendar to manage all your meetings and events in one place in the Zoom Workplace app.

Profile and settings

In the app header, click your profile picture (or initials) to access your profile information, set your availability and status message, check for updates, manage app settings, get support, and sign out.

AI chat panel

From the Home tab or a product tab that supports the AI chat panel, click the Open AI chat icon . In the AI chat panel, you can ask questions and receive tailored, contextual responses sourced from the different data sources and contexts available to you.

How to use in-meeting controls

When you join or start a meeting, your meeting controls are available in the meeting controls toolbar located at the bottom of the meeting window (move your mouse in the Zoom window to display meeting controls if the toolbar isn’t visible). The meeting controls toolbar includes primary meeting functions depending on your meeting role and what features you have access to, such as Audio, Video, Participants, Chat, Share, and more. Additional options are available in the More menu. You can customize the toolbar by dragging an icon to pin or remove it from the toolbar.

Learn more about meeting controls for hosts, co-hosts, and participants.

You can also join a test meeting to familiarize yourself with meeting controls before joining a scheduled meeting.

Additional resources

  • For more help with getting started on Zoom, review our guide for new Zoom users
  • Learn how to add or update your virtual background
  • Sign in to your Zoom account on the Zoom Support site and explore resources for the products included in your current plan
  • Visit the Zoom Learning Center to explore self-paced courses and learn the basics of Zoom anytime, at your own pace

Starting the Zoom Workplace desktop app

Category: Using the Zoom Workplace app > Getting started > Desktop App

How to open the Zoom desktop app

  • macOS
  • Windows
  • Web
Opening Zoom
  1. In the Dock, locate the Finder icon .
  2. Right-click on the icon, then click New Finder Window.
  3. In the new window, click Applications.
  4. Find and double-click the zoom.us application to start the app.

Note: If Launchpad is on your dock, you can click that to access your applications list, and open Zoom from there.

Saving Zoom to the Dock

Once you have the Zoom desktop app open, you can save it to your dock.

  1. In the Dock, right-click the Zoom icon .
  2. Hover your mouse over Options, then click Keep in Dock.

Note: On all versions of Windows, you can pin the Zoom desktop app to your taskbar, by right-clicking on Zoom desktop app, and then clicking Pin to Taskbar.

Windows 10
  1. In the taskbar, click the Windows icon.
  2. In your apps list, scroll until you get to the Zoom folder.
  3. Click on the Zoom folder.
  4. Double click Start Zoom to launch the application.
Windows 8
  1. In the taskbar, click the Windows icon.
  2. Click the down arrow, in the bottom left corner, to access All Apps.
  3. Scroll to the apps until you see Zoom, then click Start Zoom .
Windows 7
  1. In the taskbar, click the Windows icon.
  2. Click All Programs.
  3. In the programs list, click on the Zoom folder.
  4. Double click Start Zoom .

Using the VDI client is recommended for all virtual environments. This includes environments that use media extensions which Zoom does not currently support. Using the standard desktop app in a VDI environment is not supported or recommended.

If the Zoom icon has disappeared from your desktop and you cannot locate it after following the steps above, you need to install the Zoom desktop app.

Getting started with the Zoom Workplace mobile app

Category: Using the Zoom Workplace app > Getting started > Mobile App

How to sign in and join

After installation, open the Zoom Workplace app on your device. When you open the app for the first time, you have the option to sign in, join a meeting, or sign up.

  • Sign in: If you already have a Zoom account and want to sign in or start your own scheduled meeting, tap Sign in.
  • Sign up: If you don’t have a Zoom account yet, tap Sign up to create a free Basic account.
  • Join meeting: To join a meeting without signing in, tap Join meeting. You will be prompted to enter the meeting ID and passcode.

How to use the Zoom Workplace mobile app

Navigate through the app

Use the navigation bar at the bottom of the mobile app to select from various Zoom products and options you have access to. The More tab includes additional items not currently displayed on the navigation bar.

Note: Some tabs may not be visible to you if you do not have access to that feature or product.

  • Home tab
  • Chat tab
  • More tab

The Home tab provides a centralized view of your daily schedule. When you open the app or tap the Home tab in the navigation bar, you will see relevant information for the current day by default. You can navigate to previous or upcoming days to view meetings and schedules for other dates.

On the Home tab:

  • In the app header:
  • Tap the ellipsis icon to access the following actions:
  • Meet with Personal ID: Start a meeting using your personal meeting ID (PMI), send an invitation, or edit your PMI details.
  • Room: Connect to Zoom Rooms from your mobile device. You can start a meeting from a Zoom Room, share your screen to the room, chat and view shared content, and more.
  • Scan QR code: Scan a QR code or share your QR code with others to add you as a contact.
  • My anytime meetings: View your recurring meetings with no fixed time.
  • Transfer a meeting
  • Tap the Zoom AI icon to open the AI chat panel. In the AI chat panel, you can ask questions and receive tailored responses sourced from the different data sources and contexts available to you.
  • Quick actions menu:
  • Meet : Start an instant meeting using your PMI or a new meeting ID. Learn about in-meeting controls for hosts.
  • Join : Join a meeting using the meeting ID. Learn about in-meeting controls for participants.
  • Schedule : Schedule a one-time or recurring meeting.
  • Share : Enter a sharing key or meeting ID to share your device screen to a Zoom Room.
  • My Notes : Start My Notes to take notes during a meeting or webinar and enhance them with a transcript.
  • Meetings and scheduled events:
  • By default, events for the current day are shown. Tap the day to view scheduled events for that day, or scroll down to view scheduled events for other days.
  • Each meeting for the selected day is represented by a meeting card. Meeting cards may display the following details:
  • Meeting title (topic)
  • Meeting host
  • Start time
  • Location, such as a conference room or physical address
  • Number of participants
  • Tap on a meeting card for full meeting details. Meeting content, such as recordings, transcripts, and summaries, is accessible from the meeting details.

Note: Without the calendar and contacts integration enabled, Zoom will only show meetings you’ve scheduled, and any meetings you have been invited to will not be shown. You will need to integrate your calendar with Zoom to display meetings you’ve been invited to or other non-Zoom meetings.

Tap the Chat tab to view and send messages to a contact, a group, or a channel.

  • Tap the options at the top to quickly view different types of messages, including All, Mentions, Chats (direct messages), Channels, Meeting chats, Shared spaces, and more.
  • To filter and sort messages, such as only viewing unread messages, tap the filter icon .
  • To start a new message, tap the plus icon .

The More tab includes additional items not currently displayed on the navigation bar. Depending on the Zoom products and permissions you have access to, you may see icons such as Mail, Calendar, Whiteboards, Events, Apps, Clips, Phone, Contacts, Tasks, Canvas, and more.

To customize your icon display order, tap Reorder, then drag-and-drop icons as needed between the More menu and the navigation bar. When you’re finished customizing the display order, tap Done.

Profile picture and settings

In the app header, tap your avatar or profile picture. This is where you can view your sign in information, availability, and status message, as well as manage your profile information and app settings.

  • QR code: Tap the QR code icon to scan a QR code or share your QR code with others to add you as a contact.
  • Email: Below your display name, tap your email address to view which account you’re currently signed in with or switch to a different account.
  • Availability: Tap to manually change your presence status.
  • Status: Tap to add, update, or clear your status message, then tap Save.
  • My profile: Tap to view and manage your profile information. From your profile menu, you can:
  • Update your profile picture
  • Edit your display name
  • Delete your account
  • View or edit your personal meeting (ID)
  • View your license assignments
  • Manage the devices where you’re logged in
  • Settings: Tap to view the Settings menu, where you can manage your app settings, view About information, switch to a different account, and sign out.
Global search

In the app header, tap the search icon to perform a global search of your Zoom Workplace account, including contacts, meetings, chats, channels, whiteboards, docs, and more. You can refine your search results for certain content types using sorting and filters. Your searches are synced with the Zoom desktop app.

AI chat panel

In the app header, tap the Zoom AI icon to open the AI chat panel. In the AI chat panel, you can ask questions and receive tailored responses sourced from the different data sources and contexts available to you.

How to view your recurring meetings with no fixed time on the mobile app

You can view your recurring meetings with no fixed time from the Home tab.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the navigation bar, tap the Home tab .
  3. In the app header, tap the ellipsis icon .
  4. Tap My anytime meetings.

How to start or join a meeting on the mobile app

Start an instant meeting
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the navigation bar, tap the Home tab .
  3. Tap Meet.
  4. Tap Start a meeting.
Start a scheduled meeting
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the navigation bar, tap the Home tab .
  3. Locate the meeting you scheduled.
  4. On the meeting card, tap Start.
Join a meeting
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. In the navigation bar, tap the Home tab .
  3. If you know the meeting ID and passcode, tap Join, then do the following:
  4. Enter the meeting ID and passcode.
  5. Tap Join.
  6. If you have meetings listed on the Home tab, tap the meeting card, then tap Join.

How to use in-meeting controls

When you join or start a meeting on the Zoom Workplace mobile app, your meeting controls are available in the toolbar located at the bottom of the meeting window (tap in the Zoom window to display meeting controls if the toolbar isn’t visible). The meeting controls toolbar includes primary meeting functions depending on your meeting role and what features you have access to, such as Mute/Unmute, Start video/Stop video, and Chat. Additional options are available in the More menu.

Learn more about meeting controls for hosts, co-hosts, and participants.

You can also join a test meeting to familiarize yourself with meeting controls before joining a scheduled meeting.

Permissions requested by the Zoom mobile app

The Zoom mobile app may ask you to authorize access to the following permissions with a pop-up, depending on which features you are accessing in Zoom.
