  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. Click the** Chat** tab . Note: If you do not see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click Chat.
  3. Select a chat.
  4. In the chat compose box, click one of the following options:
  • Emoji : Display a list of emojis. Click an emoji to add it to your message. Click GIF to search for and add an animated GIF to your message.
  • GIF : Display a list of GIFs. Click GIF to add an animated GIF to your message. Click the heart icon to view your favorite GIFs.
  • File : Display the system file browser to select a file to upload.
  • Screenshot : Capture a screenshot of your entire screen, or specific tab or window open in your browser.
How to invite chat members to a meeting

You can easily start a meeting from any chat conversation, which will automatically invite all members in a group chat or channel to a meeting.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.
  2. Click the** Chat** tab . Note: If you do not see the Chat tab, click the More tab, then click Chat.
  3. Select a chat.
  4. In the top-left corner of the chat window, click the video icon .
  5. (Optional) Click the down arrow icon next to the video icon to decide if you want to meet with video or not. This is the default for the meeting and participants can enable their videos after joining.
  6. Click Yes to confirm inviting all members of the chat group or channel to a meeting.
How to start a new 1:1 or group chat

To begin messaging with one or more Zoom users:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap the** Chat** tab .
  3. At the top-right corner of the chat panel, tap the ellipsis icon , then tap the New message icon .
  4. Enter the name or email address of the Zoom contact you wish to chat with. Add additional names or email addresses as needed.
  5. Tap OK.
  6. Enter your message.
  7. In the lower-right corner of the chat compose box, tap the send icon .
How to join a public channel

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  2. Tap the Zoom Chat tab .

  3. At the top-right corner of the chat panel, tap the ellipsis icon** , then tap Join a Channel**.

  4. Use the search bar to find a channel.

  5. Tap a channel to view more information about the channel.

  6. Tap Join Chanel. You will join the channel and can begin messaging those members.

Learn more about joining, creating, and using channels.

How to add an external contact

If you’re part of an organization that uses Zoom, everyone in your organization is typically included in your contacts directory automatically, allowing you to begin chatting with anyone in your contacts directory. If you need to chat with someone outside of your organization, you will need to manually add them as a Zoom contact.

Follow these steps to add external Zoom users to your contacts. You can do this even if the other contact does not yet have a Zoom account.

  1. Sign in to the mobile app.
  2. Tap the Contacts tab .
  3. Tap the add icon .
  4. Enter one email address at a time.
  5. (Optional) You can send the contact request with personalized message.
  6. Tap Add.
  • If the person has a Zoom account, they’ll receive a contact request within Zoom Chat. After they accept the request, you can start chatting with them.
  • If the person doesn’t have a Zoom account, they’ll receive an invitation email to create a Zoom account so they can connect with you. Once they sign up for Zoom, they should click on the link in the email again to confirm the connection.

Learn more about managing your contacts.

How to adjust notifications for chats

You can adjust chat notifications for all chat and channels at once, as well as at the individual chat level. This allows you to prioritize chats and channels that need your immediate attention when there is an update, while setting defaults for new channels you are added to.

Adjust default notification settings for all chats

You can customize how you’re notified of unread messages and whether you receive push notifications for new messages. Follow these steps for basic settings to get you started:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap your profile picture in the top-left corner, then tap Settings .
  3. Tap the Zoom Chat tab .
  4. Adjust the following settings to manage your notifications:
  • Unread Messages
  • Keep all unread messages on top in chat and channel lists: Keep chats with unread messages to the top of your chats list. Select this option if you want to bring more attention to chats with unread messages. This setting only applies to chats under the Recents section.
  • Show unread count for channels: Display an icon with the number of unread messages beside each chat. If this is not selected, you will see a red dot to indicate unread messages.
  • Show unread count for meeting chats: Display an icon with the number of unread messages beside each meeting chat. If this is not selected, you will see a red dot to indicate unread messages.
  • Move messages with new replies to the bottom of the chat: Messages that have received additional replies since you last checked are moved to the bottom of the chat.
  • When viewing unread messages in a channel:
  • Start at the first unread: Choose this option if you want to go directly to the first unread message in the channel.
  • Start at the latest: Choose this option if you want to go to the most recent unread message in the channel.

Learn more about other available chat notification settings.

Adjust notification settings for specific group chats and channels

You can also change notification settings for specific group chats and channels. Follow these steps to get you started:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap the** Chat** tab .
  3. Tap the chat channel or group chat.
  4. In the top-right corner, tap Settings .
  5. Adjust the following settings:
  • Show unread message count (): Display an icon with the number of unread messages beside each chat. If this is not selected, you will see a red dot to indicate unread messages.
  • Notifications: Select when you want to receive push notifications. Push notifications are displayed using your device’s push notification system.
  • All messages: Get notified for all message activity.
  • Mention and replies: Includes all chats, group or personal mentions, and replies to you.
  • Off: Turn off all chat notifications.
  • Mute channel: Turn off all notifications unless mentioned. Note: Adjusting the notification setting for an individual chat channel or group chat will create an exception to the default notification settings for Zoom Chat.
How to search for group chats, channels, or specific messages

You can use the global search bar at the top of the app to search for chats.

How to send files, video or voice messages, screenshots, emoji, animated GIFs, or code snippets

In addition to regular chats, you can use the chat compose box to send additional types of messages or files to enhance your Zoom Chat experience. Some options listed below may not be available, depending on your personal settings in the desktop app or any admin settings at the account or group level.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap the** Chat** tab .
  3. Tap a chat, group chat, or channel.
  4. To the right of the chat compose box, tap the mic icon to start recording an audio message.
  5. In the chat compose box, tap the smiley icon .
  • Tap GIF to add an animated GIF to your message.
  • Tap the heart icon to view your favorite GIFs.
  1. To the left of the chat compose box, tap the plus icon and choose from the following options:
  • Send a File : Display options to attach a file to the message. Tap Your Computer or any 3rd-party file services to send a file on Zoom Chat. Note: If sending a video file, recipients will be able play the video directly in the chat window.
  • Video Message : Start recording a video message to attach to your message.
How to invite chat members to a meeting

You can easily start a meeting from any chat conversation, which will automatically invite all members in a group chat or channel to a meeting.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap the** Chat** tab .
  3. Tap a chat, group chat, or chat channel.
  4. To the left of the chat compose box, tap the plus icon .
  5. Tap Video Meet .
  6. Tap Yes to confirm inviting all members of the chat group or channel to a meeting.

How to navigate the Zoom Chat sidebar

Note: Upgrade to the latest desktop app version (6.7.0) to access the redesigned Zoom Chat sidebar.

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
Default tab view and customization

When you first open Zoom Chat, you’ll see the following default tabs:

  • All: Displays all your Zoom Chat conversations in one place.
  • Mentions : Shows messages where you’ve been @mentioned directly, making it easier to stay on top of important notifications.
  • Chats : Includes all your direct conversations, from 1:1 chats to group discussions.
  • Channels : Lists the channels you’ve joined, keeping you connected to your various teams and projects.
  • Meeting chats : Stores in-meeting chat conversations, which are accessible even after the meeting has ended.
  • More : This section includes additional tools and settings for further customization and enhanced functionality.

These tabs are pinned at the top of the sidebar for quick access. You can add, remove, and reorder them based on your preferences.

Additional tools in the More section

You can access and manage additional tools by navigating to the More section:

  • Starred: Messages you’ve marked as important for quick access.
  • Folders: Custom folders you’ve created to organize chats and channels.
  • Shared Spaces: Displays spaces created for collaboration across different teams, keeping your cross-functional projects organized and accessible.
  • Apps: Provides easy access to third-party apps and integrations connected with Zoom Chat, helping you stay productive within your workspace.
  • Drafts: Messages you started typing but haven’t sent yet.
  • Sent: A list of messages you’ve sent.
  • Bookmarks: Messages or content you’ve saved for reference.
  • Reminders: Notifications you’ve set for messages you want to revisit later.
  • Missed calls: Shows your missed Zoom Phone or Zoom Chat calls.
  • External: Conversations with external contacts or organizations.
  • Drag to pin or reorder: Click Reset to restore the sidebar to its original layout.

Notes:

  • Reorder tabs in the sidebar by dragging and dropping them into your preferred position.
  • You can also drag tabs in or out of the More section to choose which tabs are visible in your main sidebar view.
Chat drop-down

A quick-access menu that lets you customize how your Zoom Chat sidebar is displayed and managed. From this menu, you can separate chats and channels, limit viewing to one section at a time, choose whether to show unread counts for channels and meeting chats, collapse all sections, or open your chat settings.

Sidebar behavior
  • Separate chats and channels: Organize your sidebar by displaying chats and channels in different sections instead of grouping them together.
  • Open only one section at a time: Keep your sidebar tidy by allowing only one section (chats, channels, or meeting chats) to expand at a time. Expanding a new section will automatically collapse the others.
  • Manage sidebar: Open the Zoom Chat settings menu to customize your chat preferences.
Badging
  • Show unread count for channels: Display an icon with the number of unread messages beside each channel. If this option is off, you’ll see only a red dot to indicate unread messages.
  • Show unread count for meeting chats: Display an icon with the number of unread messages beside each meeting chat. If this option is off, you’ll see only a red dot to indicate unread messages.
  • Manage badges: Open the Zoom Chat settings menu to manage badge settings.

Replying to and editing Zoom Chat messages

Category: Getting started and setting up

How to send and edit a Chat message

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Zoom Web App
  • Android | iOS
Reply to a message

After receiving a chat message, you can reply to that message to keep all related replies in the same thread. This allows users to easily identify replies and keep content around that topic in one tidy thread.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the Chat tab , select a 1:1 chat, group chat, or channel.
  3. Hover your cursor over the message you want to reply to. Additional options will appear to the right of the message.
  4. Click the reply icon .
  5. Enter your reply in the chat compose box in line with other messages in the thread, then press the Enter key. Besides text, replies can also send screenshots, files, code snippets, emojis, or animated GIFs. Your reply will be displayed under the parent message. All future replies will be displayed under the parent message.

Note: If adding an emoji to the message or reply, you can search for and insert emojis by typing a : followed by at least two characters to find matching emojis. For example, :jo will provide the :joy:, :joy_cat:, and :joystick: emojis. You can also click the smiley icon in the chat compose box to see all available emojis, GIFs, and saved GIFs to select from.

Add reactions to messages

Some messages may not need a direct response, so you may opt to acknowledge or react to them with emojis. These reactions are displayed under the message for everyone to see, as well as add their own reaction. This is a great way to gauge the response to a message or announcement.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the Chat tab , select a 1:1 chat, group chat, or channel.
  3. Hover your cursor over the message you want to react to. Additional options will appear to the right of the message.
  4. Click the reaction icon . A small box will appear, providing you with your recently used emojis for quick access.
  5. Select a recently used emoji or click the more option to view the full list of available emojis. The selected emoji reaction will appear below the message. Additional emojis can be selected.
  6. (Optional) To remove the reaction, click the emoji that you added to the message.

If others have already reacted with the emoji you would like to use, you can click the emoji displayed below the message to send that reaction as well. The number beside the emoji will increase to note the additional reaction. Hovering your cursor over the emoji will show all the users who have used that reaction for this message.

Format a message with standard text formatting

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. In the Chat tab , select a 1:1 chat, group chat, or channel.

  3. Enter your message in the chat compose box. You can apply formatting as you enter the message or apply it to sections after you’ve finished typing the message by highlighting the text and choosing from the available options.

Zoom Chat provides the following standard formatting options:

  • Bold icon : Bold the highlighted text.
  • Italicize icon / : Italicize the highlighted text.
  • Strikethrough icon : Strikethrough the highlighted text.
  • Bulleted list icon : Begin a bulleted list.
  • Numbered list icon : Begin a numbered list.
  1. Press the Enter key or click the send icon . Note: If using rich text formatting, you must click the send icon to send your message, as the Enter key will just make a new paragraph.

You can also use the following keyboard shortcuts to format text:

  • Bold: Ctrl/Cmd + B
  • Italicize: Ctrl/Cmd + I
  • Strike-through: Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + X
  • Bulleted list: Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + 8
Format a message with rich text formatting

Beyond the standard formatting options, you can also utilize additional formatting options, such as colored or highlighted text, adjusting the indent, adding headings, and more.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. In the Chat tab , select a 1:1 chat, group chat, or channel.

  3. Below the chat compose box, click Format to access the rich text options.

Zoom Chat provides the following formatting options:

  • Bold icon : Bold the highlighted text.
  • Italicize icon / : Italicize the highlighted text.
  • Underline icon : Underline the selected text.
  • Strikethrough icon : Strikethrough the highlighted text.
  • Text color icon : Access both the ability to adjust the color of the text itself and/or the color highlight around the text. The Clear option removes any selected colors and reverts the text to standard black/white formatting.
  • Text size icon : Adjust the size of the font, choosing from Small, Medium, and Large text sizes.
  • Link icon : Insert a link for the highlighted text.
  • Heading icon : Adjust the style of the text, choosing from Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3, and Paragraph.
  • Bulleted list icon : Begin a bulleted list.
  • Numbered list icon : Begin a numbered list.
  • Increase indent icon : Increase the indent of the selected text.
  • Decrease indent icon : Decrease the indent of the selected text.
  • Quote icon : Create a quote of text.
  • Eraser icon : Clear all formatting of the selected text.
  1. Click the send icon to send your message to the contact(s) or channel.

Note: If using rich text formatting, you must use the send icon , as the Enter key will just make a new paragraph.

Format a message with Markdown formatting
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. In the Chat tab , select a 1:1 chat, group chat, or channel.
  3. Enter your message in the chat compose box. You can apply Markdown formatting as you enter the message or apply it to sections after you’ve finished typing the message. Learn more about available Markdown actions in Zoom Chat.

Zoom Chat comparison by platform

Category: Getting started and setting up

Comparison of Chat desktop app, mobile app, and Zoom Web App features

Click the embedded links to learn more about each feature.

[TABLE]

Using the Google Drive for Chat App

Category: Integrations, apps, and extensions > Apps and Marketplace

How to install from the Zoom App Marketplace

  1. Sign in to the Zoom App Marketplace.
  2. In the top right of your screen, search for Google Drive by Zoom
  3. Click Add.
  4. Review the requested permissions and click Authorize. Once installed, the app is displayed under the Apps section of the Chat tab of the Zoom desktop app.

How to connect the Chat App to your Google Workspace Account

  1. Sign in to the desktop app.

  2. Click the Chat tab .

  3. At the bottom of the left chat panel, find the Apps section.

  4. Select Google Drive.

  5. Click Connect. You will be prompted to connect your Zoom account with your Google Workspace account.

  6. Sign-in with your Google Workspace account.

When sign-in is successful, you will see a message from the Chat App indicating the app is ready to use.

How to use the Google Drive for Chat App

With Google Drive for Chat you will be able to

  • Share files from Google Drive within Chat
  • Create Google Docs, Presentations, and Spreadsheets
  • Set Sharing Permissions for files shared from Google Drive
Share a file
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab .
  3. Select the 1:1, group chat, or channel you want to share a file with.
  4. Below the chat text compose box, click on the Google Drive app icon. A menu of options will appear
  5. Click Share from Google Drive. The Google Drive file picker will appear.
  6. Search for and select a file from your Google Drive
  7. Click Select to post it to the Chat conversation.

Docs, spreadsheets, and presentations can also be quickly shared by using a slash command.

Create a new Google Drive file
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab .
  3. Select the 1:1, group chat, or channel you want to share a file with.
  4. Below the chat text compose box, click on the Google Drive app icon. A menu of options will appear
  5. Click the type of document you want to create:
  • Create a Document
  • Create a Spreadsheet
  • Create a Presentation
  1. Enter a title for the new document.
  2. Click Create. A new document will be created and available for use.

Docs, spreadsheets, and presentations can also be quickly created by using a slash command.

Set Sharing Permissions for files shared from Google Drive

Upon posting a document from Google Drive to a chat conversation, you will be able to set your sharing permissions. This allows you to control who has access to the document.

  1. Click on the document preview box.
  2. Click the Share with… drop-down menu.
  3. Choose who can access the document (Channel Members, Your Organization, or Anyone with link) and what type of access they have to the document (View, Comment, or Edit) After updating doc permissions, a message only visible to you will be posted to the channel confirming who now has access to the document.
Slash commands for the Google Drive app

Once installed, the Google Drive app can be used from any Chat channel. The following slash commands are available in any 1:1, group chat, or chat channel:

  • /googledrive connect Enter /googledrive connect to Sign in to your Google Account
  • /googledrive disconnect Enter /googledrive disconnect to Sign out of your Google Drive account.
  • /googledrive help Enter /googledrive help to receive a list of all available commands.
  • /googledrive create doc Enter /googledrive create doc to create a new Google Docs document.
  • /googledrive create slide Enter /googledrive create slide to create a new Google Slides presentation.
  • /googledrive create sheet Enter /googledrive create sheet to create a new Google Sheets spreadsheet.
  • /googledrive share Enter /googledrive share to share a file from your Google Drive account.

How to disconnect the Chat App to your Google Workspace Account

  1. Sign in to the desktop app.
  2. Click the Chat tab .
  3. At the bottom of the left chat panel, find the Apps section.
  4. Select Google Drive
  5. Enter the slash command /googledrive disconnect
  6. Click on the Disconnect button and the app will be disconnected from your Google Workspace account

How to remove the Google Drive App

  1. Sign into the Zoom App Marketplace with your Zoom account.
  2. In the top right of the page, click Manage.
  3. In the navigation menu, click Added Apps.
  4. Next to the Google Drive app, click Remove.
  5. Confirm the dialogue and click Remove.

Data Security

  • This app has access to the following information on Google Drive:
  • Read permission - See your primary Google account email address and associate you with your personal information on Google
  • Read, write, edit permissions - See, edit, create and delete all of your Google Drive files.
  • This chat app has the following permissions on Zoom:
  • This chat app can send a chat message to an IM channel or Zoom user under the Zoom account.
  • View your user information
  • View current user’s Chat channels
  • Communications between this chat app and Zoom/Google Drive are encrypted:
  • Protocol: TLS 1.2
  • Cipher suite: ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
  • Key length: 128 bits
  • Perfect Forward secrecy: YES
  • This chat app stores access credentials in the local data store:
  • Google Drive API tokens and Zoom OAuth credentials (both user-level only) are stored in an encrypted database.

Creating folders for Zoom Chat

Category: Product features > User features

How to create folders in Zoom Chat

After creating your first folder, new folders can be created from any chat or channel.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Zoom Web App
  • Android | iOS

  1. At the top left of the chat or channel window, click the button.

  2. Click Create a Folder.

  3. In the Folder Name section, provide a name for this folder.

  4. In the Add Contacts, Chats, or Channels section, recent chats and channels are shown by default or you can begin typing names of specific contacts, group chats, and channels you want to include in this folder. Note: This can be adjusted after you finish creating the folder.

  5. Click Create Folder. The new folder will appear on the left panel above the Starred section and is easily distinguished by the folder icon. Clicking on the folder icon or name will open the folder, listing the contained chats and channels.

  6. At the top left of the chat or channel window, click the button.

  7. Click Create a Folder.

  8. In the Folder Name section, provide a name for this folder.

  9. In the Add Contacts, Chats, or Channels section, recent chats and channels are shown by default or you can begin typing names of specific contacts, group chats, and channels you want to include in this folder. Note: This can be adjusted after you finish creating the folder.

  10. Click Create Folder. The new folder will appear on the left panel above the Starred section and is easily distinguished by the folder icon. Clicking on the folder icon or name will open the folder, listing the contained chats and channels.

  11. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  12. Tap the Chat tab .

  13. Just below the Starred section, tap the Folders option.

  14. In the top-right corner, tap the button.

  15. Provide a name for this folder and tap Next.

  16. Add contacts and channels you want included in this new folder. Recent chats and channels are shown by default or you can begin typing names of specific contacts, group chats, and channels you want to include in this folder. Note: This can be adjusted after you finish creating the folder.

  17. Tap Create.

Account

To enable or disable audio or video messages for a group of users:

How to send voice or video messages in Chat

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
Send a voice message
  1. Below the chat box, click the Audio button. Zoom will open the audio recorder.
  2. Click the recording button to begin recording audio. Your default microphone is used to record an audio message up to 60 seconds long.
  3. Click the stop button to end the recording.
  4. Click the play button to listen to your recording, then click the send button to send the audio message. The message will be sent to the chat or channel and can be listened to, reacted to, replied to, and pinned.
Send a video message
  1. Below the chat box, click the Video button. Zoom will open the video recorder.
  2. (Optional) Click the virtual background button to adjust the background or touch-up appearance options for your video message. Note: This requires a device that supports virtual background. By default, your meeting virtual background choice is used for video messages.
  3. Click the Record button to begin recording audio and video. Your default microphone and camera are used to record a video message up to 3 minutes long.
  4. Click the stop button to end the recording.
  5. In the middle of the video preview, click the play button to view to your recording
  6. Click Retake to record a replacement video, or click the Send button to send the video message. The video message will be sent to the chat or channel and can be viewed, reacted to, replied to, and pinned.

Note: Sending a video message is currently only supported on Windows and macOS.

Send a voice message
  1. To the right of the chat box, tap the mic icon . Zoom will open the audio recorder.
  2. Tap the Start button to begin recording audio. Your default microphone is used to record an audio message up to 60 seconds long.
  3. Tap the stop button to end the recording.
  4. Tap the play button to listen to your recording, or tap X Cancel to discard the audio recording.
  5. Tap the Send button to send the audio message. The message will be sent to the chat or channel and can be listened to, reacted to, replied to, and pinned.
Send a video message
  1. To the left of the chat box, tap the more icon .
  2. Tap the Record Video button. Zoom will open the video recorder. You can record your video message in portrait or landscape mode.
  3. (Optional) Tap the virtual background button to adjust the background or touch-up appearance options for your video message. Note: This requires a device that supports virtual background. By default, your meeting virtual background choice is used for video messages.
  4. Tap the record button to begin recording audio and video. Your default microphone and camera are used to record a video message up to 3 minutes long.
  5. Tap the stop button to end the recording.
  6. In the middle of the video preview, tap the play button to view to your recording
  7. Tap Retake to record a replacement video, or tap the send button to send the video message. The video message will be sent to the chat or channel and can be viewed, reacted to, replied to, and pinned.

Category: Product features > User features

How to send a video in Zoom Chat

  • Windows | macOS

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  1. Browse the file system and select the file you want to send. When the file is uploading, click Cancel or X to cancel the upload.
  2. (Optional) Enter any text to accompany the file.
  3. Press Enter to send.

Once the video is uploaded, it is available to those you sent the video. Click the play button to begin downloading the video, and, when complete, the video will begin playing. Standard video controls are available, such as:

  • Play / Pause : Start or pause the playback of the video.
  • Elapsed time/total video length: Shows the current elapsed time of video playback, and the total length of the video file.
  • Playback slider : Allows you to skip to other points of the video playback range.
  • Volume : Allows you to adjust the volume of the video being shared.
  • Expand : Makes the video fill more of the desktop app.
  • Fullscreen : Allows you to make the video full-screen.
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap the Chat tab .

  7. The video will appear in the chat window. Tap the video preview to download and begin playback.

Once the video is uploaded, it is available to those you sent the video. Tap the play button to begin downloading the video, and, when complete, the video will begin playing. Standard video controls are available, such as:

  • Play / Pause : Start or pause the playback of the video.
  • Elapsed time/total video length: Shows the current elapsed time of video playback, and the total length of the video file.
  • Playback slider : Allows you to skip to other points of the video playback range.

Tap the ellipsis button to view other options, such as Open with Other App, which allows the video to be opened in another available app on the device.

Effect of Zoom Chat settings on inter-account communications

Category: Security and compliance > Encryption

Zoom cloud storage retention

Chat cloud storage retention policies are applied to 1:1 chats, group chats, channels. While 1:1 chats use the shortest chat retention period between both users, group chats and channels use the chat retention period of the owner of that group chat or channel.

Below are a few examples of how chat retention periods are handled based on the chat interactions of 2 accounts, with Account A having a retention period of 2 years and Account B having a retention period of 5 years.

[TABLE]

Note: Chats that contain free and paid users can also affect cloud storage retention. Learn more about how these scenarios can affect cloud storage retention.

File sharing

Both users must have file sharing enabled by their account owner/admins to send or receive files in chats and channels. If their settings conflict, the following logic applies.

Account A Account B
File sharing setting Enabled and all file types allowed Disabled
Users can send files to internal or external users Yes No
Users can receive files from internal or external users Yes No

Note: If enabling file sharing, admins can restrict the allowed file types that users can send.

Advanced chat encryption (ACE)

While Chat messages in-transit between users and the Zoom Cloud are encrypted by default using TLS, advanced chat encryption (ACE) facilitates more secure Zoom Chat messaging between Zoom users. This setting requires a paid Zoom account and can be enabled by an account admin. When ACE is enabled, among other chat feature limitations, chat messages subject to the advanced chat encryption are not available for archiving, review in the Chat History Report, or recovery in the event of device loss. In general, this applies to all members of an ACE-enabled account. However, any 1:1 chats, group chats, or chat channels started by a user with ACE enabled will use ACE for all messages, including by external users without ACE enabled.

The following table outlines how ACE operates between two accounts with different settings. As a reminder, you can send chat messages to 3 different recipient groups: a single contact directly (1:1 chats), a group (group chats), or an established chat channel (channels).

Note: 1:1 chats behave differently than group chats and channels with respect to advanced chat encryption.

Messages from ACE enabled user Messages from Non-ACE enabled user
1-on-1 chats started by ACE enabled user Encrypted with ACE Encrypted with ACE
1-on-1 chats started by non-ACE enabled user Encrypted with ACE Encrypted with ACE
Group chat/channel started by ACE enabled user Encrypted with ACE Encrypted with ACE
Group chat/channel started by non-ACE enabled user Encrypted with ACE Not encrypted with ACE

Chat Etiquette Tool

Chat etiquette policies only apply to the users on the account where the policy is enabled. Polices do not apply to the external users.

** Account A ** ** Account B **
Chat etiquette policy(ies) Enabled Disabled
User’s messages can trigger chat etiquette policies from account A Yes No

Configuring the Zoom Calendar Client

Category: Getting started and setting up > User guide

How to perform initial Zoom Calendar setup

Zoom Calendar can connect with your existing Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) calendar service, or with the Zoom Calendar Service directly.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
Connect your Google account with the Zoom Calendar Client
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Meetings tab. If you have never configured your Zoom account for email or calendar access, you will be prompted to do so.
  3. Click the Sign in with Google to allow access to your Google account. Your Zoom Profile page will open in your default browser and open your Calendar and Contacts Integration permissions.
  4. Change the permissions for the service, ensuring to include both Read and Write permissions for Calendar. You can also authorize Zoom read and write permissions for your email, which allows you to access your emails through the Zoom Mail Client.
  5. Select Google as the service you want to connect with.
  6. Click Next You will be directed to Google’s sign-in page.
  7. Sign in to your Google account and then click Allow to let Zoom access your calendar (and email if chosen). After allowing access, you will be redirected back to the Zoom Calendar Client to view your calendar.
Connect your Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account with the Zoom Calendar Client
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Meetings tab.
  3. If you have never configured your Zoom account for email or calendar access, you will be prompted to do so.
  4. Click the Sign in with Microsoft to allow access to your Office 365 account. Your Zoom Profile page will open in your default browser and open your Calendar and Contacts Integration permissions.
  5. Change the permissions for the service, ensuring to include both Read and Write permissions for Calendar. You can also authorize Zoom read and write permissions for your email, which allows you to access your calendar through the Zoom Mail Client.
  6. Select Office 365 as the service you want to connect with.
  7. Click Next You will be directed to the Office 365 sign-in page.
  8. Sign in to your Office 365 account.
  9. Ensure the Authorize with OAuth 2.0 option is checked and then click Allow to let Zoom access your calendar (and email if chosen). After allowing access, you will be redirected back to the Zoom Calendar Client to view your calendar.
Connect your Zoom Mail account with the Zoom Calendar Client

Connecting with the Zoom Mail and Calendar Services requires a Zoom Workplace Pro, Zoom Workplace Business, or Zoom Workplace Enterprise account and these services to be enabled for use by an admin.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Calendar tab. If you have never configured your Zoom account for email or calendar access, you will be prompted to do so.
  3. Click Connect Zoom Calendar.
  4. If you already have a Zoom Mail email address, enter it and click Login. Otherwise, click Create an Account.
  5. Enter your desired Zoom Mail email address and click Create Account. If the provided email address is already taken or not allowed, you will be prompted to enter a different email address.
  6. Click the Create Zoom Mail.

The Zoom mobile app currently supports the Zoom and Google calendar services, but does not currently support connecting to Microsoft 365 (Exchange) calendar services. While the Zoom mobile app can view and manage your calendar, the initial setup of Zoom Mail and Calendar Services must be done through the desktop app.

Connect your Google account with the Zoom Calendar Client
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap the More tab.
  3. Tap Calendar .
  4. Review the introduction to Zoom Calendar and tap Get Started.
  5. Tap the Sign in with Google to allow access to your Google account. Your Zoom Profile page will open in your default browser and open your Calendar and Contacts Integration permissions.
  6. Change the permissions for the service, ensuring to include both Read and Write permissions for Calendar. You can also authorize Zoom read and write permissions for your email, which allows you to access your emails through the Zoom Mail Client.
  7. Select Google as the service you want to connect with.
  8. Tap Next You will be directed to Google’s sign-in page.
  9. Sign in to your Google account and then tap Continue to let Zoom access your calendar (and email if chosen). After allowing access, you will be redirected back to the Zoom Calendar Client to view your calendar.

  5. Click Next to continue.
  6. Enter your desired Zoom Mail Service email address and click Create Account. If the provided email address is already taken or not allowed, you will be prompted to try a different email address. If accepted, your new Zoom Mail inbox will be loaded.

The Zoom mobile app currently supports Zoom, Google Mail services, and Microsoft 365 (Exchange) mail services. While the Zoom mobile app can view and manage your emails, the initial setup of Zoom Mail and Calendar Services must be done through the desktop app.

Connect your Google account with the Zoom Mail Client
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap Mail .
  3. Review the introduction to Zoom Mail and tap Get Started.
  4. Tap the Sign in with Google to allow access to your Google account. Your Zoom Profile page will open in your default browser and open your Calendar and Contacts Integration permissions.
  5. Change the permissions for the service, ensuring to include both Read and Write permissions for Mail. You can also authorize Zoom read and write permissions for your calendar, which allows you to access your calendar events through the Zoom Calendar Client.
  6. Select Google as the service you want to connect with.
  7. Tap Next You will be directed to Google’s sign-in page.
  8. Sign in to your Google account and then tap Continue to let Zoom access your email (and calendar if chosen). After allowing access, you will be redirected back to the Zoom Mail Client to view your calendar.

How to add another email account

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
Add and connect another email account with the Zoom Mail Client
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Mail tab.
  3. In the top-right corner of the window, click the gear icon .
  4. Add email accounts in the following ways:
  • Add account after clicking the gear icon :
  1. After clicking the gear icon , under Accounts in the menu, click + Add Account.
  2. Follow the prompts to connect your Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account to view and manage your calendar through the Zoom client.
  • Add account through Email Settings:
  1. After clicking the gear icon , in the menu, click Email Preferences .
  2. Under Email Settings, click Accounts .
  3. On the Accounts page, click + Add Account.
  4. Follow the prompts to connect your Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account to view and manage your calendar through the Zoom client.
Add another email account that you want to send mail from

You can add an email account to your account. You can send emails with the added account without switching accounts by using the Google Send mail as feature.

You must add another email account to your Gmail account that is connected to the Zoom Mail client so that you can view and select the added account in the Zoom client.

Add and connect another email account with the Zoom Mail Client
  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap Mail .
  3. Tap the menu icon .
  4. In the menu, under Accounts, tap + Add Account.
  5. Follow the prompts to connect your Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account to view and manage your calendar through the Zoom client.

How to select an outgoing email account

Users can add an email account to their own account. They can send emails with the added account without switching accounts by using the Send mail as feature.

  • Windows | macOS
  1. Add another email account to your Gmail account that is connected with the Zoom Mail client.
  2. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  3. Click the Mail tab .
  4. Create a new email or respond to an email.
  5. In the email compose window, click the From line. A dropdown menu will appear.
  6. View the added account and select the account to send email from.

Getting started with Zoom Mail and Calendar as a user

Category: Getting started and setting up > User guide

How to perform initial setup of Zoom Mail and Calendar

Connect Zoom Mail with your account

The Zoom Mail Client allows you to view and manage your emails directly from the Zoom desktop app, further centralizing all your meeting, phone, chat, whiteboard, and email needs in one application. After connecting your existing Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account, you can view and send emails through the Zoom client. You can also create a new email address through the Zoom Mail Service if you would prefer not to use either of those 3rd-party services.

You can also connect your Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account to view and manage your calendar through the Zoom client.

Learn more about configuring the Zoom Mail client initial setup and using Zoom Mail.

Sign in and activate your Zoom mailbox
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Mail tab . If you have never configured your Zoom account for email or calendar access, you will be prompted to do so.
  3. Click Accept to agree to the Terms of Service. This will prompt a screen to appear where you can select your mail service. Note: This is a one-time action, as the desktop app will remember your choice moving forward.
  4. Once you’ve made your selection, click Connect Zoom Mail. Your device will generate encryption keys for secure email sending. Note: Advanced encryption will be enabled for your emails. Only the device you used to sign in will have access to new encrypted emails. Learn more about Zoom Mail Service Encryption and Limitations.
  5. Review the Devices and Activity pop-up window, then click Save to approve the devices. A backup key will be automatically generated. Note: Ensure that you keep a copy for safekeeping. This backup key will be necessary in case the key file becomes broken or goes missing for any reason.
  6. Click Next.
  7. Review the Zoom Mail onboarding text, then click Get Started.
Connect Zoom Calendar with your account

The Zoom Calendar Client allows you to view and manage your calendar directly from the Zoom desktop app, further centralizing all your meeting, phone, chat, whiteboard, and calendar needs in one application. After connecting your existing Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account, you can view and create calendar events through the Zoom client, add a Zoom Meeting and invite details to the event, and invite others. If eligible, you can also create a new calendar through the Zoom Calendar Service if you would rather not use either of those third-party services.

You can also connect your Google or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account to view and manage your email through the Zoom client.

Learn more about configuring the Zoom Calendar Client and using Zoom Calendar.

How to change your temporary password

When hosts add you to their account and create a temporary password, you can change your password in the Zoom web portal.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal, using the temporary password that was generated for you. When you first sign in to the Zoom web portal, an Update Password page will appear. You will be required to update your password.
  2. Enter a new password, then click Update. Note: The new password cannot match the previous one. Your password will be updated for your Zoom account.

How to set delegates for Zoom Mail

Zoom Mail users can assign delegate mail access to other Zoom Mail users on their account, allowing them to view, reply, and compose emails on behalf of the user. Delegating users can also enable settings to include the delegate’s email on outgoing email (Sent by…) and keep emails marked as unread, even if the delegate has opened them. Additionally, users assigning delegated access will automatically have the encryption key change notification enabled for each delegated user.

Learn more about delegating access for Zoom Mail.

How to back up emails in Microsoft Outlook

You can export emails to .pst files to store them for importing later. The messages in the .pst file are the same as other messages. You can forward, reply, or search through the stored messages.

Learn more about backing up emails in Microsoft Outlook.

Import Emails via IMAP

Note: Users must import their email, as this functionality is not admin-automated.

  1. Sign in to Zoom Email on the web.
  2. At the bottom left, click the settings icon .
  3. Click Accounts to see your already configured accounts.
  4. Click … on the mailbox you would like to import.
  5. Select Import via IMAP.
  6. Enter your email credentials and click Start Import to begin the email migration.

Managing calendar client settings

Category: Getting started and setting up > User guide

How to access calendars and subscriptions in Zoom Calendar

  • Windows | macOS
Access Zoom Calendar settings
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop client.
  2. Click the Calendar tab .
  3. In the top-right corner of the window, click the gear icon and then click Calendar Settings .
Manage Accounts settings
  1. Access Zoom Calendar settings.
  2. In the Calendar Settings navigation menu, click Accounts .
  3. Under Linked Accounts, link any third-party email address to easily switch between inboxes.
  • To add and link an account:
  1. Click + Add Account to add a third-party account. Note: You can only add and/or manage one third-party account.
  2. Follow the prompts to connect your account with Zoom Calendar.
  • To remove an account:
  1. To the right of the account you want to remove, click Remove Account. You will be directed to the Zoom web portal.
  2. Under Others, in the Calendar and Contacts Integration section, click Delete next to the account you want to remove. A confirmation window will appear.
  3. In the window, click Delete.
Manage General settings
  1. Access Zoom Calendar settings.
  2. In the Calendar Settings navigation menu, click General .** Note: You can control General** settings for Google and Microsoft in the Zoom client.
  • Date Format: Choose how you want dates to be formatted.
  • Time Format: Choose how you want times to be formatted.
  • Start Week on: Choose how you want your week to start. Note: This feature adheres to the operating system’s settings.
  • View options: Select the Show declined events checkbox to display all your declined meetings on your calendar. Deselect the Show declined events checkbox to hide all your declined meetings on your calendar. Note: This option currently only supports Google and Zoom calendars.
  • Time zone: Choose your timezone, add a secondary timezone, and customize the name of each time zone. When you add a secondary timezone, you can see two time zones side by side when you collaborate with a colleague from a different time zone. You can also enable or disable the second time zone when you schedule meetings with colleagues in the same time zone.
  • To add a secondary timezone:
  1. Click Add Secondary Timezone.
  2. Click the time zone dropdown to select the secondary time zone.
  3. (Optional) Enter a label for the time zones.
  4. (Optional) To the right of the timezone you want to remove, click X.
Managing Scheduling settings
  1. Access Zoom Calendar settings.
  2. In the Calendar Settings navigation menu, click Scheduling.
  3. Configure the following settings:
  • Default Event Duration: Set the default length of time for a new event.
  • Allow Invitees to: Choose which permissions event invitees have for the event they are invited to.
  • Modify the event: Invitees can edit the event details, such as title, date/time, duration, and more.
  • Invite others: Invitees can invite additional guests.
  • See list of invitees: Invitees can see the full list of other invitees.
Manage Import settings
  1. Access Zoom Calendar settings.
  2. In the Calendar Settings navigation menu, click Import.
  3. Under Import an ICS file, complete the following actions:
  • To the right of Import to, click the dropdown and select the calendar to which you want to import the calendar events.
  • Click Select .ics file… and select an ICS file to import calendar events.
  1. Click Import.
Manage Your Calendars settings

Under Your Calendars, all calendars created by this account are displayed.

Create a calendar
  1. Access Zoom Calendar settings.
  2. In the Calendar Settings navigation menu, under Your Calendars, click + Create to create a calendar.
  3. Enter the Calendar Name.
  4. (Optional) Under Calendar Description (Optional), enter a description for the calendar.
  5. View the calendar Owner.
  6. Click Create Calendar.
Manage a calendar’s settings
  1. Access Zoom Calendar settings.
  2. In the Calendar Settings navigation menu, under Your Calendars, click a calendar that you want to manage.
  3. Manage the calendar settings:
  • Calendar Name: Enter a calendar name.
  • Calendar Description: Enter a description for your calendar.
  • Permissions: Share your calendars with specific users and assign permissions to each added user. Shared users can view the calendar’s private events.
  1. Click + Add. A pop-up window will appear.
  2. In the window, enter an email address or name of a user you want to share your calendar with.
  3. Click the permissions dropdown and select the permissions that you want to user to have.
  4. Click Add. The user will be added under Permissions.
  5. (Optional) Once a user is added, complete the following actions:
  • To the right of an added user, click the permissions dropdown and change their permissions.
  • To the right of an added user, click the icon to remove them from the calendar.
  1. (Optional) Select the People at your company checkbox, then select the permissions for users in your company to share your calendar.
  2. (Optional) Select the Anyone else checkbox, then select the permissions for external users to share your calendar.
  • Event notifications: Choose how you want to receive notifications for events on this calendar.
  • All-day event notifications: Choose how you want to receive notifications for all-day events on this calendar.
  • Other notifications: Choose how you want to receive email notifications when changes are made to this calendar. Select the checkboxes of the notifications that you want.
Manage Subscription settings

View your calendar’s subscriptions.

  1. Access Zoom Calendar settings.
  2. In the Calendar Settings navigation menu, under Subscriptions, click a subscription that you want to manage.
  3. Manage subscription settings:
  • (Optional) At the top of the page, view the subscription link and copy it.
  • Calendar Name: Enter a calendar name.
  • Calendar Description: If you have permission, enter a description for your calendar.
  • Event notifications: Choose how you want to receive notifications for events on this calendar.
  • All-day event notifications: Choose how you want to receive notifications for all-day events on this calendar.
  • Other notifications: Choose how you want to receive email notifications when changes are made to this calendar. Select the checkboxes of the notifications that you want.
  • (Optional) Click Remove from list if you want to remove this subscription from your calendar.

Using the Zoom Calendar Client

Category: Getting started and setting up > User guide

How to view your calendar events

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
View your calendar

After you’ve connected your Zoom Calendar Client to your Zoom Calendar, Google, or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account, you can access your calendar directly from the Zoom desktop app.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Calendar tab. If you have never configured your Zoom account for email or calendar access, you will be prompted to do so. Otherwise, your calendar will open.
  3. The current calendar view (Day, Work Week, or Week) is displayed in the top-right corner. To the right of the currently displayed date, click the back icon and forward icon to move backward or forward 1 day or week, depending on the current calendar view.
  4. (Optional) Click the today button to return to the current date.
  5. To the left of the currently displayed date, click the more options icon to view additional calendars and the entire month, helping you search other users’ calendars to find a time to meet. The panel contains the following information:
  • Entire calendar month: The current entire month is displayed, with the options to page through to past or future months.
  • Search People bar: Search for contacts and view their calendar events alongside your calendar.
  • Available calendar views: Calendars you already have access to are displayed. Others, such as the calendars of colleagues, can be searched for and added to this list. Click the checkbox next to each calendar to toggle it being displayed.
  1. In the top-right corner of the calendar window, click the Meet Now down arrow icon to use the following actions:
  • View personal meeting ID (PMI): Display your PMI. You can also start a meeting using your PMI.
  • Copy PMI link: Copy your PMI link.
  • Click the Meet Now button: This will start an instant meeting.
  1. In the top-right corner of the calendar window, click the Work Week down arrow icon next to the current calendar view to change one of the following views:
  • Day: Display only one day of calendar events at a time.
  • Work Week: Display only a work week (5 days) of calendar events at a time.
  • Week: Display an entire week’s calendar events at a time.
  1. Click a calendar event to see more details. The calendar window will open and display the following information for that calendar event:
  • Title
  • Date and time
  • Location
  • Occurrence
  • More icon : Click to access additional options for the calendar event:
  • Copy invitation
  • Invite People
  • Message Host
  • Chat with Everyone (if you’re the host)
  • Start Meeting (if you’re the host)
  • Join Meeting
  • Join from a Room
  • Decline & Remove
  • Duplicate (if you’re the host)
  • Edit (if you’re the host)
  • Delete (if you’re the host)
  • Join or Start (if a Zoom Meeting)
  • View Meeting Info: Copy the meeting link.
  • Attachments: Display the files attached to the meeting. Note: To access the files from Zoom Hub, click the Zoom Hub icon .
  • Your current attendance response: Displays your current RSVP to the meeting, such as Yes, No, and Maybe.
  • Invited guests and their attendance response
  • Calendar event description and meeting invitation (if a Zoom Meeting)
  • Customized questions and attendees’ responses
  • Link to the Scheduler’s scheduled event
View declined events

When all attendees have declined a meeting, you will see a warning label on the meeting event in Zoom Calendar. When you hover your mouse over the warning label on the event, the following tooltip will appear: All attendees have declined this event.

Note: The warning label will not appear when only a few attendees have declined the meeting.

After you’ve connected your Zoom Calendar Client to your Zoom Calendar, Google, or Microsoft 365 (Exchange) account, you can begin accessing your calendar directly from the Zoom desktop app.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap Calendar . Note: Versions older than 5.14.0 have the Calendar option behind the More option, rather than being visible on the main row of options. If you have never configured your Zoom account for email or calendar access, you will be prompted to do so. Otherwise, your calendar will open to the current day’s events.
  3. (Optional) Tap another day of the week to view that day’s events, or tap the down arrow below the current week to see the full month’s worth of dates.
  4. Tap on a calendar event to see more details. The following information and options for that calendar event are displayed:
  • How many participants have joined thus far, if any have joined.
  • Title
  • Date and time
  • Location
  • More icon : Click to access additional options for the calendar event:
  • Copy invitation
  • Edit
  • Delete
  • Join from a Room
  • Decline & Remove
  • Join or Start (if a Zoom Meeting)
  • Your current attendance response: Displays your current RSVP to the meeting, such as Yes, No, and Maybe.
  • Invited guests and their attendance response
  • Calendar event description and meeting invitation (if a Zoom Meeting)
  • Customized questions and attendees’ responses

How to create and schedule events

The Zoom Calendar client makes it easy to schedule calendar events, add Zoom meeting or phone conferencing details, and invite contacts to that calendar event.

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS

To quickly create a new calendar event, click New Event at the top of the calendar. Additionally, when creating an event in the main calendar view, you only have to click a time slot once to see the scheduler pop-up window. When you click a time slot twice, the full scheduler page will appear.

To view various dates and compare your calendar with others to find the best time:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Calendar tab .
  3. Once you’ve found a date and time that works for you and potentially others, click and drag on the calendar to create a new event. The calendar window will open to begin drafting your calendar event.
  4. Complete the following details for your calendar event:
  • Event title: Name the calendar event. This will be shown to invitees, as well as used for the Zoom Meeting.
  • (Optional) Click the Time Off toggle to enable or disable it. When enabled, you will appear as “Off” to everyone who can see your calendar, and external users will not be able to book time with you. Note: This option will only appear when your calendar is connected with the Zoom Calendar client.
  • Attendees: Enter the names of others that you want to invite to this event. You can also view their profile card and their contact details. The added attendees will be listed under Attendees.
  • Hover your mouse over an attendee that you want to manage and use the following options:
  • (Optional) Click the next to each name to remove them from the list.
  • Click the hidden icon to make the attendee hidden from the event list. Click the visible icon to make the attendee visible on the event list.
  • Click the optional button to mark the attendee as optional. Their icon will change to the optional icon . Note: Once the meeting is created, optional attendees will receive invitation emails that indicate they are not required to join the meeting.
  • Use Suggested Times. The suggested time automatically recommends available time slots based on all attendees’ availability. Note: This feature is currently only available for Google and Zoom Calendar users.
  1. Invite attendees to your event.
  2. Under the list of added attendees, click Suggested Times. Suggested time slots (up to 7 days) will appear.
  3. Click one of the recommended slots (if available) to finish creating the event.
  • Date and time: Select the date and time of the calendar event. By default, this will use the next hour or half-hour time slot (if clicking the New Event button) or the date/time selected on the calendar.
  • (Optional) Select Find a Time to find available times on guests’ calendars when scheduling meetings.
  • To use Find a Time:
  1. Click an event slot on the calendar. The event window will automatically move to the selected time slot.
  2. Hover over the time slot, then resize the time slot . This will change the event duration (by extending or shortening it).
  3. View the start/end times of the calendar event.
  • (Optional) Select the All Day checkbox. If a meeting is all day, the meeting will be scheduled for 12:00 AM-11:59 PM.
  • (Optional) Click the Repeat dropdown menu to select how often your event will occur.
  • Calendar: Select a calendar service to add the meeting and send out invites to participants.
  • Outlook: Open the Outlook desktop app and create an event for the meeting. Note: You will see Outlook when using the Windows client.
  • iCal: Open iCal and create an event for the meeting. Note: You will see iCal when using a macOS.
  • Google Calendar: Open Google Calendar in your default browser and create an event for the meeting.
  • Other Calendars: Open a new window, where the meeting text can be copied and pasted into the user’s preferred communication method. You can also down an ICS file which can be opened in most email applications.
  • Click the color dropdown and select the color that you want your event to be.
  • Event Type: Select whether this event is Offline, Zoom Meeting, or Zoom Phone Call. Choose to schedule this meeting with added virtual meeting or call details. The following options are provided:
  • Offline: No additional meeting details are added. This is best for in-person meetings and events.
  • Zoom Meeting: The calendar event will be scheduled with a corresponding Zoom Meeting. Your default meeting settings are used.
  • Zoom Phone Call
  • Add a Location or Room: Enter a location or room for this meeting.
  • Add a Description or Attachments: Add some additional context and description for this event, as well as add any relevant attachments invitees need to have before the meeting starts.
  • Visibility: Choose how you want this calendar event to be visible to others viewing your calendar, either Default visibility, Public, or Private.
  • Show Yourself as: Choose how you want your status to be displayed to others during this calendar event, either as Busy or Free.
  • Allow Attendees to: Adjust these calendar event permissions regarding how other invitees can view and adjust the calendar event.
  • Modify the event
  • Invite others
  • See list of attendees
  • Export: Select the checkbox to use an external calendar.
  • More Options: Click this to view more options for scheduling an associated Zoom Meeting, such as security, video, audio, and other advanced options.
  1. Click Save to schedule the meeting. Note: When you make changes to an event and try to close the window without saving, a pop-up message will appear, asking if you want to Discard unsaved changes.

Your scheduled event will appear in the Zoom Calendar client.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.
  2. Tap Calendar . Note: Versions older than 5.14.0 have the Calendar option behind the More option, rather than being visible on the main row of options.
  3. In the top right corner, tap the new event icon .
  4. Enter the following details for your calendar event:
  • Event title: Name the calendar event. This will be shown to invitees, as well as used for the Zoom Meeting.
  • Invitees: Enter the names of others that you want to invite to this event. Click the X next to each name to remove them from the list.
  • Date and time: Select the date and time, time zone, and any recurrence pattern for the calendar event. By default, this will use the next hour or half-hour time slot (if clicking the New Event button) or the date/time selected on the calendar.
  • Calendar: Choose which calendar you want to schedule this for, if you have access to multiple calendars.
  • Location: Click to add a location for this calendar meeting.
  • Description or Attachments: Add some additional context and description for this event, as well as add any relevant attachments invitees need to have before the meeting starts.
  • Conferencing: Choose to schedule this meeting with added virtual meeting or call details. The following options are provided:
  • Offline: No additional meeting details are added. This is best for in-person meetings and events.
  • Zoom Meeting: The calendar event will be scheduled with a corresponding Zoom Meeting. Your default meeting settings are used.
  • Zoom Phone Call
  • Meeting Security (if a Zoom Meeting is enabled as the conferencing option)
  • Require Passcode
  • Passcode
  • Waiting Room
  • Only Allow Authenticated Users
  1. Tap Create to schedule the meeting.

How to duplicate an event

Users can create a duplicate event and add different event details or private information without notifying other attendees.

  • Windows | macOS
  1. Schedule a calendar event.
  2. View your calendar and click the event you want to duplicate. The calendar window will open and display the information for that calendar event.
  3. At the top of the event card, click the More icon, then click Duplicate.
  4. Edit the duplicated event, then click Save.

How to send a reply note or propose a new time

  • Windows | macOS
Send a reply note

This feature is available for Microsoft, Google, and Zoom calendars.

  1. View your calendar.
  2. Click an event you want to RSVP to. The event card will appear.
  3. At the top of the event card, to the right of Going?, click the ellipsis , then click Send Reply Note. A pop-up window will appear.
  4. In the window, select your attendance response.
  5. In the text box, enter a reply note to inform the host why you can or cannot attend the event.
  6. Click Send. Your attendance response and reply note will appear on the event card.
Propose a new time

This feature is only supported for Zoom and Outlook service calendar clients.

Note: This is not available for Google Calendar.

  1. View your calendar.
  2. Click an event for which you want to propose a new time. The event card will appear.
  3. At the top of the event card, to the right of Going?, click the ellipsis , then click Propose New Time.
  4. Under Proposed Time, select the date and time that you want to propose.
  5. (Optional) Under Message (Optional), explain why you are proposing a new time.
  6. Click Propose New Time. Your proposed date and time will appear on the event card.

How to manage Zoom Calendar on the Zoom Workplace app

  • Windows | macOS
Change calendar colors

Zoom and Google Calendar service clients support this feature.

Note: This feature is not supported by Microsoft/Outlook.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Calendar tab .
  3. In the left panel, change colors for the following calendars:
  • My Calendars: Display all calendars created by your account.
  • To change calendar colors:
  1. To the right of your calendar that you want to manage, click the ellipsis , then click Change color.
  2. Select a color. This color change will be visible to all viewers.
  • Subscriptions: View calendars that you are subscribed to.
  • To change calendar colors:
  1. To the right of a subscription calendar that you want to manage, click the ellipsis , then click Change color.
  2. Select a color. This color change will be visible only to you.
Manage calendar client settings

Zoom Calendar settings are located separately from the main client settings. These settings control the defaults used by the calendar client, such as the 12-hour/24-hour clock, date order (Month-Day-Year), event length, and more.

Learn more about managing calendar client settings.

How to manage Zoom Calendar accounts

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
View and switch accounts

When you access Zoom Calendar client settings, you can use the Accounts section to see the email account that you signed in with and view other email provider accounts. You can use the dropdown menu to easily switch between multiple calendars.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Calendar tab.
  3. In the top-right corner of the window, click the gear icon , then view your accounts under the Account section.
  4. Click the calendar account you want to switch to. The calendar of the selected account will be displayed.
Disconnect your calendar account

To sign out of the current calendar account:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Calendar tab.
  3. In the top-right corner of the window, click the gear icon .

Disconnect your calendar account

To sign out of the current calendar account:

  2. Tap Calendar . Note: Versions older than 5.14.0 have the Calendar option behind the More option, rather than being visible on the main row of options.

Using the Zoom Mail client

Category: Getting started and setting up > User guide

How to view emails

  • Windows | macOS
  • Android | iOS
Search for and filter emails

When looking for a specific email or just trying to filter out certain categories of emails, the search and filtering options can help you get to the message you want more quickly. Emails can be searched by a specific sender, subject, or other keyword contained in the email.

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click the Mail tab .
  3. In the top-right corner of the mail window, click the search icon .
  4. Enter your search query into the search bar.
  5. (Optional) Click to use the following search filters:
  • Has Attachment
  • Starred
  • From me
  1. Press the Enter key to search. All emails matching that query will be displayed below.

You can also filter the default view of your inbox to only display specific messages:

  1. Click the filter icon and then select from the following:
  • Unread
  • Starred
  • Important
  • Has Attachment

Emails can be drafted and sent either as a new email or a response to an email you’ve received.

How to manage devices with encryption access and backup encryption keys

When using the Zoom Mail Service, your encryption key is vital to maintaining the privacy of your emails. With this in mind, managing devices that have your encryption key stored locally is important, especially if a device has been lost or stolen.

  • Windows | macOS
  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
  2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings. This will open the settings window
  3. Click the Profile tab .
  4. Click Device Management for Encryption. Note: If this option is not available, you are not currently connected to the Zoom Mail Service. The following options will appear.
  • Activity: View all devices currently with access to your encrypted emails. Select one or more devices listed, and click Remove to revoke their encryption access.
  • Generate Backup Key: Generate a backup key, which can be stored elsewhere for safekeeping and imported on a new device, if you need to regain access to your encrypted emails after losing access to a device.
  • Input Backup Key: Import a previously generated backup key to regain access to your encrypted emails.

How to use Zoom Mail in offline mode

When you are not connected to the internet, you can still access certain emails and perform actions automatically. Offline mode automatically turns on if you are not connected to the internet, and it turns off the minute the internet connection is restored. You can view on your Zoom client whether you are offline or not.

When Zoom Mail is offline, you can do the following actions:

  • Users can access previously loaded emails while offline and select an email to check if it has been synced for offline use.
  • Open emails and attachments when you are offline. In offline mode, you can open emails and attachments that are stored for offline mode (if attachments cannot be opened, they can be downloaded).
  • Write responses or forward stored emails when you’re offline, and have them sent when you’re back online. You can see your emails that will be sent once you’re back online; those emails are distinguished from other sent emails or drafts.
  • Compose emails and compose replies that will be saved to your drafts.
  • Reply to an email thread and have it saved in your drafts.

Notes:

  • If you are not logged into the Zoom client when you do not have an internet connection, you cannot use offline mode on Zoom Mail.
  • If you disable offline mode after having it enabled, all stored data will be deleted.

Information on the last time the fingerprint was changed will appear in the window.

Notes:
