Zoom Whiteboard

Using Whiteboard Content Generation with AI Companion

Category: AI features > Features

How to generate sticky notes using Whiteboard Content Generation

  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. In the left toolbar, click the AI Companion icon . The Whiteboard Content Generation prompt will appear.
  3. Enter a command in the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  4. Right next to the prompt field, expand the drop-down list and select Generate Stickies.
  5. Click the send icon . Your generated content will appear.
  6. (Optional) Click Refine Results to narrow down your search criteria, apply filters, and obtain more precise and relevant information. You can enter a more detailed command into the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  7. (Optional) Click Add More to add more relevant content in sticky notes.
  8. (Optional) Click the close icon to cancel the sticky notes generation.
  9. When you are satisfied with the generated content, click the checkmark icon .

How to generate a table using Whiteboard Content Generation

  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. In the left toolbar, click the AI Companion icon . The Whiteboard Content Generation prompt will appear.
  3. Enter a command in the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  4. Right next to the prompt field, expand the drop-down list and select Generate Table.
  5. Click the send icon . Your generated content will appear. A notification bar will also appear on the right.
  6. Click Preview.
  7. (Optional) Click Refine Results to narrow down your search criteria, apply filters, and obtain more precise and relevant information. You can enter a more detailed command into the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  8. (Optional) Format the table using the following options:
  • Click Fill to complete or populate a table with relevant data or information. .
  • Click Add row to insert a new row into the table.
  • Click Add column insert a new column into the table.
  1. (Optional) Click the close icon to cancel the table content generation.
  2. When you are satisfied with the generated content, click the checkmark icon .

How to generate texts using Whiteboard Content Generation

  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. In the left toolbar, click the AI Companion icon . The Whiteboard Content Generation prompt will appear.
  3. Enter a command in the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  4. Right next to the prompt field, expand the drop-down list and select Generate Text.
  5. Click the send icon .
  6. (Optional) Click Refine Results to narrow down your search criteria, apply filters, and obtain more precise and relevant information. You can enter a more detailed command into the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  7. (Optional) Expand the Length drop-down menu to adjust the length of your generated text. You have the option to shorten or lengthen the text, summarize in a single sentence, or rewrite it in bullet points.
  8. (Optional) Expand the Tone drop-down menu to change the tone of your generated text. You can choose from Professional, Casual, Formal or Forceful.
  9. (Optional) Click the close icon to cancel the text generation.
  10. When you are satisfied with the generated content, click the checkmark icon .

How to generate Mindmap using Whiteboard Content Generation

  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. In the left toolbar, click the AI Companion icon . The Whiteboard Content Generation prompt will appear.
  3. Enter a command in the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  4. Right next to the prompt field, expand the drop-down list and select Generate Mindmap.
  5. Click the send icon .
  6. (Optional) Click Refine Results to narrow down your search criteria, apply filters, and obtain more precise and relevant information. You can enter a more detailed command into the prompt field or select from the list of suggested ideas.
  7. (Optional) Click Simplify to generate a simpler flowchart.
  8. (Optional) Click Expand to generate a more complex flowchart.
  9. (Optional) Click the close icon to cancel the Mindmap generation.
  10. When you are satisfied with the generated content, click the checkmark icon .

How to edit existing whiteboard content using Whiteboard Content Generation

Organize sticky notes
  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. Select one or multiple sticky notes that you want to organize using Whiteboard Content Generation. A pop-up menu will appear.
  3. Click the AI Companion icon .
  4. Select an option that allows you to enhance the selected content.
  • If you select a single sticky note, you can create additional similar stickies.
  • If you choose multiple sticky notes, you have the option to create similar stickies or identify and group related ones together for better organization and management.
Format table
  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. Select the table that you want to format using Whiteboard Content Generation. A pop-up menu will appear.
  3. Click the AI Companion icon .
  4. Format the table using the following options:
  • Fill: Allows you to populate the cells of a table with data or content.
  • Add row: Allows you to insert a new row into a table.
  • Add column: Allows you to insert a new column into a table.
Edit text
  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. Select the text that you want to edit using Whiteboard Content Generation. A pop-up menu will appear.
  3. Click the AI Companion icon .
  4. Edit the text using the following options:
  • Length: Allows you to shorten or lengthen the text, summarize in a single sentence, or rewrite it in bullet points.
  • Tone: Allows you to modify the tone of the text to match your preference, selecting from options such as Professional, Casual, Formal, or Forceful.

Enabling or disabling Whiteboard content generation with AI Companion

Category: AI features > Settings

How to enable or disable Whiteboard content generation with AI Companion

Account

To enable or disable Whiteboard Content Generation for all users in the account:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin with the privilege to edit account settings.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Account Management then Account Settings.
  3. Click the AI Companion tab.
  4. Under Whiteboard, click the Whiteboard content generation with AI Companion toggle to enable or disable it.
  5. If a verification dialog displays, click Enable or Disable to verify the change.
  6. (Optional) To prevent all users in your account from changing this setting, click the lock icon , and then click Lock to confirm the setting.
Group

To enable or disable Whiteboard Content Generation for a group of users:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal as an admin with the privilege to edit groups.
  2. In the navigation menu, click User Management then Groups.
  3. Click the applicable group name from the list.
  4. Click the AI Companion tab.
  5. Under Whiteboard, click the Whiteboard content generation with AI Companion toggle to enable or disable it.
  6. If a verification dialog displays, click Enable or Disable to verify the change. Note: If the option is grayed out, it has been locked at the account level and needs to be changed at that level.
  7. (Optional) To prevent all users in the group from changing this setting, click the lock icon , and then click Lock to confirm the setting.
User

To enable or disable Whiteboard Content Generation for your own use:

  1. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.
  2. In the navigation menu, click Settings.
  3. Click the AI Companion tab.
  4. Under Whiteboard, click the Whiteboard content generation with AI Companion toggle to enable or disable it.
  5. If a verification dialog displays, click Enable or Disable to verify the change. Note: If the option is grayed out, it has been locked at either the group or account level. You need to contact your Zoom admin.

Getting started with Zoom Whiteboard

Category: Getting started and setting up

How to create a whiteboard

  • Zoom meeting or webinar
  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Android | iOS
  • Web
  • Zoom Web App
  • Zoom Hub

  1. Start a meeting or webinar from the Zoom desktop app.

  2. On the in-meeting controls, click the Whiteboards button .

  3. Click New Whiteboard. The whiteboard will open in the meeting window.

  4. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  5. At the left navigation menu, click the Whiteboards button . Note: If you don’t see the Whiteboards option, click More then select Whiteboards from the list.

  6. At the top right, click New whiteboard to create a new whiteboard.

  7. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  8. At the bottom of the screen, tap More then tap Whiteboards .

  9. At the top, tap New whiteboard to create a new whiteboard.

  10. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.

  11. On the left navigation menu, click Whiteboards.

  12. At the top right, click New whiteboard to create a new whiteboard.

  13. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.

  14. Click the Whiteboards button . Note: If you don’t see the Whiteboards option, click More then select Whiteboards from the list.

  15. At the top right, click New whiteboard to create a new whiteboard.

Learn about how to create whiteboards and other assets in Zoom Hub.

How to use the whiteboard tools

To edit a whiteboard, use the editing tools available located on the left side of the screen. Click and drag the icons to the canvas to draw, add shapes, type text, and more. For most controls, clicking on the canvas will then create an object of that type. Learn more about using the Zoom Whiteboard.

How to customize the display name of a whiteboard

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. At the top left of the whiteboard page, click the whiteboard title to rename it. The new display name will take effect immediately.

Note: To edit the name of a whiteboard, you need to have editor access.

How to share a whiteboard

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. At the top right of the whiteboard page, click Share.
  3. Enter the email addresses of the users you would like to share the whiteboard with and set their permissions.
  4. Click Share Whiteboard.
  5. (Optional) Click Copy link and then paste the link in a message or email to send to others.

Learn more about sharing a whiteboard inside and out of Zoom meetings. You can also share a whiteboard directly from Zoom Hub.

How to delete a whiteboard

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. At the top left of the whiteboard page, click the More icon .
  3. Click Whiteboard then Move to trash.
  4. In the verification dialog, click Move to trash to delete the whiteboard.

Learn more about deleting and recovering a whiteboard.

How to use AI Companion in whiteboard

AI Companion can help you brainstorm, create visuals, and organize content into a board that’s easier to read and act on. Learn more about using Whiteboard Content Generation with AI Companion.

How to use whiteboard shortcuts

Zoom Whiteboard shortcuts can save time and improve your productivity when using the platform. Knowing the most common shortcuts can make navigating the whiteboard easier and help you stay focused on the content. Learn more about using keyboard and mouse shortcuts with Whiteboard.

Adding a page to the whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to add a page to the whiteboard

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. At the top-left corner of the whiteboard, click the Page icon . The Pages panel will appear.
  3. At the bottom of the Pages panel, click Add Page. The Page icon will display the total number of pages on the whiteboard.

Note: You can add up to 12 pages to your whiteboard.

How to manage a whiteboard page

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. At the top-left corner of the whiteboard, click the Page icon . The Pages panel will appear.
  3. Select a page you want to manage.
  4. Click the ellipsis icon to perform the following actions:
  • Rename: Enter a display name for the page.
  • Copy: Create a duplicate of the selected page that you can paste later.
  • Paste: Paste a previously copied or cut page to the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Create a new page that is an exact copy of the selected page.
  • Export: Export page as a PDF file, PNG image, and CSV file.
  • Background color: Change the canvas background color for everyone on the whiteboard.
  • Delete page contents: Remove all content on the selected page while keeping the page itself.
  • Delete: Remove the selected page entirely from the whiteboard.
  1. (Optional) To change the sequence of your pages, click on a page and move it up or down by dragging it vertically.

Adding table to the whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to insert a table on whiteboard

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.

  2. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the More Tools icon .

  3. Select Table.

  4. Use the scroll bar to view all the table templates and then select the type of table you want to use.

Your cursor will change into a table icon .

  1. Click anywhere on canvas to insert the selected table.

How to manage a table in whiteboard

Table placement will be on the back layer of the whiteboard. You can perform the following actions on tables:

Move table

Hover your cursor anywhere around the table until it changes to a pointing hand. Drag the table anywhere on canvas to move it.

Alternatively, you can hover your cursor to the upper left corner of the table until the four-arrow icon appears. Click and drag the table anywhere on canvas to move it.

Resize table and cells
  • How to resize the entire table: Hover your cursor anywhere around the table and then click to select it. Click and drag the corner of the object to adjust its size.
  • How to resize the cell: Click and drag the arrow in the corner of the cell to resize it. You can resize the cell vertically or horizontally.
Enter and format text

  1. To enter text, click (or tap on a Touch device) in a cell.

  2. Enter your text.

Text entered into the header row will default to Bold font. Text in all other rows will default to Regular font.

  1. To edit text, select the Text Format icon . The Format bar will display.

  2. Use the options to format your text.

Manage rows
  • How to add a row: Select the table and then click the Add Row icon in the context menu. The new row will be added to the bottom of the table.
  • How to move a row: Hover over the left side of the table to move a row. The Move row icon displays on each row. Click (or tap on a touch device) and move the Move row icon up or down to place the row to the desired location.
  • How to resize a row: Click (or tap on a touch device) on the row line. Drag the line up or down to resize the row.
Manage columns
  • How to add a column: Select the table and then click the Add Column icon in the context menu. The new column will be added to the right of the table.
  • How to move a column: Hover over the top of the table to move columns. The Move column icon displays on each column. Click (or tap on a Touch device) and drag the Move column icon to place the column to the desired location.
  • How to resize a column: Click (or tap on a Touch device) on the column line. The resize arrow will display. Drag the line horizontally to resize the column.
Lock table
  • Click the lock icon to prevent users with edit access from accidentally modifying objects and group of objects on the canvas.
  • Click the unlock icon to allow changes to objects and group of objects on the canvas.
Add colors
  • How to adjust the fill of the table: Select the table and then click the Fill icon in the context menu. Pick a desired fill transparency and color.
  • How to adjust the border color: Select the table and then click the Outline icon in the context menu. Pick a desired color for your border.
  • How to adjust the text color: Select a cell, row/column, or the entire table. Click the Text Format icon and then expand the Text Color. Pick a desired color for your text.
More menu
  • Select the table and then click the ellipses icon in the context menu.

You can do the following actions:

  • Copy: Copy the selected table.

  • Copy as image: Copy the table as an image which can then be shared or pasted into applications that support images.

  • Paste: Place the copied table somewhere else on the whiteboard.

  • Duplicate: Make an exact copy of the selected table.

  • Copy Link to Object: Copy the hyperlink or URL of a selected table which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.

  • Export: Export data from selected table as a PDF, PNG or CSV file.

  • Save as Template: Save the selected table as a template.

  • Info: Show the creator and last editor of the selected table.

  • Lock: Lock table to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the content.

  • Delete: Remove the selected table.

  • Select a cell and then click the ellipses icon in the menu. You can do the following actions:

  • Copy: Copy the selected cell.

  • Paste: Place the copied cell somewhere else on the whiteboard.

  • Insert Row Below: Add a new row below the currently selected cell.

  • Insert Row Above: Add a new row above the currently selected cell.

  • Insert Column Right: Add a new column to the right of the currently selected cell.

  • Insert Column Left: Add a new column to the left of the currently selected cell.

  • Move Row Down: Move the selected row downwards in a table.

  • Move Row Up: Move the selected row upwards in a table.

  • Move Column Right: Move the selected column to the right in a table.

  • Move Column Left: Move the selected column to the left in a table.

  • Delete Row: Remove the selected row from a table.

  • Delete Column: Remove the selected column from a table.

Note: Adding shapes to tables is not supported at this time.

Adding Zoom Cards to the whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to insert a Zoom Card into a whiteboard

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the More Tools icon .

  4. Click New Zoom Card. Your cursor will change into a card icon .

How to edit a Zoom Card

  1. Add a Zoom Card to your whiteboard.

  • Assignee icon : Search for contact or email of people within your organization, or external members who have access to the whiteboard.
  • Calendar icon : Pick a due date for the task.
  • Status icon : Display the task’s status (To do, Blocked, In progress, Done).
  • Color icon : Group similar cards visually.
  • Lock icon : Lock cards to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the whiteboard content.
  1. Click the ellipsis icon to see more options.
  • Copy: Copy the selected card.
  • Copy as image: Copy the selected card as an image which can then be shared or pasted into applications that support images.
  • Paste: Place the copied card somewhere else on the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Make an exact copy of the selected card.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copy the hyperlink or URL of a selected card which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Convert to Jira Card: Convert a Zoom Card into a Jira Card.
  • Convert to Azure Card: Convert a Zoom Card into an Azure Card.
  • Bring Forward: Move the selected card up one layer.

  • Add Comment: Add comments directly to the card.
  • Save as Template: Save the selected card as a template.
  • Info: Show the creator and last editor of the selected card.
  • Lock: Lock cards to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the content.
  • Delete: Delete the selected card.

How to connect Zoom Card to objects

  1. Add a Zoom Card to your whiteboard.
  2. Click the card with the Select tool.
  3. Click and drag one of the small dots outside the card’s box. As you drag, your cursor and arrow will be drawn.
  4. Drag the arrow to another object to create the connector.

Adding, deleting, and resolving comments in Zoom Whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to add, delete and resolve comments in Zoom Whiteboard

Add a comment

Whiteboard owners and users with co-owner, editor, or commenter access can add a comment on a whiteboard.

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the comment icon . Alternatively, you can right-click on the canvas and select Add Comment from the options, or type C when nothing is selected on the canvas. Your cursor will change to a plus comment icon as you place it on the canvas.
  3. Click anywhere on the canvas where you want to post your comment.
  4. Enter your comment and then click the Comment button. Note: You can mention a whiteboard user in the comment using the @mention format. You will be asked to grant access if the person you mention does not have access.
  5. (Optional) To edit a comment, click the ellipses icon then Edit. Once you leave a comment, collaborators can add a reply to your comment. You can hover over the comment icon to preview the comments.
  6. To reply to your own comment or someone else’s, enter a message in the Add your reply or @ someone box.
  7. Click the Reply button when you are finished.
Delete a comment

Whiteboard owners or authors of the comment can delete comments on a whiteboard.

  1. Open an existing whiteboard.
  2. At the top right, click the comment icon to open the comment panel. You will see all the comments across all pages. However, you can filter the comments by page using the filter icon .
  3. To the right of the comment you wish to remove, click the ellipses icon then select Delete.
Resolve a comment

Whiteboard owners can resolve comments on a whiteboard.

  1. Open an existing whiteboard.
  2. At the top right, click the comment icon to open the comment panel.
  3. To the right of the comment you wish to resolve, click the Resolve icon . The resolved comment will disappear in the comment panel.
  4. (Optional) To show resolved comments, click the filter icon and then check the Show Resolved Comments.
  5. (Optional) To unresolve comments, click the Unresolve icon .

Creating a Mind Map in Zoom Whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to create a Mind Map in Zoom Whiteboard

  1. Create a new whiteboard in the Zoom web portal or Zoom desktop app. Note: To edit an existing whiteboard, open a whiteboard from the dashboard.
  2. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the More Tools icon .
  3. Select Mind Map.
  4. Choose between Horizontal or Vertical Mind Map. The Mind Map cursor will appear, enabling the user to select where to place the Mind Map. The placement becomes the Mind Map Origin.
  5. Double-click the Mind Map origin to add text. The format menu will appear.
  6. Use the format menu to add formatting to the elements.
  • Text Format: Enables users to choose bold, underline, italics, or strikethrough for the Mind Map text.
  • Swap Orientation: Rotates the Mind Map origin clockwise to the new orientation. For example, a horizontal Mind Map origin rotates clockwise to the vertical position and a vertical Mind Map origin rotates clockwise to the horizontal position.
  • Tidy: Restores the Mind Map to the default width. This option also restores associated elements of the Mind Map to the default width. When the user selects specific elements, the Tidy option works as follows:
  • Origin element: Tidies the entire Mind Map
  • Parent element: Tidies all proceeding branches
  • Child element: Tidies all proceeding branches
  • Subsidiary element: Tidies all proceeding branches
  • Color: Select the element to change, then select the Color option.
  • Origin: Applies the color to the origin element. If a color is not selected, the element defaults to bold and black. If the element is black, the default changes to white.
  • Parent: Applies the color to the element plus the entire route from the branch of origin and all the way through the branch.
  • Child: Applies the color to the element plus the branch of the parent and all the way through the branch.
  • Subsidiary: Applies the color to the element plus the branch of the child and all the way through the branch.
  • More: Select the More menu to apply additional options to the Mind Map.
  • Copy, Paste, or Duplicate: Enables users to paste or duplicate as a new origin element.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copies the hyperlink or URL of a selected Mind Map which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Object Order: Enables users to select the origin element to Bring to Front, Send to Back, Bring Forward, or Send Backward. This action applies to the entire Mind Map as one unified object.
  • Export as Data: Export data from selected Mind Map as a CSV file.
  • Save as Template: Enables users to save the Mind Map as a new origin template.
  • Delete: Enables users to delete the origin element. This action also deletes the entire Mind Map. If another element is deleted (for example, a parent element), then the proceeding elements are also deleted. If a child element is deleted, all of its subsidiary elements are deleted.

How to add elements to the Mind Map origin

Adding elements to the Mind Map origin enables users to expand and grow their Mind Map.

Add parent elements
  1. Click the Mind Map origin.
  2. Click the plus icon to add the parent element. The parent element will start the branch.
  3. (Optional) Use the format text menu to do the following:
  • Add text to the parent element. The width of the parent element automatically adjusts to accommodate the text.
  • Format the text for bold, italics, and underline.

Note: The parent element inherits the font size from the origin element. Multiple parent elements can be added to the origin.

Add child elements

Users can add child elements to the parent element. This creates branches and routes for the Mind Map.

  1. Select a parent element.
  2. Click the plus icon to create a child element.
  3. The child element will be added to the branch.
  4. (Optional) Use the format text menu to do the following:
  • Add text to the child element. The width of the child element automatically adjusts to accommodate the text.
  • Format the text for bold, italics, and underline.

Note: Users can add multiple child elements. The parent element does not resize based on the child elements.

Add subsidiary elements

Users can add elements below the child element level. These elements are subsidiary elements.

  1. Select a child element.
  2. Click the plus icon to create a subsidiary element.
  3. Subsidiary elements will be added to the child element.
  4. (Optional) Use the format text menu to do the following:
  • Add text to the subsidiary element. The width of the subsidiary element automatically adjusts to accommodate the text.
  • Format the text for bold, italics, and underline.

Embedding content using the iFrame widget

Category: Product features > User features

How to embed content using the iFrame widget

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.
  2. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the More Tools icon .
  3. Click Embed Content. The Embed iFrame Code Snippet widget will appear.
  4. Copy the embed code for the content you want to add. This is usually provided by the content source (for example, YouTube, Vimeo, data visualization tools) in the Share or Embed section.
  5. Go back to the Embed iFrame Code Snippet widget and paste the copied embed code.
  6. Click Embed.

How to manage the embedded content

Click on the embedded video to display the toolbar.

Display the content info

On the toolbar, click the info icon to display the content details such as the title and its source.

Expand the content

On the toolbar, click the expand icon to enlarge or maximize the content, providing a larger and more detailed view.

Open the content in a new tab

On the toolbar, click the linkout icon to open the content in a new tab.

Lock the content

On the toolbar, click the lock icon to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying or removing the whiteboard content.

More options

On the toolbar, click the ellipsis icon and select from the following options:

  • Copy: Copy the embedded content.
  • Copy as image: Copy the content as an image which can then be shared or pasted into applications that support images.
  • Paste: Place the copied content somewhere else on the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Make an exact copy of the embedded content.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copy the hyperlink or URL of an embedded content which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Bring Forward: Move the embedded content up one layer.
  • Bring to Front: Put the embedded content on the top layer.
  • Send Backward: Move the embedded content back one layer.
  • Send to back: Put the embedded content on the bottom layer.
  • Add Comment: Add comments directly to the content.
  • Save as Template: Save the selected content as a template. Users can use the saved template to create a new whiteboard.
  • Info: Show the creator and last editor of the embedded content.
  • Lock: Prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying or removing the embedded content.
  • Delete: Delete the embedded content.

Managing custom templates for Zoom Whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to create a custom template

  1. Create or open an existing whiteboard.
  2. At the top right, click the ellipsis icon .
  3. Select Save Page as Template.
  4. Enter a name, add description, and select categories for your template.
  5. Click Save Template.

How to access custom templates

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Web
  • Android | iOS
  • Zoom Web App

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop client.

  2. At the top, click the Whiteboards button . Note: If you don’t see the Whiteboards option, click More and then select Whiteboards from the list. The Zoom Whiteboard dashboard will display.

  3. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

  4. In the left menu, click My Templates.

  5. Select a template you want to open.

  6. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.

  7. On the left menu, click Whiteboards.

  8. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

  9. In the left menu, click My Templates.

  10. Select a template you want to open.

  11. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  12. At the bottom of the screen, tap More .

  13. In the Added Features section, tap Whiteboard .

  14. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

  15. In the left menu, scroll down to the bottom and click My Templates.

  16. Select a template you want to open.

  17. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.

  18. At the top, click the Whiteboards button . The Zoom Whiteboard dashboard will display.

  19. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

  20. In the left menu, click My Templates.

  21. Select a template you want to open.

How to share a custom template

  1. Open My Templates.
  2. Select a template you want to share.
  3. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Share with Contacts.
  5. Enter the contact name, or email address of the user you would like to share the whiteboard with and set their permissions with the drop-down arrow to the right of the entry box. Note: Custom templates can only be shared with users from the same organization.
  6. Click Share. Once shared, any updates to a shared template are immediately accessible by other users with access.

How to submit a custom template to organization

  1. Open My Templates.
  2. Select a template you want to share.
  3. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Submit to Organization to share templates that will benefit the entire organization.
  5. Click Submit. A copy of the template will be submitted to admin for approval. Once approved, this will become an org template. Any edits to the org template after it is submitted to an organization does not impact the submitted copy.

How to preview a custom template

  1. Open My Templates.
  2. Select a template you want to share.
  3. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Preview. The preview screen will display. From the preview screen, you can also use the template in whiteboard, share, submit to organization, edit, or delete the template.

How to edit a custom template

  1. Open My Templates.
  2. Select a template you want to share.
  3. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Edit.
  5. Change the name, description, or categories of the template.
  6. Click Save Template.

How to favorite a custom template

  1. Open My Templates.
  2. Select a template you want to share.
  3. On the top right of the selected template tile, click the star icon . All the templates you have marked as favorites will be visible in the Starred tab.

How to use a custom template in whiteboard

  1. Open My Templates.
  2. Select a template you want to share.
  3. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Use Template. The new whiteboard will open with the added template.

How to delete a custom template

  1. Open My Templates.
  2. Select a template you want to share.
  3. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  4. Click Move to Trash.
  5. Click Delete.

  • Enter the contact names, Zoom Chat channel, or email addresses of the users you would like to share the whiteboard with and set their permissions with the drop-down arrow to the right of the entry box.

How to share a whiteboard using a shareable link

You can also share your whiteboard using a shareable link. At the top right of the whiteboard, click the Share button to display the Share Whiteboard dialog box.

To set who can access the link, click the down arrow below Link Access and choose one of the following:

  • Only invited members can access this board (default): Only specific individuals or channels will have access.
  • Anyone at (Company Name): Enables permission for the entire account without having to name individual users (for example, make the board accessible to your entire company).
  • Anyone with the link can view this board: Makes the board available to all users with a Zoom account, including users outside your organization.

To set the permission level for those who can access the link, click the down arrow and choose one of the following:

  • Co-owner: Users with link access can have the same permissions as the original board owner, including sharing, editing, commenting, and deleting.
  • Viewer: Users with link access can view the board.
  • Editor: Users with link access can edit the board.
  • Commenter: Users with link access can comment on the board.
  • Transfer Ownership: Users who are board owners have the ability to transfer ownership of their boards to collaborators within the same board. Ownership cannot be transferred externally.
  • Remove: Remove a user’s access or permissions from the board.

At the bottom left, click the Copy Link and paste the URL in the chat message, Zoom Chat channel, or email.

Uploading documents and images to the whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to upload documents and images to the whiteboard

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop client.
  2. Create or open a whiteboard.
  3. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the Upload PDFs and Images icon . The file dialog will appear.
  4. Select a file or image from your computer. Learn how to upload files from your Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive.
  5. Click Open. The file or image will appear on the canvas.

Controls when you click on a file

  • Download File icon : Save the file to your device.
  • Extract Pages icon : Select specific pages from the file and extract them as a separate document.
  • Previous icon and Next icon : Navigate through the pages of the file.
  • Lock icon : Lock files to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the whiteboard content.
  • More icon : Represents additional options.
  • Copy: Copy the selected file.
  • Copy as image: Copy the selected file as image which can then be shared or pasted into applications that support images.
  • Paste: Place the copied file somewhere else on the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Make an exact copy of the selected file.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copy the hyperlink or URL of a selected file which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Bring Forward: Move the selected file up one layer.
  • Bring to Front: Put the selected file on the top layer.
  • Send Backward: Move the selected file back one layer.
  • Send to back: Put the selected file on the bottom layer.
  • Save as Template: Save the selected file as a template.
  • Info: Show the creator and last editor of the selected file.
  • Lock: Lock file to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the content.
  • Delete: Delete the selected file.

Controls when you click on an image

  • Download Image icon : Save image to your device.
  • Crop icon : Select a portion of the image and remove the rest.
  • Lock icon : Lock an image to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the whiteboard content.
  • More icon : Represents additional options.
  • Copy: Copy the selected image.
  • Copy as image: Copy the selected image which can be pasted into applications that support images.
  • Paste: Place the copied image somewhere else on the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Make an exact copy of the selected image.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copy the hyperlink or URL of a selected image which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Bring Forward: Move the selected image up one layer.
  • Bring to Front: Put the selected image on the top layer.
  • Send Backward: Move the selected image back one layer.
  • Send to back: Put the selected image on the bottom layer.
  • Save as Template: Save the selected image as a template.
  • Info: Show the creator and last editor of the selected image.
  • Lock: Lock image to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the content.
  • Delete: Delete the selected image.

Using Kanban board in Zoom Whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to insert a Kanban board on whiteboard

  1. Create or open a whiteboard.

  2. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the More Tools icon .

  3. Select KanBan.

  4. Click Kanban Board.

  5. Click anywhere on canvas to insert the Kanban Board.

A kanban board will be added with these default states:

  • To do
  • In progress
  • Done

How to use the Kanban board

Add card

One card is automatically inserted to each column. To add more cards, click + Add below the existing card inside the column.

Edit card

Click the card you want to edit, then click the icons in the context menu to edit the cards.

Delete card

Click the card you want to remove, then click the ellipses icon in the context menu. From the drop-down menu, click Delete.

Move card

Select a card and drag it sideways to move it to another column. Select a card and drag it vertically to reorder the cards within the column.

Add column

Click the ellipses icon beside the column name (To do, In progress, Done), and then select Add Column.

Rename column

Hover your mouse over the column name. Click the existing name to remove it and enter a new name.

Delete column

Click the ellipses icon beside the column name (To do, In progress, Done), and then select Delete.

Move column

Hover your mouse over the swimlane. Click and drag the swimlane sideways to move it to the right or left.

Change color

By defaults, colors are added to each column. Colors can be used to indicate priority or represent tasks. To change the color, click the ellipses icon beside the column name (To do, In progress, Done), then select Change Color. Select from the default 8 colors, or add a new color by entering its hex code or by using the color picker.

How to manage the Kanban board

  1. Insert a Kanban board on your whiteboard.
  2. Right-click anywhere on the Kanban board. Alternatively, you can also click the ellipsis icon on the mini toolbar below or at the top of the Kanban board.
  3. Select from the following options:
  • Copy: Copy the selected board.
  • Copy as image: Copy the selected board as an image which can then be shared or pasted into applications that support images.
  • Paste: Place the copied board somewhere else on the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Make an exact copy of the selected board.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copy the hyperlink or URL of a selected board which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Bring Forward: Move the selected board up one layer.
  • Bring to Front: Put the selected board on the top layer.
  • Send Backward: Move the selected board back one layer.
  • Send to back: Put the selected board on the bottom layer.
  • Export as Data: Export data from selected board as a CSV file.
  • Add Comment: Add comments directly to the board.
  • Save as Template: Save the selected board as a template. Users can use the saved template to create a new whiteboard.
  • Info: Show the creator and last editor of the selected board.
  • Lock: Lock board to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the content.
  • Delete: Delete the selected board.
  1. (Optional) To rename a Kanban board, click the board name Kanban to remove it, and then enter a new name.

Using keyboard and mouse shortcuts with Whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

Navigation

  • Use the Tab key to navigate on the following areas of the whiteboard:

  • Whiteboard key

  • Owner name/date

  • Current collaborators

  • Share button

  • More menu

  • Toolbar

  • Alert badge (Who can see what you share)

  • Zoom in/out menu

  • Page menu

  • Use the scroll wheel to scroll up and down.

  • Press Shift + scroll to scroll side to side.

  • Use the Left, Right, Up and Down arrow keys to navigate through the toolbar, previous or next menus, and submenus.

  • Use the ESC key to leave the zoom in/zoom out navigation and dismiss the alert badge.

Activate tools

  • Press V to activate the Select Tool.
  • Press P to activate the Draw Tool.
  • Press S to insert Shapes.
  • Press L to insert a Line.
  • Press T to enter a Text.
  • Press Shift + N to insert Sticky Notes.
  • Press E to activate Eraser.

Activate actions

  • Use the Enter or Spacebar key to:
  • Activate Share, Comment, More menu, toolbar, alert badge, and Zoom primary actions.
  • Zoom in or out
  • Press Ctrl/Cmd + D to duplicate objects.
  • Press Ctrl/Cmd + Shift+ 0 to zoom to fit.
  • Click the looking glass icons to Zoom In or Zoom Out. Click 100% to reset to the default zoom.
  • Press Ctrl/Cmd + (+) or (-) to zoom in or out.

To see the list of all available keyboard shortcuts, type the ? key. Click the Escape key to exit the shortcuts list.

Using the Draw tool

Category: Product features > User features

Pen and Highlighter

In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the pencil icon or press P on your keyboard to begin drawing. To activate the Pen or Highlighter tool, click the pencil icon and then select Pen or Highlighter.

To change the thickness, click the pencil icon in the left menu and select the brush size from the options bar: Thin, Regular, and Thick. When the Pen tool is active, the selected brush size will not be applied to the Highlighter tool. You need to adjust the thickness manually for each tool.

Clicking an object using the Select tool will open the context menu. You can change the line thickness and color, or click the ellipses icon to reveal More options.

  • Copy: Copies the selected object.
  • Copy as image: Copy the object as an image which can then be shared or pasted into applications that support images.
  • Paste: Place the copied object somewhere else on the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Make an exact copy of the selected object.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copy the hyperlink or URL of a selected object which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Bring Forward: Move the selected object up one layer.
  • Bring to Front: Put the selected object on the top layer.
  • Send Backward: Move the selected object back one layer.
  • Send to back: Put the selected object on the bottom layer.
  • Add Comment: Add comments directly to the object.
  • Save as Template: Save the selected object as a template. Users can use the saved template to create a new whiteboard.
  • Info: Show the creator and last editor of the selected object.
  • Lock: Lock objects and groups of objects to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the whiteboard content.
  • Delete: Delete the selected object.

Using the Select tool

Category: Product features > User features

Select mode

In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the Select tool icon or press V on your keyboard to activate it. When Select mode is selected, you can click on objects to move and edit them. Clicking an object and opening its context menu gives you More options by clicking the ellipses icon .

  • Copy: Copies the selected object.
  • Paste: Place the copied object somewhere else on the whiteboard.
  • Duplicate: Makes an exact copy of the selected object.
  • Copy Link to Object: Copies the hyperlink or URL of a selected object which can then be shared or pasted elsewhere.
  • Bring Forward: Moves the selected object up one layer.
  • Bring to Front: Put the selected object on the top layer.
  • Send Backward: Moves the selected object back one layer.
  • Send to back: Put the selected object on the bottom layer.
  • Export as Data: Export data from selected object as a CSV file.
  • Save as Template: Saves the selected object as a template. Users can use the saved template to create a new whiteboard.
  • Info: Shows the creator and last editor of the selected object.
  • Lock: Locks objects and groups of objects to prevent other users with edit access from accidentally modifying the whiteboard content.
  • Delete: Deletes the selected object.
Move objects
  • To move a single object, click an object and drag it anywhere on canvas.
  • To move multiple objects, press Shift and then click on objects you want to move. This will put every selected object in a single selection box. Drag the selection box to move multiple objects at once.
Rotate objects
  • To rotate a single object, click on an object and then hover your cursor over the double arrow icon in the lower left corner of the object. Click and drag the icon to rotate it.
  • To rotate multiple objects, press Shift and then click on objects you want to move. This will put every selected object in a single selection box. Click and drag the double-arrow icon in the lower left corner of the selection box to rotate it.
Resize objects
  • To resize a single object, then hover your cursor over one of the small squares that form right angles around the object. Click and drag the corner of the object to resize it.
  • To resize multiple objects, press Shift and then click on objects you want to resize. This will put every selected object in a single selection box. Click and drag the small squares that form right angles around the selection box to resize it.

Grab mode

In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the Select tool icon or press V on your keyboard to activate it. Click the hand icon to activate the Grab mode. When Grab mode is selected, you cannot select or move objects but you can pan around to navigate within the canvas.

Using the Zoom Whiteboard

Category: Product features > User features

How to use the Zoom Whiteboard tools

The whiteboard editing tools available for use are located on the left side of the screen. To activate a tool, click its icon. Once selected, the mouse cursor will change to indicate the current tool mode. For most controls, clicking on the canvas will then create an object of that type. If using the select tool, you will be able to select one or more objects and change their properties.

Editing tools
  • Select tool: Places cursor in select mode so you can click objects and change their properties. Selecting an element will bring up the settings menu allowing you to copy, paste, and duplicate the selected element. You can also use this menu to adjust the element layers.
  • Grab: Places cursor in hand mode to move the canvas freely without unintentionally selecting and moving objects.
  • Pen tool: Places cursor into drawing mode to perform freehand sketching.
  • Brush types: Choose between a Pen or a Highlighter
  • Eraser types: Choose between Eraser (removes entire objects) or Pixel Eraser (erases specific areas)
  • Lasso tool: Use a free-form lasso to circle and highlight objects
  • Context menu:
  • Change line thickness
  • Change color
  • Smart Drawing: Convert drawings into basic shapes
  • Shape tool: Places cursor into shape mode to create basic shapes, callout shapes, flowchart symbols, UML symbols, and equations. Users can click + drag and click + tap anywhere on the whiteboard to draw shapes.
  • Context menu:
  • Change fill (full, opaque, hollow)
  • Change shape
  • Change color
  • Line tool: Creates line objects. Users can drag lines from the toolbar, attach them to shapes, and use them as connectors.
  • Line types: straight, one-end arrow, double-end arrow, elbowed arrow
  • Context menu:
  • Change line thickness
  • Change color
  • Text: Creates text. Double-clicking a text object puts the object into text editing mode. When users type a text in a text box, the text box width automatically adjusts to fit the text completely.
  • Context menu:
  • Change font style (bold, italic, underline)
  • Font size
  • Font alignment
  • Font color Note: The maximum number of characters per text edit is 5000.
  • List (bulleted, numbered)
  • Link
  • Lock
  • Comment
  • Other options include Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Export, Delete, Order, Move to, Frame selection, Save to shapes, Launch individual, Create task, Activity history
  • Sticky Note: Creates a note idea that can be used to draw attention. When users select a sticky note, they can conveniently create a poll and send it to others to gather quick feedback.
  • Context menu:
  • Change background color
  • Add emoji and tags
  • Show or hide the author
  • Add vote (up vote, down vote)
  • Insert text
  • Add a link
  • Lock the sticky note
  • Add a comment
  • Comment: Allows users to add comments to specific elements or areas on the whiteboard canvas.
  • Frame: Allows users to organize and sequence content within a canvas. Users can easily switch between aspect ratios, such as 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, Letter, and A4. For unique specifications, users have the freedom to define a custom aspect ratio, enabling complete control over the canvas dimensions.
  • Templates: Gives a pre-formatted structure and layout that can be used as a base to create many whiteboards.
  • Upload PDFs and Images: Allows users to upload files such as word document, PDF, PowerPoint slide and images from their computer onto the board. When files and images are uploaded to the canvas, users can move the files around, adjust the size, crop the unwanted parts, connect to other shapes, and add comments on or around them. Additionally, users can extract individual PDF pages to add annotations and download the files that have been uploaded to the Whiteboard.
  • Stickers and emojis: Allows users to add stickers and emojis anywhere on the whiteboard canvas.
  • Code block: Allows users to add formatted text and code directly to the whiteboard canvas.
  • Quick actions: Allows users to have access to commonly used tools.
  • More Tools: Allows users to add advanced tools such as:
  • Table
  • Mind Map
  • Kanban
  • Card
  • Chart
  • Embed Content
  • Diagram
  • Whiteboard Content Generation with AI Companion: This feature leverages AI technology, which may include third-party models, to help users add and refine whiteboard contents with just one click.

How to use Zoom Whiteboard controls

Controls on the top-left section
  • Star icon : Allows users to star or favorite a whiteboard for quick reference. Starred whiteboards are displayed in the Starred tab on the Zoom Whiteboard dashboard.
  • More actions icon : Contains additional options and features that are not displayed on the main whiteboard menu.
  • Board
  • Duplicate Board: Create an exact copy of a whiteboard.
  • Save Page as Template: Save a copy of a whiteboard page as a reusable template.
  • Star this whiteboard: Allows users to star or favorite the opened whiteboard.
  • Lock Board: Temporarily prevents editors, commenters, and viewers from opening and editing the whiteboard content, while owners and co-owners retain full editing functionality.
  • Board History: Allows users to view activity and restore previous versions of a whiteboard.
  • Activity: Allows users to review changes, select a change to show where the change was made on the board, and see changes grouped by dates.
  • Version: Allows users to preview and restore old whiteboard versions.
  • Move to Trash: Delete a whiteboard.
  • Preferences
  • Grid: Helps users align and organize content on the canvas. There are 3 background options for whiteboard:
  • None: Displays a blank canvas without any visible grid lines. This can be useful for creating free-form drawings or designs.
  • Line Grid: Displays a grid of evenly spaced horizontal and vertical lines on the canvas. These lines can be helpful for aligning text, images, and other elements on the canvas.
  • Dot Grid: Displays a grid of evenly spaced dots on the canvas. This can be useful for creating precise drawings or diagrams that require precise measurements and alignment.
  • Snap to Grid: Aligns objects perfectly, eliminating the need to manually create a grid with boxes. The snap to grid feature is applicable to all canvas objects, including shapes, text boxes, sticky notes, lines, images, and more.
  • Alignment Guides: Allows users to align objects or elements relative to each other or to specific reference points on a canvas.
  • Gap Guides: Helps users in maintaining consistent spacing between objects.
  • Object Size Guides: Helps users maintain consistent object sizes or proportions.
  • View: Enables users to see certain elements while working on a whiteboard, such as comments, collaborator cursors, alignment guides, gap guides, and object size guides.
  • Comments: Allows users to view the comments.
  • Collaborators Cursors: Allows users to see other people working on the same whiteboard when their cursors appear as they move their mouse, even without clicking on the canvas. Up to 10 active cursors can be displayed at a time.
  • Votes: Allows users to easily create a poll and send it to others for quick feedback when they select a sticky note. The poll results are then displayed in real-time, making it easy to see what others are thinking.
  • Find: Performs a search and find text within a whiteboard, including text located within sticky notes, text fields, and shapes.
  • Export: Allows users to export whiteboard content as a PDF, PNG, or CSV file.
  • Help: Provides users with Help Center resources and information on whiteboard keyboard shortcuts to help them use the platform more effectively. This also allows users to report any inappropriate content or behavior that they encounter while using the platform.
  • Leave Feedback: Directs users to a survey where they can provide detailed feedback about their experience with the whiteboard.
  • About: Provides information about the version of the whiteboard application currently being used.
  • Timer icon : Allows users to set a countdown timer for a specified amount of time. Timers set outside meetings are not visible during meetings and timers set during meetings only affect users in the same meeting.
  • Laser icon : Enables easy highlighting and annotation without editing the document. This feature is designed to address the difficulty in following along while presenting content, especially when the canvas supports multiple content types and multiple users are editing the document at the same time.
Controls on the top-right section
  • Invite All to Follow Me icon: As a presenter, you can invite or require all participants to follow you in the Whiteboard presentation. This icon is only available for in-meeting whiteboards.
  • Binoculars icon: As a viewer, you can click the collaborators small profile pictures next to the Invite All to Follow Me drop-down and then the Binoculars icon next to a participant to follow that participant. This icon is only available for in-meeting whiteboards.
  • Share button: Allows users to share their whiteboard with others in real-time.
  • Comment icon : Opens the Comment panel to view the
Controls on the bottom-right section
  • Undo icon : Undo the last action.
  • Redo icon : Redo the last action.
  • Zoom out icon : Zoom out from a specific area of the whiteboard.
  • Zoom in icon : Zoom in on a specific area of the whiteboard.
  • Zoom percentage icon : Sets the level of magnification or reduction of the whiteboard content on the screen. Users can adjust the size of whiteboard content in increments of 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, 200%, and can also opt for a Fit to screen option, providing precise control over the displayed dimensions.
  • Mini Map icon : Allow users to see where the content is located on their canvas and easily navigate to a specific area of the board.
  • Page icon : Allow users to organize the content better, create additional space for collaboration, and provide a clear separation between different sections of whiteboard.
Controls when you right-click on the canvas
  • Paste: Allows users to insert or add copied or cut content from the clipboard onto the whiteboard canvas.
  • Add sticky note: Creates virtual sticky notes on the whiteboard canvas.
  • Add text: Adds text directly onto the whiteboard canvas.
  • Add shape: Adds predefined shapes to the whiteboard canvas.
  • Add card: Creates and organizes content on individual cards that can be moved around the whiteboard canvas.
  • Add comment: Allows users to add feedback or annotations to specific areas of the whiteboard canvas.
  • Snap rotation: Can be turned on to allow users to quickly and easily align objects on the canvas to specific angles or orientations.
  • Show grid: Can be turned on to allow users to show grid on the canvas.
  • Snap to grid: Can be turned on to allow users to easily align objects on the canvas to a predefined grid pattern.
  • Save page as template: Allows users to save a copy of a whiteboard page as a reusable template.

Using Zoom Whiteboard in a Zoom meeting

Category: Product features > User features

How to create a whiteboard during a Zoom meeting

  1. Start a meeting from the Zoom desktop client.
  2. On the in-meeting controls, click the Whiteboards button .
  3. Click New Whiteboard. The whiteboard will open in the meeting window.

Note: Meeting hosts have control over who and when attendees can create new whiteboards while in a meeting. Any whiteboards created during the meeting are owned by the host.

How to edit a whiteboard during a Zoom meeting

  1. Start a meeting from the Zoom desktop client.
  2. On the in-meeting controls, click the Whiteboards button .
  3. Click Existing Whiteboards.
  4. In the pop-up window, you will be asked to select from the following:
  • How do you want to open the board?
  • Collaborating: Users are granted edit access.
  • Presenting: Board opens in presentation mode and users are granted view access.
  • Allow persistent access to verified meeting participants after closing the whiteboard.
  1. Click Open Board. The whiteboard will open in the meeting window.
  2. Use the editing tools to create and manipulate objects on the whiteboard.
  3. (Optional) When you are done, click Close Whiteboard at the top of the screen.

How to share a whiteboard during a Zoom meeting

  1. Start a meeting ora webinarfrom the Zoom desktop client.
  2. In the meeting controls toolbar, click the Whiteboards button .
  3. At the top right, click New Whiteboard or Existing Whiteboards. The new whiteboard will open in the meeting window.
  4. If you selected Existing Whiteboards, you will be asked to select from the following:
  • How do you want to open the board?
  • Collaborating: Users are granted edit access.
  • Presenting: Board opens in presentation mode and users are granted view access.
  • Allow persistent access to verified meeting participants after closing the whiteboard.
  1. At the top right, click Share to send the whiteboard to other users outside the meeting.
  • Enter the contact names, Zoom Chat channel, or email addresses of the users you would like to share the whiteboard with and set their permissions with the drop-down arrow to the right of the entry box.
  • Add an optional message to help recipients understand why this project was shared with them in the email that will be sent to them.
  1. Click Share Whiteboard.

Using Zoom Whiteboard templates

Category: Product features > User features

How to access Zoom Whiteboard templates

  • Windows | macOS | Linux
  • Web
  • Android | iOS
  • Zoom Web App

  1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.

  2. At the top, click the Whiteboards button . Note: If you don’t see the Whiteboards option, click More and then select Whiteboards from the list. The Zoom Whiteboard dashboard will display.

  3. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

  4. Sign in to the Zoom web portal.

  5. On the left menu, click Whiteboards.

  6. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

  7. Sign in to the Zoom mobile app.

  8. At the bottom of the screen, tap More .

  9. In the Added Features section, tap Whiteboard .

  10. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

  11. Sign in to the Zoom Web App.

  12. On the left menu, click Whiteboards.

  13. Click All templates. The templates dashboard will display.

How to create a new whiteboard from a template

  1. Open the templates dashboard.
  2. In the left menu, select a category and search for a specific template you want to use.
  3. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  4. (Optional) Click Preview to preview the template picture with sample data.
  5. Click Use Template. The new whiteboard will open with the added template.

How to insert a template from an existing whiteboard

  1. Open an existing whiteboard.
  2. In the toolbar on the left side of the screen, click the Templates icon . The templates dashboard will display.
  3. In the left menu, select a category and search for a specific template you want to use.
  4. In the lower right corner of the selected template tile, click the ellipsis icon .
  5. (Optional) Click Preview to preview the template picture with sample data.
  6. Click Use Template. The selected template will be inserted onto the opened whiteboard.

August 25, 2024
Changes to existing features
  • Enhancements to link sharing permissions Zoom Whiteboard can be shared with users outside of an account or with those who do not have a Zoom Account. In addition to being able to view the whiteboard, external viewers can also comment on and/or edit it.
New and enhanced features
  • User features
  • Quickly access last used whiteboard in meetings Users can access their last used whiteboard directly from the Screen Share menu in Zoom meetings. The dashboard will default to the last opened whiteboards in that meeting. The whiteboard automatically opens in collaborate mode, without needing to go through the permissions window.
  • Ability to upload SVG and PNG files to shapes library Users can upload SVG and PNG files to the shape library, increasing the variety of shapes available.
  • Support for canvas background color Users can change the background color of their canvas from the Whiteboard settings. Changing the background color will update it for everyone collaborating on the whiteboard. This allows users to create a visually appealing workspace that suits their preferences.
  • Enhancements to Miro content importer The Miro content importer has been updated with new features, including transparency for shape fills, fixes for text grouping errors, and better background color options for frames and shapes. Pages now align more closely with original PDF exports, and text and font scaling within shapes and text boxes has been improved. Arrowheads in flowcharts point correctly, Miro tables convert smoothly to Zoom Whiteboard tables, and symbols and letters (e.g., “>” vs. “V”) are oriented properly. In addition, the order of overlapping shapes and lines has been improved and connector labels are now supported.
Resolved issues
  • Minor bug fixes
August 4, 2024
New and enhanced features
  • Admin features
  • Ability to restrict external link sharing for Zoom Whiteboard Admins can disable external link sharing within their organization. If the Allow external link sharing checkbox is unchecked in the admin portal under the Sharing section, the option Anyone can access is disabled in the share sheet. A tooltip displays “Your admin has disabled this function” when users attempt to share a link externally. This feature gives admins more control over external collaboration while still allowing external users to be invited.
  • Email and team chat notifications management for Whiteboard Account owners and admins can manage email and team chat notifications for Zoom Whiteboard. They can disable email and team chat notifications for the entire organization or specific groups. Users can also turn email and team chat notifications on or off at an individual level. However, notifications for permission requests remain enabled by default. This feature allows organizations to reduce notification noise and control the volume of emails received related to Whiteboard activities.
  • Enhancements to default access level settings Admins can set the default access level for Anyone as Editor or Commenter in the Whiteboard Sharing Defaults section of the admin settings. Previously, the default access level for Anyone was limited to Viewer. This enhancement enables more flexible collaboration scenarios, as the default access level is applied to users’ shared whiteboards.
  • User features
  • Notify users when account sharing settings prevent meeting users from collaborating on a whiteboard after a meeting Notifications will be displayed to inform users if meeting participants cannot collaborate on a whiteboard opened in a meeting because they have out of meeting sharing disabled.
  • Notification for exceeding maximum size of individual whiteboard Users are notified when a whiteboard has exceeded its maximum size. Board owners and co-owners with non-Plus licenses can clear the version history to free up space. Billing admins with non-Plus licenses also have the option to upgrade their license. This feature helps ensure users can continue collaborating on whiteboards without exceeding storage limits.
  • Annotation with stamps, stickers, emojis, and GIFs Users can add stamps, stickers, emojis, and GIFs to the Zoom Whiteboard canvas. A new submenu houses these annotation tools, allowing users to add them consecutively on the canvas. Stamps will be added as an annotation tool, while stickers, emojis, and GIFs can be added one by one. This feature provides a more engaging and expressive way for users to give feedback and collaborate on visual documents.
  • Cast Zoom Whiteboard in a room Users can open a previously created Zoom Whiteboard in a nearby room with a simple workflow. The Open this WB in a room option appears if the admin has enabled the Show Pair and Save setting. This new flow simplifies the process of sharing and collaborating on whiteboards across devices.
  • Restrict viewer actions on shared whiteboards Owners and co-owners can restrict viewers from exporting, duplicating, downloading content, or making templates from their whiteboards. By default, all actions are enabled for viewers. Owners can choose whether the restrictions apply to all viewers or only external viewers. This feature gives document owners greater control over how their whiteboards are accessed and used by viewers.
  • Connectors added to shapes library Users can now conveniently access connectors directly from the shapes panel. New connector options include Straight Line, Straight Arrow, Elbowed Arrow, and Curved Arrow. Connectors are grouped under a dedicated folder within the shapes panel, enabling users to swiftly add them alongside shapes.
  • Sticky notes duplication Users can easily duplicate sticky notes side by side on the whiteboard using the CMD+D shortcut. The duplicated sticky notes are placed at the next available position without overlapping, allowing users to rapidly jot down ideas or content. When duplicating frames, both the frame and its content are copied, keeping the content within the new frame.

June 23, 2024
New and enhanced features
  • Admin features
  • Content Importer settings Account owners and admins can enable or disable extracting uploaded content into editable Zoom Whiteboard objects. This setting is configurable at the account, group, and user level. Account owners and admins can manage the specific types of content that can be extracted, such as PDF’s exported from Miro. If disabled, the dashboard importer is visible but grayed out. This feature provides more control over the content importing process for organizations.
  • User features
  • Ability to easily reopen whiteboard during a meeting Users can easily re-open the whiteboards they previously had open during a meeting using a back to dashboard button, instead of having to start a new whiteboard each time. This feature provides a quick way for users to find and access their last-opened or modified whiteboards within the same meeting, enabling smooth collaboration and continuity in their workflows.
  • Enhancements to tag objects on canvas Users can create and assign tags to objects like sticky notes and cards on the canvas. Tags are accessible to all editors and above at the board level. Users can quickly apply a new or existing tag to a card or note from the halo menu. Users can also create and manage tags from the board options menu. This feature allows users to easily label and organize content on the canvas.
  • My saved shapes collections Users with a Whiteboard Plus license can save custom shapes and objects they create to a personal content library in Zoom Whiteboard. This library is searchable and allows users to categorize and organize their saved content. Objects saved to the library can be retrieved and placed on canvases with a single click. Users also gain access to save objects to the library through the object overflow menu or by drag and drop. The ability to build and maintain personal shape libraries enhances diagramming workflows and encourages content reuse.
  • Enhancements to flowcharting and diagramming Users can quickly access and add shapes, lines, and connectors to build flowcharts in Zoom Whiteboard. The entry point to flowchart shapes is more obvious, with a description under the All Shapes button indicating where to find them. Users can also drag and drop shapes from the panel onto the canvas. Additionally, a Decision diamond shape has been added to the flowchart section, making it easier to create decision points in flowcharts. The time to show the dotted outline for quick shape creation has been reduced, improving the overall experience when creating flowcharts and diagrams.
  • Swimlane component for flowchart diagrams Users can add a swimlane component to the canvas for creating flowchart diagrams. They can change the orientation of the swimlane, add rows or columns, and change the color of cells. When the orientation is row-labeled, the text appears vertically as per standard swimlane design. Moving the swimlane around the canvas moves all the objects inside it. This feature allows users to visualize processes with multiple levels in an intuitive way, improving their diagramming experience.
  • Enhanced Whiteboard follower experience Users can enjoy a gentle, smooth follower experience when viewing another participant’s cursor movements on the Zoom Whiteboard canvas. The user’s cursor is centered on the screen, and there is a smooth panning transition when following cursor movements so users can easily understand how others are navigating the whiteboard.
  • Mouse wheel support for canvas navigation Users can use a mouse wheel to scroll and zoom in and out of the Zoom Whiteboard canvas. The application automatically detects whether a user is scrolling on a mouse or trackpad and adjusts the behavior accordingly. Users can choose their preferred method of navigation, such as using the mouse wheel to zoom or panning with a right-click and drag. This provides a flexible way to navigate and interact with the canvas, especially for first-time users who may be unfamiliar with keyboard shortcuts.
  • Increased whiteboard storage capacity for Whiteboard Plus users Whiteboard Plus users can now add more content to their whiteboards with an increased maximum board size of 1GB. This increased storage capacity allows for more flexibility and collaboration when working on whiteboards.
  • Option to hide legal disclaimer on Zoom Whiteboard canvas Users can choose to hide the legal disclaimer at the bottom of the Zoom Whiteboard canvas by checking the do not show again option. This feature allows users to declutter their canvas view and maximize the available workspace. Once the disclaimer is hidden, it will no longer appear, providing a distraction-free environment for collaboration and ideation.

New and enhanced features
  • Admin features
  • Sharing account setting toggle alert Account owners and admins can set whether external users can access and edit whiteboards within their organization. When disabling external sharing, a warning is provided to admins about the impact of the change, and all external collaborators are removed from whiteboards. This ensures consistent behavior for external collaboration both inside and outside of meetings.

This enhancement improves user experience and productivity by making it easier and faster to locate specific whiteboards based on their content, including shapes, sticky notes, and text boxes, even if the board name or creation date is forgotten.
  • Enhancements to whiteboard access management Users can easily see their roles in documents and ask for higher access levels, with requests sent straight to the document owner.   • Easy access to whiteboards after meetings Links to whiteboards will be added in the in-meeting chat and continuous meeting chat (CMC) after a whiteboard is closed in the meeting.   • Providing an option to clear either the entire board or individual pages from an easily accessible location outside the page navigation.
  • Simplified whiteboard opening experience on mobile and tablet devices Account owners and admins can simplify the process of opening a new whiteboard for users on touch devices like mobile phones and tablets during meetings. The new design streamlines the steps required to start a new whiteboard session, providing a smoother and more intuitive experience for touch device users. This enhancement aims to improve the overall user experience and increase productivity for mobile and tablet users who frequently utilize the whiteboard feature.
  • Embed Zoom Whiteboard into Coda pages Users can now embed Zoom Whiteboards into Coda pages. The embedded whiteboard provides a view-only experience, allowing users to view and pan the whiteboard directly in a Coda. Document owners can control whether their whiteboard can be embedded in third-party applications.
